analysis.one_line_summary: An LLM-extracted, vector-indexed fact store with scopes (user, agent, run, app). In this version (V3) writes only add: Memory.add appends new facts and dedups them by MD5 hash. Mutable records are overwritten in place with an append-only SQLite audit log. Retrieval is hybrid (semantic + BM25 + entity boost). It has no supersession links, dependencies, invalidation, concurrency control or action gating.
analysis.architecture:
Language: Python (mem0/), with a TypeScript port (mem0-ts/). Library core: mem0/memory/main.py, classes Memory and AsyncMemory (about 3.9k lines, sync and async code duplicated).
Storage, three parts:
(1) A pluggable vector store (mem0/vector_stores/*, about 25 backends; the Qdrant default lives in qdrant.py). It holds one point per memory: the embedding plus a payload {data, hash (md5), text_lemmatized, created_at, updated_at, user_id/agent_id/run_id, actor_id, role, attributed_to, expiration_date, custom metadata}. Qdrant also stores a BM25 sparse vector.
(2) A second vector collection, '<collection>_entities' (_entity_collection_name, main.py:422). Each entity point has payload {data, entity_type, linked_memory_ids[], scope ids}. This is the only 'link' structure.
(3) SQLite through SQLiteManager (mem0/memory/storage.py). It has two tables. history(id, memory_id, old_memory, new_memory, event ADD/UPDATE/DELETE, created_at, updated_at, is_deleted, actor_id, role) is an append-only audit log. messages(session_scope, role, content) holds recent conversation turns. One process-local threading.Lock guards the SQLite connection.
The graph store (Neo4j etc.) is no longer in the OSS source; it shows up only in AGENTS.md and exceptions.py.
Process model: in-process library, or a FastAPI REST server (server/main.py) with these routes: POST /memories, GET /memories, GET /memories/{id}, POST /search, PUT /memories/{id}, GET /memories/{id}/history, DELETE /memories/{id}, DELETE /memories, POST /reset, /configure, plus API-key/JWT auth (server/auth.py) and request logging.
API surface: add(messages, user_id|agent_id|run_id, metadata, expiration_date, infer), search(query, filters, top_k, threshold, rerank), get, get_all, update(memory_id, text, metadata, expiration_date), delete, delete_all, history, reset.
MCP:
- Hosted Platform MCP at mcp.mem0.ai is described only in docs/platform/mem0-mcp.mdx (README-only; server code not in repo).
- A local stdio MCP server, integrations/agent-plugin-core/python/mcp_server.py (copied into claude-code-plugin/core), exposes exactly one tool, search_memories(query, top_k, category, scope repo|dir|mine, run_id). It calls the hosted Platform API.
- The Claude Code plugin (integrations/claude-code-plugin/hooks/hooks.json) wires these hooks: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit (context injection), PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure (evidence capture), SubagentStart and SubagentStop, Stop, PreCompact and SessionEnd (flush to Mem0).

mechanisms.name: Additive-only extraction (V3 pipeline)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Memory._add_to_vector_store (main.py:881-1220) runs these phases: (0) load the last 10 messages for the session scope; (1) vector-search the top 10 existing memories in the same user/agent/run scope; (2) map their UUIDs to integer ids '0'..'9' (the code calls this 'anti-hallucination'); (3) make one LLM call with ADDITIVE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT (mem0/configs/prompts.py:468), which outputs only ADD operations plus optional linked_memory_ids; (4) batch-embed; (5) skip any fact whose md5(text) matches an existing or in-batch hash; (6) batch-insert new points with fresh uuid4 ids; then write history rows (event=ADD); (7) link entities; (8) save messages. The old LLM UPDATE/DELETE decision step (the classic mem0 'memory update' prompt) is gone. Contradictions are never resolved at write time, and old and new facts coexist.
mechanisms.evidence: mem0/memory/main.py _add_to_vector_store lines 881-1220; mem0/configs/prompts.py ADDITIVE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT line 468 and generate_additive_extraction_prompt around lines 1020-1062
mechanisms.limitations: The prompt asks the LLM for linked_memory_ids ('updated/shifted preference, follow-up event'), but the OSS code throws that field away: grep shows no read of mem.get('linked_memory_ids'). So there is no supersedes or relates-to edge between memories, and stale and fresh facts are both returned by search. Dedup works only on exact text hashes.
mechanisms.why: It shows that a popular system moved to append-only writes and away from LLM-decided in-place UPDATE/DELETE. That supports ContextDB's immutable revisions. ContextDB must add the part mem0 dropped: an explicit supersession edge and head pointer, so readers can tell which revision is current.

mechanisms.name: In-place update with append-only history log
mechanisms.how_it_works: Memory.update and _update_memory (main.py:1829, 2052-2112) do vector_store.get(id), copy the payload, overwrite data/hash/text_lemmatized/updated_at (created_at is kept), re-embed, call vector_store.update (an overwrite), then SQLiteManager.add_history(memory_id, old_memory, new_memory, 'UPDATE', actor_id, role). _delete_memory (main.py:2114) hard-deletes the vector point and writes a DELETE history row with is_deleted=1. Identity keys (user_id/agent_id/run_id/actor_id) cannot change after creation (_strip_identity_keys, main.py:143). history(memory_id) returns rows ordered by created_at.
mechanisms.evidence: mem0/memory/main.py update(), _update_memory(), _delete_memory(), history(); mem0/memory/storage.py SQLiteManager.add_history / batch_add_history / get_history
mechanisms.limitations: The live record is mutable. History is a side log that stores only text diffs (no embedding, no metadata snapshot) and cannot be used to roll back or read at a past point in time. History and vector writes are not atomic: there is no transaction across the two stores. It has no revision numbers.
mechanisms.why: Mutable head plus an audit log is exactly what ContextDB replaces with immutable revisions plus a CAS head. It is useful only as a migration shape: a ContextDB revision chain can reproduce mem0's history() API.

mechanisms.name: expiration_date TTL filter
mechanisms.how_it_works: add/update accept expiration_date (YYYY-MM-DD). _normalize_expiration_date stores it in the payload. _payload_is_expired (main.py:442) compares it with today's UTC date. Search, get and get_all skip expired items unless show_expired=True. Nothing is deleted.
mechanisms.evidence: mem0/memory/main.py _normalize_expiration_date (427), _payload_is_expired (442), _search_vector_store expiry check, _get_all_from_vector_store
mechanisms.limitations: Expiry is wall-clock only, at day granularity. It is not tied to any dependency or event. The docs mention decay notices (detect_decay_usage_from_delete) as Platform upsell, and decay is not implemented in OSS.
mechanisms.why: It is the only staleness mechanism here. ContextDB could offer time-based validity as one more dependency type (a time-bounded Cur dep), with the same hide-but-keep (show_expired) semantics.

mechanisms.name: Entity side-index (linked_memory_ids)
mechanisms.how_it_works: After insert, extract_entities_batch (mem0/utils/entity_extraction.py, spaCy-based) pulls entities from each fact. Each entity is matched to an existing entity point, either by exact normalized text (_existing_entities_by_text) or by vector match with score >= 0.95 in the same scope. The new memory ids are then unioned into that entity's payload.linked_memory_ids, or a new entity point is inserted. On update or delete, _remove_memory_from_entity_store strips the memory id, and _link_entities_for_memory re-links using the new text. At search time, _compute_entity_boosts finds entities matching entities in the query and boosts their linked memories (ENTITY_BOOST_WEIGHT=0.5 in mem0/utils/scoring.py).
mechanisms.evidence: mem0/memory/main.py _upsert_entity (605), _remove_memory_from_entity_store (652), _link_entities_for_memory (707), Phase 7 in _add_to_vector_store (around 1120-1200), _compute_entity_boosts (1747); mem0/utils/scoring.py score_and_rank
mechanisms.limitations: Used only to rank search results. These are not dependency edges, and nothing propagates through them. Entity payload updates are read-modify-write with no CAS, so concurrent adds can lose links. All failures are swallowed with logger.debug/warning.
mechanisms.why: Entities make cheap 'Sem' dependency candidates: ContextDB could suggest Sem deps from shared entities, but never treat them as justification edges.

mechanisms.name: Coding-session provenance stamping (plugin)
mechanisms.how_it_works: RepoContext (integrations/agent-plugin-core/python/memory_core.py:324) captures the repo identity (normalized git remote), branch and head_sha (git rev-parse HEAD), and pins them per session in the session_scopes table (repo_for_session, around line 757). At flush, memories are sent with metadata {source, branch, git_sha}, and the episode text contains 'Provenance: repo=..; branch=..; head=..; packet=..' (build_episode around line 1650; flush_session around lines 1990-1995).
mechanisms.evidence: integrations/agent-plugin-core/python/memory_core.py RepoContext, _resolve_repo_cached, EvidenceStore.repo_for_session, build_episode, flush_session
mechanisms.limitations: git_sha is stored as metadata only. Nothing compares it with the current HEAD at read time, so a memory about code changed after that commit is never flagged as stale.
mechanisms.why: This is exactly the Pin dependency on a code revision that ContextDB formalizes. mem0 collects the data but never validates it, so ContextDB can add 'git_sha/file-hash Pin dep -> PENDING when HEAD diverges' on top of the same capture hooks.

mechanisms.name: Scope lanes: user_id / agent_id / run_id / app_id with filter algebra
mechanisms.how_it_works: Every memory carries user_id, agent_id and/or run_id (_build_filters_and_metadata, main.py:314). Search filters support AND/OR/NOT and operators (_process_metadata_filters, _has_advanced_operators). The coding plugin builds lanes in _search_filters (memory_core.py:251). The 'shared' lane is agent_id=project_id AND app_id=repo. The personal lane is user_id AND app_id. A 'dir' scope narrows with metadata.dirs contains <dir>, using directory_chain to tag every ancestor directory. Wildcard identities are rejected (_scope_value) so a filter cannot be widened by accident.
mechanisms.evidence: mem0/memory/main.py _build_filters_and_metadata, _build_session_scope, _process_metadata_filters; integrations/agent-plugin-core/python/memory_core.py _search_filters, directory_chain, _shared_project_ids, _scope_value
mechanisms.limitations: Sharing is plain namespace filtering. It gives no visibility or consistency guarantees, no per-agent read snapshot, and no notification when another agent writes.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB needs repo/dir/user/session lanes anyway, and this lane design (shared repo lane, personal lane, ancestor-dir tags, wildcard rejection) has proven itself across many coding-agent harnesses.

mechanisms.name: Concurrency control (none at the memory level)
mechanisms.how_it_works: No version field, ETag, compare-and-set or lock on memory records. vector_store.update is a blind overwrite (e.g. mem0/vector_stores/qdrant.py update at line 500). The only locks are SQLiteManager._lock (a process-local threading.Lock around the SQLite connection) and BEGIN/COMMIT around single history inserts. The Qdrant client is shared to avoid RocksDB lock contention (main.py:569), which is a resource lock, not a semantic one.
mechanisms.evidence: mem0/memory/main.py _update_memory (read-modify-write with no version check); mem0/memory/storage.py SQLiteManager._lock; mem0/vector_stores/base.py interface has no conditional-update method
mechanisms.limitations: Two agents updating the same memory: last writer wins silently. Two concurrent add() calls can both insert the same fact, because the hash check reads only the top-10 search snapshot. Entity linked_memory_ids updates race.
mechanisms.why: This confirms that a gap exists. ContextDB's CAS on logical heads is a real differentiator over the most-starred memory layer.

mechanisms.name: Idempotent, content-addressed flush packets (plugin EvidenceStore)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Hook events go into a local SQLite events table. prepare_flush (memory_core.py:797) runs under BEGIN IMMEDIATE. It either resumes an unfinished flush for the (repo, session) (status not in semantic-succeeded/explicitly-stored/gave-up), or claims all unflushed events. It computes packet_id = sha256(repo\0session\0event_start\0event_end)[:32], does INSERT OR IGNORE into flushes, and stamps events.flush_id with WHERE flush_id IS NULL. Retries are bounded by MAX_FLUSH_ATTEMPTS, then the flush moves to 'gave-up'. flush_worker.py and the handoff files recover pending flushes after a crash (hook_runner.recover_pending_handoffs).
mechanisms.evidence: integrations/agent-plugin-core/python/memory_core.py EvidenceStore._migrate (schema around 596-706), prepare_flush, update_flush, has_inflight_flush; hook_runner.py hand_off_flush, recover_pending_handoffs
mechanisms.limitations: Single-machine, single-writer outbox. It gives exactly-once-ish delivery to the remote API, not consistency of the memory contents.
mechanisms.why: A local outbox with content-addressed idempotency keys is a solid pattern for ContextDB's agent-side client. Writes from hooks must survive crashes and compaction without duplicate revisions.

mechanisms.name: Hybrid scoring and per-session injection ledger
mechanisms.how_it_works: _search_vector_store (main.py:1642) collects semantic candidates (dropping those below the threshold), keyword_search BM25 scores (squashed through a sigmoid whose midpoint depends on query length, get_bm25_params / normalize_bm25), and entity boosts. score_and_rank combines them as (sem + bm25 + 0.5*entity) / max_possible, then an optional reranker runs. In the plugin, EvidenceStore.retrievals (PK session_id, repo_id, memory_id) records exactly which memories, with rank, score and text, were injected into a session. unseen() filters them out of later prompts. injected_memories() replays them to subagents.
mechanisms.evidence: mem0/utils/scoring.py get_bm25_params, normalize_bm25, score_and_rank; mem0/memory/main.py _search_vector_store; integrations/agent-plugin-core/python/memory_core.py EvidenceStore.unseen / mark_injected / injected_memories, format_context
mechanisms.limitations: The ledger records ids and text, not revision or version, so it cannot detect that something injected earlier was later changed. It is not used for any gating.
mechanisms.why: The injection ledger is a near-relative of ContextDB's 'certified context read'. Record revision ids plus the dependency frontier in it and it becomes the read-set a certificate checks at action time. The hybrid scoring formula can be taken as-is for retrieval.

mechanisms.name: Agent harness hooks (capture and inject only, no gating)
mechanisms.how_it_works: In hooks.json: UserPromptSubmit and SessionStart inject searched memories as context (first_prompt_memory_output). PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure record tool evidence (record_tool / tool_payload). PreCompact, SessionEnd and Stop flush episodes to Mem0. SubagentStart and SubagentStop hand injected memories to a 'sidekick' agent running in a separate git worktree. There is no PreToolUse hook and no decision blocking.
mechanisms.evidence: integrations/claude-code-plugin/hooks/hooks.json; integrations/agent-plugin-core/python/hook_runner.py run(), first_prompt_memory_output; memory_core.py record_tool, start_subagent/stop_subagent
mechanisms.limitations: Nothing validates memories before an action, and a tool call cannot be blocked because the context it relied on went stale.
mechanisms.why: It reuses the same hook points ContextDB needs. ContextDB would add a PreToolUse certificate check (did any revision in the session's read-set get superseded or go PENDING?), which mem0 lacks entirely.

mechanisms.name: Minimal MCP tool and REST CRUD
mechanisms.how_it_works: The local stdio MCP server (mcp_server.py) implements JSON-RPC by hand (handle_request; protocol 2024-11-05). It exposes one tool, search_memories, with a strict JSON schema (additionalProperties false; scope enum; top_k 1..20). Writes happen implicitly through hooks, not as MCP tools. The REST server (server/main.py) offers CRUD plus history and reset, with admin-only configure and reset (require_admin). The hosted Platform MCP, with add/update/delete tools and OAuth, is described only in docs.
mechanisms.evidence: integrations/agent-plugin-core/python/mcp_server.py TOOL_SCHEMA, handle_request, call_search_memories; server/main.py route handlers lines 322-560; docs/platform/mem0-mcp.mdx (README-only)
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: local MCP and REST: implemented; hosted MCP tool set: README-only
mechanisms.limitations: Search is the only MCP tool, so agents cannot declare dependencies, supersede, or validate through MCP.
mechanisms.why: The design choice of one read tool, with writes captured by hooks rather than relying on the agent to call write tools, is worth copying for adoption. ContextDB adds explicit put_revision, cas_head, validate_certificate tools.

mechanisms.name: Pluggable vector backend plus SQLite side tables
mechanisms.how_it_works: VectorStoreBase (mem0/vector_stores/base.py) defines insert/search/update/delete/get/list/keyword_search/search_batch. About 25 implementations exist, chosen through utils/factory.py. History and messages live in SQLite (history_db_path). The server uses Postgres through SQLAlchemy and Alembic for auth, API keys and request logs (server/db.py, server/alembic).
mechanisms.evidence: mem0/vector_stores/base.py; mem0/utils/factory.py; mem0/memory/storage.py; server/db.py, server/models.py
mechanisms.limitations: No cross-store transaction. Vector store and SQLite history can diverge on partial failure: the code logs and continues.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB's system of record should be transactional (SQLite/Postgres), with the vector index as a derived, rebuildable projection. mem0's split without a transaction shows the failure mode to avoid.

analysis.overlap_with_contextdb:
Little overlap. mem0 has no dependency graph, no transitive invalidation, no support counting, no PENDING/structural-vs-semantic validity, no alternative (OR) justifications, no CAS or versioned heads, and no action-time gating or certificates.

Closest analogues:
(a) An append-only history audit log (storage.py). It covers text only and runs beside a mutable record.
(b) Additive-only writes (V3). Old facts are never changed by extraction, but there is also no supersedes edge. The LLM's linked_memory_ids are requested in the prompt and then dropped by the OSS code.
(c) An entity side-index used only to boost ranking.
(d) The plugin records git_sha/branch provenance per memory but never compares it with the current HEAD.
(e) The plugin's per-session retrievals ledger records what was injected, a crude read-set, but without revision ids and with no validation.
(f) Wall-clock expiration_date filtering.

Concurrency is last-writer-wins.
analysis.could_contextdb_be_built_as_plugin_on_it:
Not as the core. mem0's write path is a hard-coded LLM-extraction pipeline over a mutable vector store, with blind overwrites. There is no extension point for conditional writes, typed edges, or propagation, and VectorStoreBase has no compare-and-set. Building ContextDB inside it would mean replacing storage and the add/update semantics, which is all of mem0's core.

Realistic integration paths:
(1) Use mem0, or its pattern, as a downstream retrieval projection. ContextDB is the transactional source of truth (revisions, heads, justification DAG). It publishes current, VALID revisions into a mem0-compatible vector index, with revision_id and validity in the payload, and keeps using mem0's hybrid scoring.
(2) Copy the coding-agent harness patterns from integrations/agent-plugin-core:
- hook wiring,
- repo/dir/user scope lanes,
- the git_sha provenance capture,
- the idempotent outbox flush,
- the injection ledger.
Then extend them with a PreToolUse certificate check and a Pin dependency on git_sha.
(3) Offer a mem0-compatible API shim (add/search/get/update/delete/history), so existing mem0 users can migrate.

Licensing (Apache-2.0) allows reusing code.

checks.mechanism: Additive-only extraction (V3 pipeline)
checks.correction: The core claim holds. _add_to_vector_store (main.py:881-1220) is ADD-only: it vector-searches the top 10 in scope, builds a md5 hash dedup set from the existing results and the current batch, inserts with uuid4 ids, writes ADD history rows, then links entities and saves messages. DEFAULT_UPDATE_MEMORY_PROMPT is still defined in prompts.py:176, but nothing outside prompts.py references it, so the UPDATE/DELETE decision step really is gone. Three corrections. (1) The phase numbering is off. The code runs Phase 0 context, Phase 1 retrieval, Phase 2 LLM, Phase 3 embed, Phase 4/5 dedup, Phase 6 persist + history, Phase 7 entities, Phase 8 messages. (2) The 'anti-hallucination' mapping is half-wired. uuid_mapping is built at line 937 and never read again. The prompt (prompts.py:513) tells the LLM that linked_memory_ids 'uses the UUIDs from this list', but the list it receives has only integer ids '0'..'9'. So even if the code read the field, the ids would not resolve. (3) Old facts coexist only on the extraction path. The public update()/delete() still mutate the vector point in place and delete it (with a history row), so the record of truth is not immutable.

verification.overlap_verdict: Confirmed, with refinements. mem0 OSS has no dependency graph, no propagation, no support counting, no OR-justifications, no PENDING/validity states, no CAS or versioned heads, and no action-time gating (no PreToolUse hook exists anywhere in integrations/). Writes are last-writer-wins: entity payloads are read-modify-write without CAS, and update() overwrites the vector point in place. Corrections to the analogue list: (b) the supersession data is dropped twice over. The OSS code never reads linked_memory_ids from the LLM output, and the prompt asks for UUIDs while showing the LLM only integer ids, with uuid_mapping built and never used. So the 'supersedes' signal is broken at the prompt level as well as in the code. (a) The history log is append-only in normal operation, but reset() drops it, and explicit update()/delete() still mutate or remove the primary record. (d) The git_sha provenance is sent to the hosted Platform /v3/memories/add/ endpoint, not to OSS Memory. (e) The retrievals ledger uses INSERT OR IGNORE, so it keeps the first-injected text and could not detect later changes even in principle. (f) The expiry filter does not apply to get(memory_id).

analysis.commit_or_version_read: c5f585f8f8568ed0677eb2e70fe830c4c483e2a2 (shallow clone of default branch). Read mainly hindsight-api-slim/hindsight_api/** and hindsight-integrations/claude-code/**.
analysis.one_line_summary: Hindsight is a Python/FastAPI plus Postgres (pgvector, also Oracle) agent memory server. Retain pulls LLM-extracted facts into banks. A background LLM consolidator rolls those facts up into "observations" that keep source_memory_ids and proof_count. Mental models are pinned reflect documents that record what they cite in based_on. Invalidation is a move into an archive table. When a fact is invalidated, the observations built on it are deleted (one hop, not recursive) and their other sources are queued to be consolidated again. Mental models that cite missing facts are detected and refreshed by the LLM. There is no revision/head model, no CAS, no AND/OR justification graph, and no gating of agent actions.
analysis.architecture: Language: Python 3 (asyncio, FastAPI, asyncpg, pydantic, FastMCP), Alembic migrations (114 versions). Storage: PostgreSQL with pgvector and BM25/trigram search, plus an Oracle backend (engine/db/oracle.py, ops_oracle.py). The 'memories store' tables are listed in engine/schema.py STORE_TABLES: memory_units, memory_links, unit_entities, documents, chunks, entities, entity_cooccurrences, invalidated_memory_units. Other tables: banks, mental_models, mental_model_history, observation_history, knowledge_pages, directives, async_operations, graph_maintenance_queue. Each tenant gets its own Postgres schema (fq_table and get_current_schema in engine/schema.py). Data model: a bank is the shared memory space. memory_units rows have fact_type in world/experience/observation. Observations carry source_memory_ids UUID[], proof_count, consolidated_at and tags. memory_links are typed edges (temporal/semantic/entity/causal) that graph maintenance rebuilds. documents are retained with full-replace semantics. Process model: an API server plus workers that claim async_operations with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (worker/poller.py). Consolidation, graph maintenance and mental-model refresh run as queued jobs. API surface: a large REST API (api/http.py, about 11k lines), an MCP server (mcp_tools.py register_mcp_tools with tools retain, sync_retain, recall, reflect, list/create/update/delete/refresh/clear mental models, knowledge-base pages and folders, directives, list/get/update/invalidate memory, documents, operations, tags, banks, clear_memories), and generated clients (hindsight-clients). There are about 60 agent integrations (hindsight-integrations/*). The Claude Code plugin uses SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit (recall injected as additionalContext), Stop (async retain) and SessionEnd hooks, and no PreToolUse hook. Extension points: extensions/operation_validator.py OperationValidatorExtension (pre/post hooks on retain, recall, reflect, consolidate, memory update, bank read/write, plus tag-scope resolution).

mechanisms.name: Invalidate = move live row to archive table (no validity predicate on hot path)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Invalidating a memory does INSERT ... SELECT from memory_units into invalidated_memory_units (same columns, minus the embedding), adds invalidation_reason, invalidated_at, an entity_ids snapshot and a causal_links JSON snapshot, then deletes the memory's links and deletes the live row. Recall, consolidation and graph queries therefore need no 'is valid' filter. Revert moves the row back, rebuilds search_vector, recomputes the embedding and resets consolidation.
mechanisms.evidence: hindsight-api-slim/hindsight_api/engine/memories/pg/writes.py invalidate_memory (~L421-456), restore_memory (~L467+); alembic/versions/c9a1b2d3e4f5_add_invalidated_memory_units.py; engine/memory_engine.py update_memory_unit (L12484, Phase 2 invalidate/revert branch ~L12925-12985)
mechanisms.limitations: It is a destructive move with a single archived copy. There is no revision chain: an edit overwrites the row in place (apply_edit) and only an edited_at marker remains. Recomputable links are dropped and rebuilt later.
mechanisms.why: A live/retired split of physical storage is a cheap way to keep reads fast. ContextDB should keep immutable revisions and model retirement as RetractBase or a head move rather than deleting rows. A separate 'live head' index that recall reads from would give the same hot-path benefit.

mechanisms.name: Observation provenance via source_memory_ids + proof_count
mechanisms.how_it_works: Each consolidated observation stores source_memory_ids (UUID[]; Oracle uses an observation_sources junction table) and proof_count = count(DISTINCT sources). UPDATE actions merge new source ids into the existing list. The consolidator LLM proposes create, update and delete actions, each citing source_fact_ids. Before a write, the cited sources are rechecked as live under FOR SHARE in the same transaction.
mechanisms.evidence: engine/consolidation/consolidator.py header docstring L1-16; _CreateAction/_UpdateAction/_DeleteAction (~L768-830); _filter_live_source_memories (L695); update write path (~L3070-3200); engine/memories/pg/consolidation.py proof_count SQL (~L167, L239, L291) and FOR SHARE liveness (L44-50)
mechanisms.limitations: There is one flat OR-style source set and no AND/OR rules or typed incidences (Pin/Cur/Sem). Sources are always memories one level down. proof_count is display-only and is never used as a support counter.
mechanisms.why: This shows the provenance shape a popular product actually ships. ContextDB's justification rules generalize it, and proof_count corresponds to support count. A 'sources' import/export path could map directly to ContextDB rules.

mechanisms.name: Stale-observation sweep (one-hop dependent deletion + re-queue)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Every path that removes or changes a memory (delete_document, full-replace re-retain, curation edit or invalidate, retag) first calls delete_stale_observations. It finds observations whose source_memory_ids overlap the removed facts, row-locks the facts, the observations and the surviving co-sources in id order (FOR NO KEY UPDATE, which avoids deadlock), deletes those observations outright along with their observation_history, and sets consolidated_at=NULL on the surviving co-sources so the next consolidation run rebuilds observations from them. The sweep runs before and after the write so that a concurrent observation insert is also caught.
mechanisms.evidence: engine/memories/pg/writes.py delete_stale_observations (~L243-345); engine/retain/fact_storage.py delete_stale_observations_for_memories and handle_document_tracking; engine/memory_engine.py _delete_stale_observations_for_memories (L17000) and call sites in update_memory_unit (~L12884, L12917, L12927-12941)
mechanisms.limitations: The cascade is one hop. The rule is 'delete when any source is gone', which is stricter than support counting (an observation with 5 sources is deleted when 1 disappears). There is no PENDING state: the derived item disappears until the LLM rebuilds it. It is not transitive across observation to mental model; a separate mechanism handles that. Edits are treated like removals, so there is no semantic recheck.
mechanisms.why: This confirms in practice that derived context has to be invalidated when its premises change, and that agents tolerate re-derivation. ContextDB's improvement is to mark the dependent PENDING or UNSUPPORTED (and keep it) instead of deleting it, and to count support so that losing one of several alternatives does not kill it. The lock-ordering detail (sort every touched id, lock once) is worth copying into a Postgres-backed ContextDB.

mechanisms.name: Retracted grounding detection for mental models (based_on liveness)
mechanisms.how_it_works: A mental model's reflect_response.based_on records the cited fact ids by type. partition_retracted(based_on, live_ids) splits the citations into live and retracted, considering only memory-backed types (world, experience, observation) and never mental-models or directives. If every citation is missing, the model is classed as 'unresolvable', meaning broken provenance after an import, so the dangling citations are pruned and the prose is left alone. Otherwise the refresh asks the LLM to 'unsay' the retracted facts and then prunes based_on. After a curation delete, edit or invalidate, _submit_refreshes_for_retracted_grounding scans auto-refreshing models with _has_retracted_grounding and enqueues a refresh (skip_if_in_flight). It skips this when consolidation is still pending, because the consolidation completion hook re-checks.
mechanisms.evidence: engine/reflect/retractions.py (partition_retracted, prune_based_on, based_on_fact_ids, RetractedGrounding.unresolvable); engine/memory_engine.py _has_retracted_grounding (L20926), _submit_refreshes_for_retracted_grounding (L20960), _execute_mental_model_refresh (L17882; retraction handling ~L18200-18470)
mechanisms.limitations: Detection is by polling and absence (an id is no longer live) rather than by propagation through a dependency index. The repair is done by an LLM and is best-effort, and some repairs are deferred. A deferred retraction keeps its citation so the problem can still be noticed later. Mental models that are refreshed only manually are never nudged.
mechanisms.why: This is the closest overlap with ContextDB. The module's docstring states the key problem itself: watermarks cannot see deletions ('a retraction is the absence of a row'). Three ideas carry over directly: (1) an allowlist of which citation types resolve against which table, (2) the 'unresolvable = all citations missing → treat as broken link, not retraction' safeguard for imports, and (3) skip_if_in_flight to coalesce refreshes. ContextDB's flip-only propagation gives the same signal eagerly and precisely.

mechanisms.name: Scope-watermark staleness for mental models
mechanisms.how_it_works: Each mental model stores last_memory_seen_at, the newest memory it was built from, and last_refreshed_at. _may_need_refresh compares a bank-wide watermark as a cheap filter. _mental_model_stale_scope then builds a MemoryScopeWatermark (since, fact_types, tags, tags_match, tag_groups), and the store answers whether any memory in that scope was written after since. A tagged model is stale only when a write lands in its tags. is_stale is shown on list and get, and min_refresh_interval and refresh_after_consolidation triggers decide when to refresh.
mechanisms.evidence: engine/memory_engine.py _may_need_refresh (~L2024-2049), _mental_model_stale_scope (~L2052-2125), _resolve_min_refresh_interval (~L4701), list_mental_models(with_staleness)
mechanisms.limitations: Staleness is based on time and scope, not on dependencies. It flags any new in-scope write, even an irrelevant one, so it over-approximates. Deletions are missed, which is why the retraction mechanism exists.
mechanisms.why: It is useful as a cheap scope-level freshness signal next to ContextDB's precise dependency state, much like a version-vector 'dirty_since' hint (SD12). It also corresponds to Sem dependencies whose premise is a query rather than specific revisions.

mechanisms.name: Bounded observation_history / mental_model_history snapshots
mechanisms.how_it_works: Before an observation is rewritten, a snapshot is inserted into observation_history: previous text, tags, temporal bounds, and new_source_memory_ids. History is trimmed to observation_history_max_entries. It used to be one unbounded JSONB column, which grew past the 256MB jsonb limit. When an observation is deleted, its history is deleted explicitly. Document-level change events are recorded only as ids and counts in async_operations.result_metadata.document_events.
mechanisms.evidence: engine/consolidation/consolidator.py _ObservationHistorySnapshot and _append_observation_history (L3021-3060); alembic/versions/a7b8c9d0e1f2_split_history_into_own_tables.py; engine/document_history.py (DocumentEventKind, track_observation_changes)
mechanisms.limitations: These are audit snapshots and cannot be addressed as revisions. Nothing can be read 'as of' an earlier state. Superseded or deleted observations are hard-deleted, and per the document_history docstring 'keeping every version would cost far more storage'. There are no heads and no CAS.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB's immutable revisions plus logical heads are a stronger model. Hindsight's storage-cost argument should still be noted: ContextDB needs a GC or compaction policy for revisions that are neither heads nor pinned.

mechanisms.name: LLM-decided supersession/contradiction of observations (delete / merged_into)
mechanisms.how_it_works: The consolidation LLM may delete an observation as superseded or contradicted (_execute_delete_action), optionally naming merged_into. If merged_into is set, _fold_deleted_evidence moves the deleted observation's live sources onto the surviving observation. Otherwise the deletion retires the belief and its evidence is not re-queued, which is deliberate so that false beliefs do not come back.
mechanisms.evidence: engine/consolidation/consolidator.py _DeleteAction (~L809-830), _execute_delete_action (~L3305-3330), _fold_deleted_evidence (L3333+)
mechanisms.limitations: Supersession is not structural: there is no supersedes edge, and it depends entirely on the LLM's judgment. Raw facts are never superseded, only observations.
mechanisms.why: The 'merge moves evidence vs retire drops it' distinction maps onto ContextDB as SetHead to a new revision that inherits justifications, versus RetractBase. It suggests exposing both as explicit operations.

mechanisms.name: Two-phase edit: slow work outside txn, re-read + row locks inside short txn
mechanisms.how_it_works: update_memory_unit runs in two phases. Phase 1 reads the row, resolves entities and computes the embedding with no write transaction open. Phase 2 opens a short transaction, re-reads the row (live2/archived2), returns None if it vanished, and re-embeds only if the entity set changed between the phases. Consolidation likewise prepares each action without a connection (embedding, LLM dedup) and then commits all writes from one LLM response, together with the consolidated_at stamps, in a single transaction (#3876). Source liveness is held with FOR SHARE. In-process asyncio scope_locks per tag-scope serialize consolidation batches. _gather_or_cancel prevents orphaned batches from committing after a failure.
mechanisms.evidence: engine/memory_engine.py update_memory_unit (L12484; 'Phase 1' ~L12625, 'Phase 2' ~L12803-12830); engine/consolidation/consolidator.py _gather_or_cancel (~L88-120), scope_locks (~L2147-2157), _PreparedUpdate/_PreparedCreate (~L860-895); engine/memories/pg/consolidation.py FOR SHARE (L44-50)
mechanisms.limitations: Last writer wins, with no CAS, version token or If-Match in the REST or MCP API. Two agents editing the same memory overwrite each other silently. scope_locks only work within one process.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB should keep CAS on heads. The pattern of preparing LLM and embedding work without a connection, then revalidating and committing atomically, matches ContextDB's need to do semantic rechecks outside the single-writer commit, then CAS. A CAS failure would force a re-prepare.

mechanisms.name: Banks + tag scopes + tenant schemas for sharing
mechanisms.how_it_works: Agents share memory by writing to the same bank_id. Visibility within a bank is controlled by tags, tags_match (any/all/exact/all_strict) and tag_groups. OperationValidatorExtension.resolve_tag_scope and resolve_write_tag_scope can force a caller's scope. When an observation is updated, the source facts' tags are merged into it so that every contributor can see it (marked SECURITY in the code). Tenants are isolated by Postgres schema. Integrations derive the bank id from project context (claude-code scripts/lib/bank.py derive_bank_id).
mechanisms.evidence: engine/search/tags.py; extensions/operation_validator.py resolve_tag_scope (~L966), resolve_write_tag_scope (~L1010); consolidator.py tag merge in the update path (~L3135-3140); engine/schema.py fq_table; hindsight-integrations/claude-code/scripts/recall.py
mechanisms.limitations: There is no per-agent principal on facts beyond tags and metadata, no branches, and no read-your-writes or snapshot guarantee across agents. Retain is asynchronous, so other agents see writes only after extraction.
mechanisms.why: Tag-scoped visibility with server-side forced scopes is a proven multi-tenant ACL pattern. ContextDB's PrincipalId (M3) could adopt resolve_*_tag_scope-style hooks.

mechanisms.name: OperationValidatorExtension (pre/post hooks on memory ops, not on agent actions)
mechanisms.how_it_works: This is a pluggable ABC with precheck (runs before the body is parsed), validate_retain, validate_recall, validate_reflect, validate_consolidate, validate_memory_update, validate_bank_read/write and validate_mental_model_*. Validators return a ValidationResult that accepts, rejects (with an HTTP status) or accepts with enrichment (injected tags or contents). There are matching on_*_complete post-hooks, and filter_mcp_tools can hide MCP tools.
mechanisms.evidence: hindsight-api-slim/hindsight_api/extensions/operation_validator.py (ValidationResult L29-80, OperationValidatorExtension L679+, methods L729-1281)
mechanisms.limitations: It gates access to the memory API (quotas, authorization, scoping). It does not check whether the context an agent acted on is still valid when the agent acts. There are no certificates. The Claude Code plugin has no PreToolUse hook.
mechanisms.why: The accept/reject/accept_with(enrichment) hook shape and the precheck-before-parse split are good API patterns for ContextDB's action-time certificate validation hook. The certificate semantics themselves would be new, because nothing in Hindsight provides them.

mechanisms.name: MCP tool surface + agent hook integrations (recall-on-prompt, retain-on-stop)
mechanisms.how_it_works: register_mcp_tools exposes about 40 tools (retain/recall/reflect, mental models, knowledge pages, directives, memory get/update/invalidate, documents, operations, banks), and recall takes a max_tokens budget. The Claude Code plugin injects recall results through UserPromptSubmit additionalContext, retains the transcript asynchronously on Stop, and saves the last recall so it can be re-injected after compaction. About 60 framework integrations follow the same pattern.
mechanisms.evidence: hindsight-api-slim/hindsight_api/mcp_tools.py register_mcp_tools (L611) and _register_* (L1010-4653); hindsight-integrations/claude-code/hooks/hooks.json, scripts/recall.py, scripts/retain.py
mechanisms.limitations: Recall output carries no version vector or certificate, so a consumer cannot later prove what it read.
mechanisms.why: Retain/recall/reflect is the interaction shape agents already adopt widely. ContextDB's MCP surface should look familiar (recall with max_tokens, invalidate_memory) and add certified reads, meaning recall that returns a certificate, plus a validate_certificate tool or PreToolUse hook.

mechanisms.name: Hybrid recall: semantic + BM25 + graph + temporal, RRF fusion, cross-encoder rerank, token budget
mechanisms.how_it_works: Up to four retrieval arms run in parallel, results are merged with reciprocal_rank_fusion (k=60), optionally reranked with a cross-encoder, and trimmed to max_tokens. Observations can carry their source facts, and graph expansion follows memory_links.
mechanisms.evidence: engine/search/fusion.py reciprocal_rank_fusion (L29); engine/search/retrieval.py, reranking.py, graph_retrieval.py; engine/memories/pg/recall.py
mechanisms.limitations: Retrieval ignores validity, because only live rows exist. It has no notion of PENDING items.
mechanisms.why: Proven retrieval stack. ContextDB can layer status filtering (SUPPORTED/PENDING) and certificates on top rather than inventing retrieval.

mechanisms.name: Postgres-first with backend abstraction; queue workers with SKIP LOCKED
mechanisms.how_it_works: DatabaseBackend/ops abstractions (PG and Oracle) sit behind a 'memories store' seam: get_memories() is the only code allowed to touch STORE_TABLES, and the guard raises StoreTableAccessError otherwise. Background jobs live in an async_operations table that workers claim with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Retention sweeps also claim with SKIP LOCKED.
mechanisms.evidence: engine/schema.py STORE_TABLES/_guard; engine/memories/__init__.py get_memories; worker/poller.py (L5, L324, L573); engine/maintenance.py (~L307-329)
mechanisms.limitations: The design relies on Postgres row locks. It has no in-memory incremental engine.
mechanisms.why: The store seam (a pluggable memories store) and the SKIP LOCKED job queue are cheap patterns to reuse for a ContextDB server that persists to Postgres while running the propagation core in Rust.

analysis.overlap_with_contextdb: Partial and one hop only. (1) Dependency-driven invalidation: YES for fact to observation, through source_memory_ids. When any source is removed or edited, the observation is hard-deleted and its other sources are queued for re-consolidation (delete_stale_observations). This is any-source-gone deletion, not support counting, and the derived item vanishes instead of becoming PENDING. Fact or observation to mental model is handled separately: retraction is detected by polling (partition_retracted / _has_retracted_grounding) and repaired by an LLM refresh. The two hops are not one transitive propagation and there is no general dependency graph; memory_links (temporal/semantic/entity/causal) are retrieval edges, not justification edges. (2) Alternative support (OR of AND-rules, support counts): NO. proof_count is display-only, losing one of N sources still deletes the observation, and there are no AND/OR rules or typed Pin/Cur/Sem incidences. (3) Structural vs semantic validity: NO separate PENDING state. Scope watermarks give an over-approximate 'is_stale' flag for mental models. (4) Immutable revisions, heads and CAS: NO. Edits are in place, observations are rewritten with bounded audit snapshots, and writes are last-writer-wins with no version token in the API. (5) Certified reads and action gating: NO. OperationValidatorExtension gates memory API calls (auth, quota, scope), not agent actions against the freshness of the context they read, and the Claude Code plugin has no PreToolUse hook.
analysis.could_contextdb_be_built_as_plugin_on_it: Not as a core, but as a companion. Hindsight's extension points are OperationValidatorExtension pre/post hooks, the get_memories() store seam (engine/memories/__init__.py, base.py), and tenant/tag-scope hooks. A replacement memories store could in principle intercept every write, including delete_stale_observations, invalidate_memory and rewrite_observation, and keep a ContextDB justification graph behind it. However, the engine's semantics (hard delete of derived observations, in-place edits, LLM-decided deletes) conflict with immutable revisions and with keeping a dependent as PENDING. It would also mean forking a Python codebase of about 180k lines that changes quickly. The realistic options are: (a) build ContextDB as its own service with a Hindsight-compatible MCP shape (retain/recall/reflect/invalidate_memory) and lift the proven ideas (live/archive split, one-hop sweep lock ordering, retracted-grounding allowlist and 'unresolvable' guard, skip_if_in_flight refresh coalescing, two-phase prepare-then-commit, the accept_with validator hook shape); or (b) add a thin adapter that mirrors Hindsight observations (source_memory_ids) and mental models (based_on) into ContextDB as justification rules, so ContextDB adds certified reads and action-time validation on top of a Hindsight deployment without changing its engine.

Revert also rematerializes the causal links, restores the entity postings and enqueues graph maintenance. apply_edit really does edit in place (edited_at=now(), consolidated_at=NULL) and keeps causal links while dropping derived links.

verification.overlap_verdict: Confirmed with two corrections. (a) Point (2) 'proof_count is display-only' is wrong. proof_count is a small reranking boost (about ±5%) and an input to the LLM prompt, but it is still not a support counter: losing any one source deletes the observation (the writes.py docstring says the text is stale 'once even one source memory disappears'). (b) Point (4) 'last-writer-wins with no version token' holds for the public REST/MCP curation API and for update_memory_unit. Internally, consolidation uses optimistic concurrency control: updated_at read-validation under FOR SHARE discards a whole LLM batch if any source was edited (#4831), and the observation fold and rewrite UPDATEs are compare-and-set on the expected text. That makes it the closest existing analogue to ContextDB's 'prepare outside, CAS on commit' pattern, although it is not head/revision CAS. Everything else in the overlap claim is confirmed: one-hop source_memory_ids invalidation with hard delete and re-queue; a separate polling-based retracted-grounding path for mental models with an LLM 'unsay' repair (the staleness check now includes it); no transitive justification graph (memory_links are retrieval edges); no PENDING state; no AND/OR rules or typed incidences; edits in place with an archive table for invalidation; no certified reads or action gating. One further correction to the integration claim: the Claude Code plugin has no PreToolUse hook, and its 'post-compaction re-injection' of last_recall.json is written but never read.

analysis.one_line_summary: OpenViking is a "context database" only in the retrieval sense. It is a multi-tenant virtual filesystem (viking:// URIs) with L0/L1/L2 LLM-generated summaries, vector search, LLM-driven memory extraction, path-lease locks, git-style snapshot commits with CAS on branch refs, ACLs and an MCP server. It has no justification graph, no per-item revisions or supersession, no dependency-driven invalidation of beliefs, and no action-time validity gating.
analysis.architecture:
Languages: Python server (openviking/, FastAPI, about 1170 non-test .py files), a Rust storage core "ragfs" (crates/ragfs, exposed to Python through crates/ragfs-python/src/lib.rs as pyo3 bindings), a C++ local vector index (src/), and a Rust CLI (crates/ov_cli).

Storage:
(1) VikingFS, a virtual filesystem over AGFS/ragfs with multibackend providers: local filesystem, S3 and a Redis cache (crates/ragfs/src/multibackend/provider/{filesystem,cache}.rs). It holds content files, with .abstract.md (L0) and .overview.md (L1) sidecars per directory, plus .relations.json.
(2) A vector index: a local C++ index (openviking/storage/vectordb/index/local_index.py), cuVS, or VikingDB, plus MySQL adapters. Schema is in openviking/storage/collection_schemas.py. Fields are id, uri, type, context_type, vector, sparse_vector, created_at, updated_at, active_count, level, abstract, content, md5, account_id, owner_user_id and acl fields. There is no version field.
(3) A git object store and ref store in Rust (crates/ragfs/src/git/{service.rs,ref_store.rs,object_store.rs,backends/local.rs,s3.rs}) for snapshots.
(4) Path-lock tokens (crates/ragfs/src/lock/*).

Data model:
- URI tree with fixed scopes: viking://resources/, viking://user/{id}/memories/..., viking://agent/skills/, peers/ and sessions/.
- Memory files are markdown with MEMORY_FIELDS metadata, typed by a memory-type registry (openviking/session/memory/memory_type_registry.py).
- Per-field merge ops: patch, replace, sum, immutable (openviking/session/memory/merge_op/).
- StoredLink {from_uri, to_uri, link_type, weight, match_text, description, created_at} (openviking/session/memory/dataclass.py:127) is an untyped associative link, not a premise.

Process model: one async server process with background queues (openviking/storage/queuefs/semantic_processor.py) for summarization and vectorization, an expiry scheduler with shard leases (openviking/scheduling/expiry/), and sessions that run LLM extraction loops (session/memory/extract_loop.py, session/compressor_v3.py).

API surface:
- REST routers in openviking/server/routers/: filesystem, content, search, sessions, skills, snapshot, watches, acl, pack, tasks and others.
- MCP server in openviking/server/mcp_endpoint.py with tools list_users, list_groups, get_acl, set_acl, find, search, read, download, list, tree, remember, write, edit, add_resource, add_skill, list_watches, cancel_watch, grep, glob, forget and health.
- Agent plugins with Claude Code, Codex and other hooks under examples/*-memory-plugin and examples/agent-hook-plugin: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit auto-recall, Stop auto-capture, a PreToolUse uri-guard, and SubagentStart/Stop.

mechanisms.name: PathLock leases (Exact/Tree) with stale-token takeover via compare-and-write
mechanisms.how_it_works: Lock tokens {owner_id, time_ns, lock_type E|T} are stored per path. The filesystem provider uses lock files; the cache provider uses Redis. acquire_batch normalizes requests and checks ancestor Tree locks and descendant locks, then does try_create_token. If a token exists and is older than lock_expire_secs (default 30s), compare_and_write_token(expected=observed stale token) takes it over, so a concurrent heartbeat is not erased. A background task refreshes held leases every expire/3 and releases leases idle for more than 2x expire. Leases have an opaque lease_ref plus an ownership_ref capability for refresh/release. They support handoff/adopt across queue workers (PathLockHandoffRef) so an HTTP write can pass its lock to the async semantic worker. Polling uses exponential backoff with jitter (50ms to 500ms).
mechanisms.evidence: crates/ragfs/src/lock/types.rs (PathLockKind, LockToken, PathLockLease::covers, PathLockHandoffRef); crates/ragfs/src/lock/manager.rs: PathLockConfig (l.29-49), acquire_batch (l.840), try_acquire_one (l.1175-1234, stale CAS takeover), check_ancestor_tree_locks (l.1254), check_descendant_locks (l.1291), refresh (l.1362), handoff (l.1713), adopt (l.1734), background stale release (l.512-612); crates/ragfs/src/lock/provider.rs PathLockProvider::compare_and_write_token, try_acquire_batch_atomic; Python usage in openviking/storage/content_write.py (_enqueue_lock_coordinator l.1033, _finish_write_lock l.1070).
mechanisms.limitations: These are pessimistic, time-based leases with no fencing token. A paused holder whose lease went stale can still write after takeover, because writes take lease_ref but storage does not check a monotonic epoch. Locks guard paths, not logical items or versions. Many read-modify-write flows read outside the lock. The MCP edit tool reads with service.fs.read_visible and then calls fs.write, which takes its own lock, so lost updates between two agents are possible (openviking/server/mcp_endpoint.py edit, l.1341-1385). Session memory extraction passes transaction_handle=None (session/compressor_v3.py l.635, l.714), so the LLM read-decide-write is not atomic across concurrent sessions.
mechanisms.why: Tree vs Exact hierarchical leases and lock handoff to async workers are useful for ContextDB's background recompute workers. ContextDB should keep optimistic CAS on logical heads as the correctness primitive, and use leases only for liveness and work distribution, with fencing via epoch or expected head.

mechanisms.name: Git-style snapshots: content-addressed commits + CAS branch ref update
mechanisms.how_it_works: commit() enumerates the account tree, or the given paths. It builds a git tree from blobs (gix object ids), writes a commit object whose parent is prev_head, then calls RefStore::cas_update(account, ref, expected=prev_head, new=commit_oid). On a mismatch it returns GitError::ConcurrentCommit {expected, actual} without retrying, and the caller decides. restore(source_commit) computes a diff, CAS-swaps the ref first, then writes the diff back into the VFS only after the swap succeeds, so a losing CAS race leaves the working tree untouched. The new commit's parent is the current HEAD, not the source. log walks parents[0]. A commit index cache (parent_oid + size/mtime) skips rehashing and falls back safely on a mismatch. Non-root commits take PathLock Exact/Tree leases on the scoped paths.
mechanisms.evidence: crates/ragfs/src/git/ref_store.rs (RefStore::cas_update); crates/ragfs/src/git/service.rs commit (l.130), commit_impl CAS step (l.718-737), restore (l.981, ordering comment l.1098-1103, Conflict mapping l.1164); openviking/storage/viking_fs/_snapshot.py commit (l.196-299), restore (l.312); REST openviking/server/routers/snapshot.py (/commit, /log, /restore, /show, /diff, /ignore).
mechanisms.limitations: Versioning is coarse, at account or subtree level, and explicit: an admin or API call creates a snapshot, while normal writes overwrite files in place. There is no per-memory revision history, no logical-head per item, no supersedes edge, and no read-at-version API for retrieval (search always hits live state). Branch is a parameter but there is no merge.
mechanisms.why: This is a proven implementation of ContextDB's 'immutable revisions + head pointer + CAS' pattern: content-addressed immutable objects, a ref CAS with expected=None meaning create-only, ConcurrentCommit returned to the caller, and 'swap ref first, then side effects'. ContextDB can mirror the RefStore trait shape per logical item rather than per branch.

mechanisms.name: Memory replacement = delete + write with link inheritance (destructive supersession)
mechanisms.how_it_works: The LLM extract loop emits upserts and DeleteId{delete_page_id, replacement_page_id}. apply_operations builds uri_remap (deleted to replacement) and applies upserts. It drops remaps whose replacement write failed, then _inherit_deleted_link_relations copies links and backlinks from the deleted file onto the replacement using merge_links (dedup on from|to|match_text, weight=max, last-writer-wins on type and description). Only then does it delete the old file, and it skips the delete if any upsert in the batch was unresolved or if link migration failed. Field-level merge ops: IMMUTABLE keeps the first non-blank value, SUM adds, REPLACE overwrites, PATCH applies SEARCH/REPLACE blocks with fuzzy matching.
mechanisms.evidence: openviking/session/memory/memory_updater.py apply_operations (l.872-1129), _invalid_replacement_sources (l.1131), _inherit_deleted_link_relations (l.1594), _apply_upsert (l.1368, re-reads disk before patching); openviking/session/memory/dataclass.py DeleteId (l.139), StoredLink (l.127); merge_op/link_merge.py merge_links; merge_op/immutable.py ImmutableOp.apply; merge_op/patch_handler.py apply_str_patch/fuzzy_search.
mechanisms.limitations: The old version is physically deleted, so no history is kept unless a snapshot was committed. Nothing that depended on the deleted memory is invalidated: links are just rewired to the replacement, which silently transfers trust. Contradiction and supersession decisions are made entirely by the LLM. The batch is not atomic, it is applied step by step with error lists and no rollback.
mechanisms.why: This is the anti-pattern ContextDB is designed against. Rewiring dependents to the replacement assumes the replacement satisfies them, which is the opposite of ContextDB's Pin/Cur semantics, where dependents should go PENDING or UNSUPPORTED. The ordering safeguard (no delete unless the replacement write and link migration succeeded) is still worth copying.

mechanisms.name: Upward summary freshness: pending-change counters + digest-based early cutoff
mechanisms.how_it_works: Each directory has L0 (.abstract.md) and L1 (.overview.md) sidecars with OKF frontmatter, including freshness {total_entries, sampled_entries, unsampled_entries, pending_child_changes}. When a child's L0 body changes, which semantic_body_digest compares before and after, _enqueue_parent_refresh calls plan_abstract_overview_refresh. Under one exact-path lease on both sidecars, it increments pending_child_changes. decide_parent_refresh then returns NOOP if the body did not change, REFRESH_NOW if there is no baseline, the directory is small, or pending/total >= refresh_ratio (0.10), and MARK_PENDING otherwise. The refreshed parent propagates to its own parent only if its own abstract body digest changed. This is change-only propagation with an early cutoff, like ContextDB's flip-only propagation.
mechanisms.evidence: openviking/storage/abstract_overview.py freshness_metadata (l.503), semantic_body_digest (l.483), write_abstract_overview body-changed computation (l.606-613), plan_abstract_overview_refresh (l.671-779), read_abstract_overview_pending_snapshot (l.782); openviking/storage/queuefs/semantic_ops/freshness_policy.py decide_parent_refresh; openviking/storage/queuefs/semantic_processor.py _enqueue_parent_refresh (l.348-435) and the callers with l0_body_changed=write_result.abstract_body_changed (l.655-661, l.781-787).
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented (README only mentions L0/L1/L2 summaries; the freshness policy is code-only)
mechanisms.limitations: It only follows the directory tree (child to parent), not arbitrary dependency DAGs. The counter counts change events, not distinct children. Staleness is a tolerated, ratio-thresholded approximation (MARK_PENDING): stale summaries stay readable and searchable with no 'not certified' flag at read time. The comparison is exact text digest, not semantic.
mechanisms.why: This validates two ContextDB ideas in production: (a) propagate only on actual change, with digest early cutoff, and (b) keep a PENDING state instead of eagerly recomputing LLM-derived artifacts. ContextDB generalizes it to typed DAG edges and must expose PENDING in reads, which OpenViking does not.

mechanisms.name: Resource diff / index-state classification (content vs vector index)
mechanisms.how_it_works: When a resource is re-ingested, each path gets a ContentState and an IndexState: ABSENT, COMPLETE, MISSING, PARTIAL, STALE (md5 mismatch), OBSOLETE (content deleted but vectors remain), ORPHAN, or LEVEL_CONFLICT. Precedence is strict, and the result drives vector repair and cleanup. index_consistency.py checks the expected L0/L1/L2 records against the vector index for a subtree.
mechanisms.evidence: openviking/storage/resource_diff.py IndexState enum (l.~85-104), ResourceDiffEntry, _index_state (l.~187-215); openviking/storage/index_consistency.py IndexExpectation, IndexConsistencyReport; md5 field in collection_schemas.py (l.127).
mechanisms.limitations: These are derived-index consistency checks (file to embedding), one hop, keyed by md5. They do not cover semantic validity of knowledge.
mechanisms.why: The enum precedence design is a good template for ContextDB's derived-artifact (embedding/summary) status, kept separate from the belief-validity status.

mechanisms.name: Experience-consumption lineage via search tags
mechanisms.how_it_works: After a session, collect_read_experience_uris scans tool-call parts for completed read/multi_read calls, including MCP mcp__openviking__read, and extracts the canonical Experience URIs the agent actually read. Failed reads are excluded using per-URI success flags. trajectory_analyzer stores the resulting trajectory with search_tags = escaped '<experience_uri>=1' plus 'trajectory_outcome=<success|failure|...>'. agent_evolution_service can then filter trajectories by experience and outcome to score experiences.
mechanisms.evidence: openviking/session/memory/experience_lineage.py collect_read_experience_uris, experience_source_tags, trajectory_outcome_tag; openviking/session/train/components/trajectory_analyzer.py (l.183, l.447-454); openviking/service/agent_evolution_service.py (l.213).
mechanisms.limitations: The URI is recorded without a version or md5, so you cannot tell which content was consumed. It is inferred after the fact from transcripts, not declared by the agent. It is used for outcome statistics, not invalidation: when an experience changes, trajectories that consumed it are not flagged.
mechanisms.why: It is close to ContextDB's 'certified context read' plus Ref edges. ContextDB should record revision ids at read time (certificate) instead of bare URIs, and can reuse the idea of deriving read-sets from tool-call transcripts for agents that do not declare them.

mechanisms.name: Context assembler with token budget, tiers and cross-turn recall ledger
mechanisms.how_it_works: A single request runs: expand queries, gather candidates (hierarchical directory-aware retrieval), plan_entries under a budget with per-type quotas and tier degradation (L0 abstract, then L1, then L2 body), render, and optionally rewrite with an LLM. RecallLedger keeps a .recall_log.json per session recording which URI was served at which turn and tier. URIs served within dedup_turns are cooled down (excluded). Failures degrade to no dedup. Hotness = sigmoid(log1p(active_count)) * exponential decay with a 7-day half-life.
mechanisms.evidence: openviking/retrieve/context_assembler/pipeline.py, budget.py (plan_entries, per_entry_cap), tiers.py, ledger.py (RecallLedger, LEDGER_FILENAME, cooled_uris), gather.py; openviking/retrieve/hierarchical_retriever.py; openviking/retrieve/memory_lifecycle.py hotness_score.
mechanisms.limitations: The ledger stores URI, turn and tier, but no revision or validity, so it cannot detect that served context later became stale. Packing ignores validity and supersession.
mechanisms.why: The served-context ledger is the natural place to attach ContextDB read certificates (revision vector), and budgeted tiered packing (abstract, then overview, then body) is a proven packing strategy to reuse.

mechanisms.name: Multi-tenant namespaces + ACL + peer/self memory isolation
mechanisms.how_it_works: RequestContext carries account, user and role (ROOT/ADMIN/USER). URIs are scoped to user/{id}, agent and resources. Context-backed ACLs have levels read, write and manage, with acl_mode none/inherit/restricted and principals user:<id>, group:<id> and user:*; they are stored as fields on vector records and enforced through filter expressions. MemoryIsolationHandler resolves which user or peer a session-extracted memory may be written to, with skip codes such as PEER_NOT_ALLOWED and AMBIGUOUS_TARGET.
mechanisms.evidence: openviking/storage/acl.py (AclLevel, AclMode, resolution); openviking/session/memory/memory_isolation_handler.py (_SKIP_REASON_MESSAGES, RoleScope, _TargetResolution); openviking/server/identity.py; MCP get_acl/set_acl in openviking/server/mcp_endpoint.py (l.406-436).
mechanisms.limitations: Agents share by writing to the same URIs. Consistency is last-writer-wins, guarded only by short path locks. There are no branches or workspaces per agent for memory (snapshots have a branch parameter but no merge), and no notification to readers when shared content changes, apart from the watches feature, which re-ingests external sources.
mechanisms.why: The ACL and principal model and the URI namespacing are reusable for ContextDB's principal parameter (SD13). The consistency model is what ContextDB should improve on.

mechanisms.name: Agent hook plugins (auto-recall / auto-capture / uri-guard)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Claude Code and Codex plugins register hooks: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit (auto-recall injects retrieved context), PostToolUse on Read (skill-experience), PreToolUse on Read|Glob|Grep|Edit|Write|Bash (uri-guard), Stop and SubagentStop (auto-capture sends the transcript to a session commit), and PreCompact and SessionEnd. uri-guard only denies local file tools whose path arguments contain a viking:// URI, which redirects the agent to the MCP tools.
mechanisms.evidence: examples/claude-code-memory-plugin/hooks/hooks.json; examples/claude-code-memory-plugin/scripts/uri-guard.mjs and scripts/shared/uri-guard.mjs (findVikingUri, DEFAULT_URI_KEYS/DEFAULT_CONTENT_KEYS); scripts/auto-recall.mjs, auto-capture.mjs, subagent-start.mjs, subagent-stop.mjs.
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented (as example plugins; not a server-side gate)
mechanisms.limitations: There is no validity or certificate check before actions. PreToolUse does path routing only, and nothing checks that the context an action relied on is still current.
mechanisms.why: It shows the exact hook surface ContextDB needs: recall at UserPromptSubmit, capture at Stop and SubagentStop, and gating at PreToolUse. ContextDB's PreToolUse would validate the action certificate (revision vector vs current heads) instead of matching URI patterns.

mechanisms.name: MCP tool surface (filesystem-shaped)
mechanisms.how_it_works: FastMCP tools mirror a filesystem: find/search (semantic), read, download, list, tree, grep, glob, write (replace/append/create, optional wait for indexing), edit (exact-string replace), forget (delete), remember (send messages for extraction), add_resource and add_skill, list_watches and cancel_watch, ACL tools and health. Tool annotations mark read-only, destructive and retry-safe. Errors are mapped to structured tool failures. Write results include indexing status hints (semantic/vector queued).
mechanisms.evidence: openviking/server/mcp_endpoint.py @mcp.tool registrations (l.358-2196), write (l.1305), edit (l.1341-1385), _indexing_hint, _mcp_error_results (l.301).
mechanisms.limitations: No tool takes an expected version or precondition. edit does read-then-write with no lock or CAS, so concurrent agents can lose updates. Reads do not return version or validity metadata. There is no 'why' or 'why not' tool.
mechanisms.why: A filesystem-shaped MCP surface (read, write, edit, ls, tree, grep) is a proven agent ergonomic at 40k stars. ContextDB should keep these verbs but add expected_head on writes and return revision ids and validity on reads.

mechanisms.name: Pluggable multibackend storage + background vectorization queue
mechanisms.how_it_works: ragfs routes paths to the local filesystem, S3 or a Redis cache backend, with encryption and multibackend GC wrappers. Writes go to the VFS synchronously. Semantic summarization and embedding run asynchronously in queuefs workers, which take the lock by handoff. wait=true blocks until the index reflects the write.
mechanisms.evidence: crates/ragfs/src/multibackend/{runtime.rs,gc.rs,provider/filesystem.rs,provider/cache.rs}; crates/ragfs/src/core/encryption_wrapper.rs; openviking/storage/queuefs/semantic_processor.py; openviking/storage/content_write.py _write_direct_with_refresh (l.1554), _wait_for_request (l.2092).
mechanisms.limitations: Search is eventually consistent with writes, and readers cannot see whether a hit is indexed from the latest content, other than through the md5 field.
mechanisms.why: This is an infrastructure choice. ContextDB's kernel needs a transactional store for heads and rules; blob and embedding storage can be anything.

mechanisms.name: Justification graph / support counting / typed dependencies / certified reads
mechanisms.how_it_works: Does not exist. No AND/OR justification structure, no support counts, no Pin/Cur/Sem/Ref edge types, no structural vs semantic validity, no PENDING state on knowledge items, and no read or action certificates. The only 'links' are associative StoredLinks with weight and type strings, used for navigation and graph view (openviking/session/memory/graph_view.py).
mechanisms.evidence: Searched openviking/ for supersed|invalidat|valid_until|obsolete: the only hits are in lock, cache, OAuth and config code, plus resource_diff's OBSOLETE index state. StoredLink in openviking/session/memory/dataclass.py:127. merge_links in merge_op/link_merge.py.
mechanisms.limitations: N/A
mechanisms.why: This confirms there is no overlap with ContextDB's core contribution.

analysis.overlap_with_contextdb:
OpenViking overlaps in positioning ("Context Database for AI Agents") and in plumbing, not in semantics.

Feature by feature:
- Dependency-driven transitive invalidation: no. The only propagation is tree-shaped directory summary refresh. A child's L0 digest change bumps the parent's pending_child_changes, and the refresh moves upward only if the parent's own digest changed. That is change-only propagation with an early cutoff, but it is limited to parent/child directories and to regenerating LLM summaries, not to belief validity.
- Memory links: they are associative StoredLinks. When a memory is replaced, its links are re-pointed to the replacement (_inherit_deleted_link_relations) instead of invalidating dependents.
- Alternative support (OR justifications, support counting): none.
- Revisions and supersession: per-item revisions do not exist, and replace means delete plus write. Git-style subtree snapshots exist, with content-addressed commits and a CAS branch ref (RefStore::cas_update, ConcurrentCommit error) and restore that swaps the ref before writing back. These are explicit, coarse and not used by retrieval.
- Concurrency: path leases (Exact/Tree, stale takeover by compare-and-write, handoff to workers), but no optimistic preconditions on the write API. The MCP edit tool and LLM memory extraction do read-modify-write outside the lock, so lost updates are possible.
- Action gating: none. Hooks do recall, capture and URI routing only; PreToolUse uri-guard only blocks local tools from touching viking:// paths.
- Certified reads: none. The recall ledger records URI, turn and tier per session without revision or validity.
- Provenance: Experience-read lineage (which experience URIs a trajectory read, plus its outcome) is stored as search tags without versions.

Net: OpenViking is a mature retrieval and storage substrate plus agent integration. ContextDB's justification/validity kernel would be entirely new relative to it.
analysis.could_contextdb_be_built_as_plugin_on_it:
Partially, and only as an external sidecar. It cannot be an in-process plugin.

Why not in-process:
- OpenViking has no extension point for validity semantics.
- Its write path mutates files in place, and replacement deletes the old file, so ContextDB's immutable revisions would have to live outside OpenViking or be encoded as distinct URIs, e.g. item/rev-<id>.md plus a head pointer file.
- OpenViking's own LLM extractor rewrites and deletes memories, re-pointing links without consulting any dependency graph. ContextDB would have to disable or wrap the extractor (remember, session commit) to keep its invariants.
- The write APIs (MCP write/edit, REST content) take no expected-version precondition, so head CAS would have to be enforced by ContextDB itself. A reusable alternative is the ragfs git RefStore::cas_update per logical item, which is not exposed per item today.

What is feasible:
- Use OpenViking as the blob, search and summary layer: viking:// URIs as revision payload storage, its hierarchical retrieval and budgeted context assembler for candidate gathering, and its ACL and principal model.
- Run the ContextDB kernel (heads, rules, support counts, L0/L1/L2 validity, certificates) as a separate service that wraps the MCP surface. It would add expected_head to writes, return revision ids and validity with reads, and log certificates in place of the recall ledger.
- Attach ContextDB's PreToolUse certificate check to the same Claude Code and Codex hook points that OpenViking's plugins already use.

Licensing caveat: the main project is AGPL-3.0, so a network service that modifies or links it inherits copyleft obligations. Reimplementing the proven patterns (RefStore CAS shape, digest early cutoff with pending counters, lease handoff, tiered budget packing) is cleaner than building on its code.
