verification.overlap_verdict: I confirm the overlap claim, with two small corrections. (1) Supersession: OpenViking has a structural supersede operation for Experiences, driven by an LLM-emitted `supersedes` field (agent_experience_context_provider.py l.88-100). The old experience is deleted, and its history and links are inherited through _inherit_deleted_link_relations (memory_updater.py l.1594). It is delete-plus-inherit with no retained supersedes edge, revision, or head, so 'no per-item revisions or supersession' holds in substance but not literally. (2) The snapshot commit's path locks come from the Python _snapshot.py layer, not from Rust commit_impl. Everything else in the overlap summary checks out against the source. Path leases with CAS stale takeover exist, but there is no fencing or epoch and no expected-version on any write or MCP API. MCP edit and session extraction (transaction_handle=None) do read-modify-write outside a lock, so lost updates are possible. Propagation is limited to directory-tree summary refresh, with a digest cutoff and a ratio-threshold MARK_PENDING. I found no OR-justification or support counting, no action gating beyond viking:// URI routing (deny for file tools, notice only for shell), and no revision in the recall ledger or the experience lineage tags. Net: OpenViking is a mature storage, retrieval and agent-integration substrate, and ContextDB's justification and validity kernel would be new relative to it.

analysis.one_line_summary: Python 'AI memory' engine. An LLM extracts a knowledge graph from documents (add, then cognify, then memify/improve) into pluggable graph, vector and relational stores, with MCP and REST access. What is worth reusing is the plumbing: refcounted source-ref ownership for deletes, transitive purge of session caches when the data behind them is deleted, a hash-chained PROV-O ledger, and propose/review/apply action gates. It has no revision heads, no CAS and no justification-DAG truth maintenance.
analysis.architecture: Language: Python 3, async (asyncio and SQLAlchemy async), FastAPI REST under cognee/api/v1/*, a CLI (cognee/cli), and an MCP server (cognee-mcp/src/server.py, FastMCP). Storage is three pluggable backends at once. (1) Graph: Ladybug/Kuzu by default, plus Neo4j, Neptune, Postgres-demo and Turso adapters in cognee/infrastructure/databases/graph/*, written with idempotent Cypher MERGE. (2) Vector: LanceDB by default, plus pgvector and Turso (infrastructure/databases/vector/*). One collection per '<Type>_<field>' (DataPoint.vector_collection). (3) Relational: SQLite or Postgres via SQLAlchemy plus alembic. Holds users, tenants, ACLs, datasets, Data rows, pipeline runs and the provenance_entries ledger. Session memory sits in a cache (fs, SQL or Redis-style adapters under infrastructure/databases/cache, infrastructure/session/session_manager.py). Data model: everything is a pydantic DataPoint (infrastructure/engine/models/DataPoint.py). The id is a random uuid4, or a deterministic uuid5 over metadata.identity_fields (DataPoint.id_for), so the same entity merges across ingestions. Nested DataPoint fields become edges. Each node carries source_pipeline/source_task/source_user/source_content_hash, feedback_weight and importance_weight, an int 'version' plus update_version(), and ontology_valid/ontology_uri. Graph nodes and edges also carry source_ref_keys and source_run_refs columns for ownership. Process model: in-process library or FastAPI server. Pipelines are task lists (modules/pipelines/operations/run_tasks.py). Locks are per-dataset asyncio locks that only work within one process. MCP tools: remember, recall, code_search, forget, improve, cognify_status (server.py lines 357-1059). The default dataset is scoped per agent from MCP clientInfo.name, e.g. 'cursor_vscode_memory' (_agent_scoped_default_dataset). Agent SDK: an @agent_memory decorator (modules/agent_memory/decorator.py) wraps an agent entry point. It retrieves memory context before the call and persists traces afterwards. Agents are tracked in an in-process registry (modules/agents/registry.py).

mechanisms.name: Refcounted source-ref ownership (multi-owner artifacts, delete when the last owner goes)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Every graph node and edge written by a pipeline is stamped with a set of owner keys. The keys are 'v1:{dataset}:{data}' at document scope or 'v2 chunk:{dataset}:{data}:{chunk}' at chunk scope (make_source_ref_key / make_chunk_source_ref_key). Stamping happens inside the same Cypher MERGE statement as the write (_provenance_fold_clause), so there is no read-then-write window and no lost update on the owner set. On delete or incremental update, execute_source_ref_removal splits matched artifacts into two groups. Unowned artifacts (no ref left after removal, _is_unowned) are hard-deleted. Surviving artifacts only have the targeted refs detached. Order: delete vectors of unowned artifacts, then remove refs from all matched artifacts (idempotent), then delete unowned nodes and edges. Shared EdgeType vectors are garbage-collected separately, only when truly orphaned. Each step is idempotent, so a retry converges. source_run_refs record which pipeline run added which ref, so one run's contributions can be rolled back.
mechanisms.evidence: cognee/infrastructure/databases/provenance/source_refs.py (make_source_ref_key, make_chunk_source_ref_key, make_source_run_ref, parse_source_ref_key); cognee/infrastructure/databases/unified/provenance_delete_planner.py (execute_source_ref_removal, _is_unowned, _cleanup_orphaned_edge_types, _cleanup_orphaned_nodeset_tags); cognee/infrastructure/databases/graph/ladybug/adapter.py lines ~84-110 (_provenance_fold_clause), lines ~1042 and ~1136 (MERGE); cognee/infrastructure/databases/provenance/source_ref_state.py (provenance_after_attach/remove, derive_run_ids)
mechanisms.limitations: Support is a flat set of extraction sources (an OR over documents and chunks), not an AND/OR justification. Nodes are deleted, never marked FALSE or PENDING. Nothing propagates to derived artifacts beyond the owner set itself, e.g. an entity summary built from a deleted entity is not touched. Owner sets are stored as delimiter-token strings in graph columns.
mechanisms.why: This is support counting at production scale over an OR-only justification. It validates ContextDB's support-count idea and its idempotent, vectors-first delete ordering across graph and vector stores. ContextDB would generalize the owner set to AND/OR justifications and flip status rather than delete.

mechanisms.name: Transitive session-cache invalidation to a fixpoint on data deletion
mechanisms.how_it_works: Each cached Q&A turn records used_graph_element_ids {node_ids, edge_ids} returned by recall, plus used_session_context_ids (the distilled lessons it consumed). Feedback entries record referenced_qa_ids, and lessons record source_feedback_ids. After a delete, SourceRefRemovalResult.deleted_node_ids and deleted_edges are passed to invalidate_sessions_for_deleted_data. A turn is contaminated if its used ids intersect the deleted ids. The function then iterates to a fixpoint along turn -> feedback -> lesson -> later turns that consumed the lesson, and deletes every contaminated entry. A dataset-level delete drops every session attributed to that dataset. A persist watermark is clamped under session_lock afterwards. The whole step is best-effort and fails open.
mechanisms.evidence: cognee/modules/session_lifecycle/invalidate_sessions.py (invalidate_sessions_for_dataset, invalidate_sessions_for_deleted_data, _invalidate_session_entries while-changed loop); cognee/infrastructure/session/session_manager.py:148-191 (used_graph_element_ids stored per QA); cognee/infrastructure/databases/unified/provenance_delete_planner.py (SourceRefRemovalResult docstring: 'Consumed by session invalidation'); cognee/tasks/ingestion/purge_stale_dlt_source_artifacts.py (also invalidates sessions)
mechanisms.limitations: Triggers only on hard delete, not on update or supersession. It deletes entries instead of marking them stale. There are no typed dependencies: every edge is effectively 'Cur'. It is best-effort with fail-open lookups. Agent-trace entries carry no element ids and are never matched (documented limit). It scans sessions linearly.
mechanisms.why: This is the closest thing in cognee to ContextDB's flip propagation: record which items a read used, then invalidate dependents transitively. It shows the 'certified read records used ids' pattern is what real systems need, since COG-5835 was completions quoting deleted facts. ContextDB should keep the read-set recording and make propagation precise (mark PENDING or STALE, use typed deps) instead of deleting.

mechanisms.name: Append-only, hash-chained PROV-O provenance ledger with archive-relabel versioning and tombstone invalidation
mechanisms.how_it_works: provenance_entries table, PK entity_id. On re-track, the live row is updated in place and the old snapshot is inserted under the archive id '{entity_id}:v:{last_updated}' (find_free_archive_id). previous_version_id links the chain, so revision_history walks it back with cycle guards. Each entry gets a global sequence_id plus previous_checksum plus checksum (integrity.compute_checksum over the canonical id), giving a tamper-evident chain that verify_chain checks in streaming fashion. invalidate() archives the pre-state, then writes a tombstone: invalidated=True, invalidated_at_time, invalidated_by, invalidation_reason. Fields also cover lineage (parent_entity_id, used_entities, derived_from_id, supersedes, revision_type, valid_from/valid_until, bundle_id, acted_on_behalf_of). get_lineage and trace_lineage walk upstream. check() reports dangling references. ProvenanceBatch commits many writes as one chained transaction. Every key is prefixed with the dataset id for tenant isolation.
mechanisms.evidence: cognee/modules/provenance/manager.py (ProvenanceManager._entity_write, track_entity, track_relationship, track_chunk, invalidate, revision_history, verify_chain, check, ProvenanceBatch.commit); cognee/modules/provenance/models/ProvenanceEntry.py and ProvenanceEntryRow.py; cognee/modules/provenance/integrity.py; cognee/tasks/provenance/record_provenance.py (opt-in cognify task, PROVENANCE_TRACKING env, default off); alembic/versions/b8c1d3e5f7a9_add_provenance_entries_table.py
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented (ported from 'semantica'), but opt-in and off by default. ProvenanceManager.invalidate has no production caller outside tests. supersedes and valid_until are stored, but nothing reads them to change retrieval. The ledger is audit-only and is not consulted by recall.
mechanisms.limitations: The 'immutable revision' is really a mutable live row plus archived copies, with no logical head or CAS. Invalidation does not propagate to entities that list the invalidated one in used_entities or derived_from_id. The ledger is disconnected from the graph that recall reads. A single global sequence chain serializes every writer.
mechanisms.why: The field vocabulary (PROV-O: used_entities, derived_from, supersedes, invalidated_by and reason) and the hash-chain integrity are a good audit-log design to copy. ContextDB would make revisions truly immutable with a CAS head pointer and wire the dependency fields into propagation.

mechanisms.name: LLM-reviewed fact conflicts with current/superseded/conflicting marks that steer retrieval
mechanisms.how_it_works: memify task review_conflicts: an LLM is shown each entity's competing facts, using labels only. validate_review_output rejects labels the call did not render and checks dates: a superseded fact dated after the current one is rejected. The model returns, per attribute, which facts are current, superseded or conflicting (schema.ReviewedConflict). A FactConflict DataPoint is written with id uuid5(dataset_id, about_id, attribute), and conflict_marks are stamped onto fact edges. A review_pending marker is set first and cleared last, so a crash leaves a repairable marker. At read time, fact_status() applies the precedence conflicting > superseded > current. Hybrid retrieval sorts superseded edges below current ones, and status_label annotates edges for the LLM as '[superseded; as of DATE]'.
mechanisms.evidence: cognee/tasks/memify/review_conflicts/{schema.py, review_facts.py, validate_review.py, write_conflicts.py (STATUS_PRIORITY, _write_reviewed_batch, PendingConflict)}; cognee/modules/engine/models/FactConflict.py; cognee/modules/graph/utils/fact_conflicts.py (fact_status, STATUS_PRECEDENCE, status_label); cognee/modules/retrieval/hybrid/entities.py ~300-400 (selected.sort by superseded)
mechanisms.limitations: Supersession is a semantic LLM judgement made in a batch job, not a structural revision relation. Superseded facts are only down-ranked and labelled, never excluded or certified. There are no dependents to re-check.
mechanisms.why: It matches ContextDB's split between structural and semantic validity: LLM judgement belongs on the semantic axis and should produce PENDING or advisory labels, not structural truth. Write-marker-first then clear-last is a good crash-safety idiom for asynchronous semantic validators.

mechanisms.name: Propose -> review -> apply gate with apply-time re-validation (text-to-SQL write-back)
mechanisms.how_it_works: An LLM drafts an UPDATE. It is validated: single UPDATE, mandatory WHERE, table allowlist (write_guard.validate_update). It is dry-run in a rolled-back transaction to capture estimated_rows, then stored as a ToolWriteProposal with status 'proposed'. apply_write_proposal re-checks the config and connection gates, executes in a transaction, and rolls back with status 'failed' if rowcount exceeds the cap or differs from the dry-run estimate ('the data changed since review'). Rejected proposals can never be applied.
mechanisms.evidence: cognee/modules/tools/text_to_sql/write_proposals.py (_check_write_gates, apply_write_proposal ~251-330, reject_write_proposal); cognee/modules/tools/models/ToolWriteProposal.py
mechanisms.limitations: The staleness check is a weak proxy (rowcount equality), not a read-set or version certificate. The status check and the commit are not atomic: there is no SELECT FOR UPDATE or conditional UPDATE, so two concurrent applies could both execute. It covers external SQL writes only, not agent actions in general.
mechanisms.why: This is real precedent for action-time validation. ContextDB's certificate validation is the principled version: replace 'same rowcount' with 'every head or revision in the read-set is unchanged and valid', and make the status transition a CAS.

mechanisms.name: Skill-improvement proposals (reviewable before/after, apply via remember)
mechanisms.how_it_works: improve_skill builds a SkillImprovementProposal DataPoint (old_procedure, proposed_procedure, runs_used, confidence, rationale, status='proposed'). GET /api/v1/proposals shows it for review. _apply_proposal overwrites skill.procedure and sets status='applied' through add_data_points.
mechanisms.evidence: cognee/modules/memify/skill_improvement.py (improve_skill ~85-160, _apply_proposal 187-220); cognee/modules/engine/models/SkillImprovementProposal.py; cognee/api/v1/proposals/routers/get_proposals_router.py
mechanisms.limitations: No CAS. _apply_proposal never checks that skill.procedure still equals proposal.old_procedure, and never checks that status is still 'proposed'. A stale proposal silently overwrites concurrent edits, and a proposal can be applied twice.
mechanisms.why: A clear counter-example: storing old_procedure without comparing it on apply gives the look of review with no conflict detection. ContextDB should make 'expected base revision' mandatory on apply.

mechanisms.name: Concurrency control: per-dataset asyncio locks, idempotent MERGE, ledger advisory lock
mechanisms.how_it_works: dataset_lock(dataset_id) serializes add/cognify/memify/delete per dataset. It is re-entrant through a ContextVar (held_datasets) and enforces a lock-before-queue-slot order to prevent a deadlock seen in production (SDK-483). The session locks are session_lock(session_id, op), session_turn_lock, and try_acquire_improve_lock_many. The provenance ledger uses a per-event-loop asyncio.Lock, a Postgres pg_advisory_xact_lock, and a unique index on sequence_id with bounded retry as the backstop. Graph writes are MERGE upserts keyed on deterministic ids (last writer wins on properties; owner-set stamping is atomic). Incremental update stages new content and publishes in one relational transaction. If the process crashes, the stored chunks no longer tile the text and the next touch fails closed into a full rebuild. Pipeline run recovery uses a filelock ownership marker.
mechanisms.evidence: cognee/infrastructure/locks/dataset_lock.py (dataset_lock, get_dataset_lock, _check_lock_slot_order); cognee/infrastructure/locks/session_lock.py; cognee/modules/provenance/storage.py 1-115 (_get_chain_lock, _acquire_chain_write_lock, append_chained_many); cognee/api/v1/update/incremental.py docstring + _write_and_publish; cognee/modules/pipelines/run_ownership.py
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented; dataset_lock docstring says outright 'process-local only ... does NOT protect against multiple processes'
mechanisms.limitations: No optimistic concurrency, version vectors or CAS on memory items. DataPoint.version/update_version() exists but nothing outside tests calls update_version, so version is effectively always 1. Two agents in different processes writing the same dataset rely on idempotent MERGE with last-writer-wins.
mechanisms.why: Validates two needs: owner-set updates must be atomic, and real deployments hit cross-process races. ContextDB's CAS logical heads fill the gap cognee admits to. The fail-closed self-heal pattern (an invariant check that forces a rebuild) is worth adopting.

mechanisms.name: Dataset-scoped ACLs plus agent-scoped default datasets
mechanisms.how_it_works: Sharing happens at dataset granularity. The ACL table holds (principal, permission, dataset) with permissions read/write/delete/share. Tenant capabilities (manage_users, grant/revoke) live in principal_capabilities. The MCP server derives a default dataset per client from clientInfo.name ('<client>_memory'), so agents are isolated by default and share by naming a common dataset. @agent_memory resolves the user and dataset scope and registers an AgentConnection in an in-process registry. Graph and vector databases can be one per dataset (DatasetDatabase handlers).
mechanisms.evidence: cognee/modules/users/models/ACL.py; cognee/modules/users/permissions/permission_types.py; cognee-mcp/src/server.py _agent_scoped_default_dataset (~1031-1055); cognee/modules/agents/registry.py; cognee/modules/agent_memory/runtime.py (resolve_agent_dataset_scope)
mechanisms.limitations: No item-level consistency model, no subscriptions or notifications to other agents when shared memory changes, and no read certificates. The agent registry is process-local.
mechanisms.why: Dataset-as-namespace with read/write/delete/share ACLs is a proven, simple sharing unit. ContextDB can use it as its scope or namespace layer and put heads, deps and certificates underneath.

mechanisms.name: Small verb-oriented MCP surface (remember/recall/forget/improve/status)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Six MCP tools. remember stores permanent memory (add, cognify, improve) or session memory when session_id is given. It accepts text or base64 files, optionally runs in the background, and reports via cognify_status. recall searches. forget deletes by data_id, dataset or everything. improve runs memify enrichment. code_search queries the code graph. Each tool wraps stdout redirect and returns TextContent errors instead of raising.
mechanisms.evidence: cognee-mcp/src/server.py lines 357 (remember), 542 (recall), 666 (code_search), 737 (forget), 814 (improve), 917 (cognify_status); cognee-mcp/src/tool_registry.py; cognee-mcp/src/cognee_client.py (direct vs API mode)
mechanisms.limitations: Recall returns no version or certificate. There are no conditional writes, no tool to check validity before an action, and no tool to watch for invalidations.
mechanisms.why: This verb set is what popular agent integrations expect. ContextDB can offer the same verbs and add certificate-bearing recall plus a validate_certificate or act-gate tool.

mechanisms.name: Hybrid graph and vector recall with feedback and importance weights
mechanisms.how_it_works: Vector search over per-field collections seeds a graph triplet search (brute_force_triplet_search). Edges are ranked, deduplicated and annotated with conflict status. Session context blocks (preferences, lessons) are packed alongside. Feedback on answers changes node feedback_weight through memify (apply_feedback_weights uses used_graph_element_ids).
mechanisms.evidence: cognee/modules/retrieval/utils/brute_force_triplet_search.py; cognee/modules/retrieval/hybrid/entities.py; cognee/infrastructure/session/session_context_builder.py; cognee/tasks/memify/apply_feedback_weights.py
mechanisms.limitations: Ranking is heuristic. Packed context carries no validity guarantee.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB's differentiator is validity-certified context, not ranking. Ranking could be borrowed later.

mechanisms.name: Three-store architecture (graph + vector + relational) with idempotent ordered cross-store deletes
mechanisms.how_it_works: Pluggable adapters behind graph_db_interface and vector_db_interface. The relational DB is the source of truth for users, datasets, Data rows, runs and the provenance ledger. Cross-store consistency comes from idempotent steps, a strict order (vectors first, then graph), and fail-closed invariant checks, not distributed transactions.
mechanisms.evidence: cognee/infrastructure/databases/graph/graph_db_interface.py; cognee/infrastructure/databases/vector/vector_db_interface.py; cognee/infrastructure/databases/unified/unified_store_engine.py; provenance_delete_planner.py docstring
mechanisms.limitations: No atomic cross-store commit. A crash between stores relies on a retry or a rebuild.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB's revision, head and dependency core needs one transactional store (e.g. SQLite or Postgres). Vectors should be a derived, rebuildable index rather than a co-equal store.

analysis.overlap_with_contextdb:
Overlap is partial and mostly in deletion paths.
(a) Dependency-driven transitive invalidation exists in exactly one place. modules/session_lifecycle/invalidate_sessions.py records the graph elements a session Q&A used, then on document deletion purges contaminated turns and follows turn -> feedback -> lesson -> later-turn edges to a fixpoint. Limits: it fires only on hard delete, deletes rather than marking stale, has no typed dependencies, and does not cover graph-to-graph derivations.
(b) Support counting exists only as OR-only owner sets (source_ref_keys refcounts in provenance_delete_planner.execute_source_ref_removal). There are no AND/OR justifications and no TRUE/FALSE/PENDING status. The provenance ledger's invalidate() writes a tombstone but propagates nothing, and production code never calls it.
(c) Alternatives and supersession: LLM-judged current/superseded/conflicting marks on fact edges only down-rank retrieval. There are no immutable revisions with logical heads. DataPoint.version is unused, and graph writes are MERGE with last-writer-wins.
(d) Action gating: text-to-SQL write proposals re-validate at apply time, using rowcount equality as a staleness proxy and a non-atomic status check. Skill proposals have no base-revision check at all. There is no certified context read and no general action-time certificate validation.
(e) Concurrency: process-local asyncio dataset locks, documented as not cross-process. No CAS anywhere on memory items.
analysis.could_contextdb_be_built_as_plugin_on_it:
Not as a faithful plugin. ContextDB's core guarantees need things cognee lacks at its foundation: immutable revisions with CAS heads, a transactional dependency DAG, flip-only propagation, and certificates checked at action time. Cognee's write path is idempotent MERGE with last-writer-wins across three loosely coordinated stores, plus process-local locks. Bolting CAS and a justification DAG on top would mean wrapping or replacing add_data_points, the delete planner and the recall path, which amounts to a fork. Practical options:
(1) Run ContextDB as the transactional source of truth for agent-shared context and decisions, and use cognee (Apache-2.0) as an optional extraction and recall backend through a custom pipeline task. Cognee's source_ref_keys and used_graph_element_ids would map onto ContextDB Ref/Cur dependencies.
(2) Expose an MCP surface that mirrors cognee's verbs (remember, recall, forget, improve) so agents can switch over. Add certified recall plus a validate-before-act tool.
(3) Port three ideas directly: refcounted owner sets with vectors-first idempotent deletes, read-set recording plus fixpoint propagation (turned into PENDING/STALE marking instead of deletion), and the PROV-O, hash-chained audit-ledger schema.

verification.overlap_verdict: Confirmed, with small corrections. (a) The fixpoint session invalidation is real. It fires on document and dataset deletes (datasets.py, forget, DLT purge) and not on incremental update or supersession, and it deletes rather than marking stale. (b) Support counting is OR-only owner sets (source_ref:v1 and source_ref:v2 keys), refcounted in execute_source_ref_removal. There is no AND/OR justification and no TRUE/FALSE/PENDING status. ProvenanceManager.invalidate() writes a tombstone, propagates nothing, and has no production caller. (c) Supersession is only LLM-judged current/superseded/conflicting marks that down-rank or label edges; when dates disagree, all facts become 'conflicting' rather than the review being rejected. There are no immutable revisions or logical heads. DataPoint.update_version has no non-test caller, and graph writes are MERGE with last-writer-wins on properties, while the provenance stamp is atomic in Kuzu. (d) The text-to-SQL apply uses rowcount equality, re-checks gates but not the SQL guard, and does a non-atomic status read and write. Skill _apply_proposal checks neither old_procedure nor status. There are no certified reads or certificate validation. (e) Dataset locks are process-local asyncio locks, documented as such; only the provenance ledger has cross-process serialization (pg advisory lock). No CAS on memory items. One addition: overlap with ContextDB's 'record read set at read time' idea is stronger than (a) alone suggests. session_manager stores used_graph_element_ids and used_session_context_ids for every QA turn, which is a de facto read-set record, although nothing validates against it before an action.

analysis.one_line_summary: A Python temporal knowledge graph library plus MCP server. LLMs pull entity/fact edges out of "episodes". Each fact edge has bi-temporal fields (valid_at/invalid_at for event time, created_at/expired_at for system time). When an LLM judges that a new fact contradicts an old one, the old edge is closed off by setting its timestamps rather than deleted. There are no dependency DAG, CAS, alternatives or action gating.
analysis.architecture:
Language: Python, asyncio, pydantic models.

Storage: a pluggable GraphDriver (graphiti_core/driver/: neo4j_driver.py, falkordb_driver.py, kuzu_driver.py, neptune_driver.py, plus an optional graph_operations_interface). Graph data model, from graphiti_core/nodes.py and graphiti_core/edges.py:
- EpisodicNode: raw ingested content, with valid_at = reference time and created_at = ingest time.
- EntityNode: name, summary, name_embedding, attributes.
- EntityEdge (RELATES_TO): fact text, fact_embedding, episodes[] (provenance list), valid_at, invalid_at, created_at, expired_at, reference_time, attributes.
- EpisodicEdge (MENTIONS, from an episode to an entity), CommunityNode/Edge, SagaNode (ordered episode chains with NEXT_EPISODE / HAS_EPISODE).

Tenancy and partitioning: group_id on every element. On Neo4j/Falkor a group_id can map to a separate database via Graphiti._resolve_request_scope, which clones the driver per request (graphiti.py ~1304-1332).

Process model: an in-process library. Graphiti.add_episode (graphiti.py:1334) runs: retrieve previous episodes, LLM node extraction, node dedup, LLM edge extraction, edge dedup and contradiction (resolve_extracted_edges), attribute and summary extraction, then one bulk write transaction (add_nodes_and_edges_bulk in utils/bulk_utils.py:128 uses session.execute_write).

Writes: MERGE by uuid followed by `SET r = edge`, a whole-property overwrite (models/edges/edge_db_queries.py get_entity_edge_save_bulk_query).

Retrieval: hybrid BM25 + vector + BFS with RRF, MMR or cross-encoder rerank (search/search.py, search_utils.py, search_config_recipes.py). SearchFilters can filter on valid_at, invalid_at, created_at and expired_at, including IS NULL (search/search_filters.py).

API surface:
- Python SDK: Graphiti.add_episode, add_episode_bulk, add_triplet, search, search_, remove_episode, build_communities, summarize_saga, retrieve_episodes.
- MCP server (mcp_server/src/graphiti_mcp_server.py) tools: add_memory, search_nodes, search_memory_facts, delete_entity_edge, delete_episode, get_entity_edge, get_episodes, summarize_saga, build_communities, add_triplet, get_episode_entities, clear_graph, get_status.
- FastAPI REST server (server/graph_service/routers/ingest.py, retrieve.py): POST /messages, POST /entity-node, DELETE /entity-edge/{uuid}, DELETE /group/{id}, DELETE /episode/{uuid}, POST /clear, POST /search, GET /entity-edge/{uuid}, GET /episodes/{group_id}, POST /get-memory.

mechanisms.name: Bi-temporal fact edges (event time and system time)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Every EntityEdge carries four timestamps. valid_at and invalid_at say when the fact was true in the world, as extracted by the LLM or set from the episode's reference_time. created_at and expired_at say when the system learned or retired it. A superseded fact is never deleted or rewritten into a new revision. The old edge's invalid_at is set to the new edge's valid_at, and its expired_at is set to now. History stays queryable through date filters. There is no revision chain and no head pointer: the 'current' fact is simply whichever edge has expired_at IS NULL (and invalid_at IS NULL).
mechanisms.evidence: graphiti_core/edges.py class EntityEdge (fields at ~lines 267-287: episodes, expired_at, valid_at, invalid_at, reference_time); graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/edge_operations.py resolve_edge_contradictions (lines 748-783)
mechanisms.limitations: Supersession is a timestamp mutation on the old record, not an immutable revision. Updates use SET r = edge, so the earlier state of the edge is lost. The edge does not record which new edge invalidated it; see the invalidated_by mechanism. Nothing links 'A was replaced by B'.
mechanisms.why: Splitting world-validity time from system knowledge time is cheap and proven. ContextDB revisions could carry valid_from/valid_to (event time) next to the commit sequence (system time). ContextDB should keep immutable revisions and explicit supersedes pointers instead of mutating the old record in place.

mechanisms.name: LLM contradiction detection, then a temporal invalidation rule
mechanisms.how_it_works:
Step 1, candidates. For each newly extracted edge there are two hybrid (RRF) searches. related_edges are edges between the same endpoint pair (_pair_search_filter / _same_pair_edges). invalidation candidates come from a group-wide semantic search on the fact text with an empty SearchFilters.

Step 2, LLM judgment. One LLM call (prompt dedupe_edges.resolve_edge) returns duplicate_facts (indexes into related_edges) and contradicted_facts (indexes across both lists). The indexes are range-checked in _dedupe_extracted_edge.

Step 3, deterministic temporal rule in _apply_temporal_invalidation:
- If the new edge already has invalid_at, it is expired immediately.
- If a contradicting candidate has a later valid_at, the NEW edge is the stale one: its invalid_at is set to candidate.valid_at and it is expired.
- Otherwise resolve_edge_contradictions skips candidates whose intervals do not overlap. For an overlapping candidate with an earlier valid_at, it sets candidate.invalid_at = new.valid_at and candidate.expired_at = now.

The invalidated edges are re-embedded and saved in the same bulk transaction as the episode.
mechanisms.evidence: graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/edge_operations.py resolve_extracted_edges (424-646, candidate searches at ~520-585), _dedupe_extracted_edge (864-1089), _apply_temporal_invalidation (715-745), resolve_edge_contradictions (748-783); graphiti_core/prompts/dedupe_edges.py (contradicted_facts field, lines ~30-90); graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/temporal_edge_utils.py normalize_future_temporal_bounds (regex heuristics so planned or deadline facts don't get a future valid_at or a spurious invalid_at)
mechanisms.limitations: Invalidation reaches exactly one level: a contradicted fact is expired, and nothing derived from it is touched. Node summaries and community summaries that quoted the fact are not recomputed, and there is no dependency graph to propagate through. The result depends on the LLM and is not deterministic. Candidate recall depends on search top-k. A case the LLM is unsure about is not marked PENDING; it is either contradicted or not. There is no contradiction check for edges with no related or existing candidates. A contradiction against a later-dated candidate expires the new edge silently.
mechanisms.why: This maps onto ContextDB's semantic validity (Sem dependencies). An LLM or semantic checker proposes conflicts, and a deterministic rule decides the outcome. ContextDB should route uncertain verdicts to PENDING rather than FALSE, and must add the transitive propagation that Graphiti lacks. The interval-overlap rule (skip non-overlapping intervals, the later valid_at wins) is a reusable, implementable tiebreak.

mechanisms.name: Episode provenance list on edges (a crude support set)
mechanisms.how_it_works:
EntityEdge.episodes is a list of the uuids of every episode that asserted the fact. When a duplicate is found, append_episode_provenance adds the new episode's uuid to the existing edge rather than creating a new one. EpisodicNode.entity_edges and MENTIONS edges link episodes to the things they produced. remove_episode works like support counting:
- The episode's uuid is removed from each edge's episodes list. An edge whose list becomes empty is deleted; otherwise it is kept and re-saved.
- An entity node mentioned only by this episode is deleted.
- Each surviving node's summary is rebuilt by the LLM from the remaining episodes.
mechanisms.evidence: graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/edge_operations.py _dedupe_extracted_edge -> append_episode_provenance (~905-908); graphiti_core/graphiti.py remove_episode (2174-2251)
mechanisms.limitations: This is OR-support over source episodes only, with no AND-justifications and no derived-from-fact dependencies. Removing an episode does NOT restore edges that its facts had invalidated, because the invalidation is never recorded (see next mechanism). Retraction is a manual delete, not a truth-maintenance flip, and there is no propagation beyond one hop of rebuilt summaries.
mechanisms.why: It is a working instance of 'keep the fact while support > 0', which supports ContextDB's support-counting design (OR over episodes). ContextDB should generalize it to AND/OR justifications and flip-only propagation, and should make un-invalidation possible.

mechanisms.name: invalidated_by map (computed in memory, never persisted)
mechanisms.how_it_works: resolve_extracted_edges accepts an optional dict invalidated_by. If the dict is given, it is filled with {invalidated_edge_uuid: [invalidating_edge_uuids]}. No production caller in graphiti_core, server or mcp_server passes the dict, and nothing stores it on the edge or in the graph.
mechanisms.evidence: graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/edge_operations.py lines 433, 441-442, 636-638; grep over graphiti_core, server and mcp_server finds no other references
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: partially (hook exists, not persisted or used)
mechanisms.limitations: Because the invalidation reason is lost, deleting the invalidating episode cannot reinstate the old fact.
mechanisms.why: It shows the gap ContextDB must close. 'Invalidated by X' should be a first-class, persisted justification edge, so that retracting X flips the old fact back.

mechanisms.name: group_id namespaces plus per-group sequential ingestion queue
mechanisms.how_it_works: Every node and edge carries a group_id, and searches take group_ids, enforced by the @handle_multiple_group_ids decorator. Graphiti._resolve_request_scope can route each group_id to its own database through a driver clone per request, avoiding the races of a shared mutable driver. In the MCP server, QueueService keeps one asyncio.Queue and one worker per group_id, so add_memory calls in the same group run one after another. add_memory returns immediately and processes in the background.
mechanisms.evidence: graphiti_core/graphiti.py _resolve_request_scope (~1304-1332); graphiti_core/decorators.py handle_multiple_group_ids; mcp_server/src/services/queue_service.py QueueService.add_episode_task / _process_episode_queue; mcp_server/src/graphiti_mcp_server.py add_memory docstring ('Episodes for the same group_id are processed sequentially to avoid race conditions')
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented (MCP server only; the core library has no such serialization)
mechanisms.limitations: Serialization lives inside one process, held in memory; two MCP server processes or direct SDK users can race. There are no agent identities, ACLs, or reader-sees-version semantics. add_memory is asynchronous and fire-and-forget, so a caller cannot read its own write or learn which facts it invalidated.
mechanisms.why: A single-writer queue per namespace is a simple, proven way to avoid LLM-dedupe races. ContextDB needs it to be durable and to work across processes, which means CAS on heads, and add_memory should return the commit and certificate ids synchronously.

mechanisms.name: Bulk write transaction; last-writer-wins MERGE/SET
mechanisms.how_it_works: All nodes and edges an episode produced or invalidated are written in one driver write transaction (session.execute_write(add_nodes_and_edges_bulk_tx)). Each edge is saved with MERGE (source)-[r:RELATES_TO {uuid}]->(target) SET r = edge, which overwrites every property.
mechanisms.evidence: graphiti_core/utils/bulk_utils.py add_nodes_and_edges_bulk (128-148), add_nodes_and_edges_bulk_tx (151+); graphiti_core/models/edges/edge_db_queries.py get_entity_edge_save_bulk_query
mechanisms.limitations: There is no version column, no compare-and-swap, no read-set validation and no conflict detection. The LLM pipeline runs for a long time on reads made before the transaction, so two concurrent episodes can each dedupe or invalidate against a stale view and overwrite each other, for example losing an appended episodes[] entry. The design assumes the per-group queue.
mechanisms.why: This is exactly the lost-update hazard that ContextDB's CAS on logical heads and certified reads are meant to prevent. Batching a whole episode into one atomic commit is worth keeping; the blind SET overwrite is not.

mechanisms.name: Hybrid search with temporal filters
mechanisms.how_it_works: BM25 fulltext + cosine vector + BFS, fused with RRF, MMR, node-distance or cross-encoder rerank, according to SearchConfig recipes. SearchFilters builds Cypher predicates on valid_at, invalid_at, created_at and expired_at, using OR-of-AND DateFilter lists with operators that include IS NULL, plus edge_types, edge_uuids, endpoint uuids and property_filters. The MCP search_memory_facts exposes edge-type and date-range filters.
mechanisms.evidence: graphiti_core/search/search.py, search_utils.py, search_config_recipes.py (EDGE_HYBRID_SEARCH_RRF), search_filters.py (SearchFilters, ComparisonOperator, edge_search_filter_query_constructor); mcp_server/src/graphiti_mcp_server.py search_memory_facts (616+)
mechanisms.limitations: Expired or invalidated edges are NOT excluded by default; no 'expired_at IS NULL' predicate is applied automatically, so callers must filter. Results carry no certificate or version stamp, and retrieval does not record what was read.
mechanisms.why: Hybrid retrieval plus as-of temporal filters is a good packing layer for ContextDB. ContextDB should default to valid heads only and should emit a read certificate (the revision ids read) with each context pack.

mechanisms.name: Action gating
mechanisms.how_it_works: Does not exist. Nothing validates a read set or certificate before an agent acts, there are no pre-action hooks, and there are no staleness checks at use time.
mechanisms.evidence: No such code in graphiti_core, mcp_server/src or server/graph_service (searched the tool list and the pipeline)
mechanisms.limitations: N/A
mechanisms.why: ContextDB's certificate validation at action time is novel relative to Graphiti.

mechanisms.name: MCP memory tool surface
mechanisms.how_it_works:
FastMCP tools:
- add_memory(name, episode_body, group_id, source=text|json|message, reference_time, saga, previous_episode_uuids, ...) queues the episode.
- search_nodes and search_memory_facts (group_ids, center_node_uuid, edge_types, date filters).
- get_entity_edge, get_episodes, get_episode_entities.
- delete_entity_edge, delete_episode, clear_graph.
- add_triplet (inserts a structured fact directly; it still runs dedup and contradiction).
- build_communities, summarize_saga, get_status.
There is also a REST server with similar operations.
mechanisms.evidence: mcp_server/src/graphiti_mcp_server.py (@mcp.tool at lines 402-1146); mcp_server/src/services/queue_service.py; server/graph_service/routers/ingest.py and retrieve.py
mechanisms.limitations: Writes are asynchronous and their outcome is opaque: no invalidation report and no commit id. There are no tools for CAS, subscriptions or watching for changes, or certificates.
mechanisms.why: It is a proven, minimal MCP vocabulary that coding agents already use (add_memory / search_memory_facts / get_episodes). ContextDB can keep familiar tool names while adding commit/CAS/certificate parameters.

mechanisms.name: Pluggable graph-DB drivers
mechanisms.how_it_works: An abstract GraphDriver with Neo4j, FalkorDB, Kuzu (embedded) and Neptune implementations. Cypher queries vary by provider (models/*/db_queries.py), and an optional graph_operations_interface overrides bulk saves. build_indices_and_constraints creates the fulltext and vector indexes.
mechanisms.evidence: graphiti_core/driver/driver.py, neo4j_driver.py, falkordb_driver.py, kuzu_driver.py, neptune_driver.py; graphiti_core/models/edges/edge_db_queries.py; graphiti.py build_indices_and_constraints (~805)
mechanisms.limitations: An external graph database is required (Kuzu is the embedded option). There is no append-only log and no immutable storage.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB's spec favors an append-only, revision-based store; a graph DB backend is optional.

analysis.overlap_with_contextdb:
Graphiti covers part of what ContextDB plans.

What it has:
1. Supersession through bi-temporal timestamps. Old fact edges get invalid_at and expired_at; they are not deleted.
2. Semantic invalidation proposed by an LLM: the contradicted_facts output, applied by a deterministic interval rule (edge_operations._apply_temporal_invalidation / resolve_edge_contradictions).
3. OR-style source support counting: EntityEdge.episodes, used by remove_episode to delete a fact only when no supporting episode is left.

What it does not have:
- Dependency-driven transitive invalidation. Invalidation is one hop, from a new fact to the facts it contradicts. Summaries and communities derived from an invalidated fact are not invalidated (summaries are rebuilt only when an episode is removed).
- Typed dependencies (Pin/Cur/Sem/Ref) and AND-justifications.
- A persisted invalidated-by link. The invalidated_by map is computed only on request and never stored, so retracting the invalidator cannot restore the old fact.
- Alternatives or multiple competing heads. Contradiction always resolves to the later valid_at.
- A PENDING state. The LLM verdict is binary.
- Immutable revisions and logical heads. Edges are mutated in place with MERGE/SET.
- CAS or conflict detection. The only protection is a per-group in-process asyncio queue in the MCP server.
- Certified reads and action-time gating.
analysis.could_contextdb_be_built_as_plugin_on_it:
Not as a plugin in any meaningful way. Graphiti has no hook points in its write pipeline for custom validity logic. The contradiction step is hard-coded inside resolve_extracted_edges. Storage is last-writer-wins MERGE/SET with no versions, so CAS, immutable revisions and certificates would mean replacing the persistence layer and add_episode itself.

What is realistic:
(a) Use Graphiti as an upstream extractor and retriever. Feed its extracted facts, plus its contradicted_facts verdicts treated as Sem-dependency PENDING signals, into ContextDB's own revision store and justification DAG.
(b) Reuse specific pieces: the bi-temporal fields, the interval-overlap supersession rule, the dedupe_edges prompt design, hybrid search with date filters, and the MCP tool vocabulary.

A fork would need persisted justification edges, a version and head layer with CAS, and a certificate layer. That is most of ContextDB, so building ContextDB natively and borrowing these patterns is cleaner.

verification.overlap_verdict: Confirmed, with refinements. The three overlapping features exist as described: bi-temporal supersession by timestamps, LLM contradiction verdicts plus a deterministic interval rule, and OR support counting over episodes. Every listed absence also holds: no transitive invalidation, no typed dependencies or AND-justifications, no persisted invalidated-by link, no competing heads, no PENDING state, mutation in place with MERGE/SET instead of immutable revisions, no CAS (only the per-group in-process MCP queue), and no certified reads. Refinements: (a) 'Contradiction always resolves to the later valid_at' holds only when both edges have valid_at. If either is None, the contradiction is silently ignored and both facts stay current. (b) The exact-text fast path skips contradiction checking entirely. (c) The overlap on 'history stays queryable / current = expired_at IS NULL' is weaker than stated. Neither search nor the MCP tools filter expired edges by default, and MCP search_memory_facts cannot filter on expired_at at all, so agents using it get superseded facts mixed in with current ones. That makes ContextDB's 'default to valid heads plus read certificate' a real differentiator. (d) handle_multiple_group_ids is FalkorDB-only routing, not general namespace enforcement.

analysis.one_line_summary: A team memory hub for coding agents. An LLM-API proxy captures every agent turn and injects memory, an LLM pipeline distills chat into L0 raw turns, L1 atoms, L2 scenes and an L3 persona, and the hub adds versioned Skills, a Wiki and a CodeGraph behind owner/team/ACL visibility. Supersession is decided by an LLM (delete-then-insert). Skills get immutable versions with CAS. Nothing does dependency-driven invalidation or action gating.
analysis.architecture:
Language: TypeScript on Node >=22. There are also Python and TS SDKs (sdk/memory-core) and a Python Hermes plugin. The system runs as four processes:
(1) MemoryCore: the HTTP gateway (src/gateway/server.ts, v2-router.ts, skill-handlers.ts) plus the extraction pipeline (src/utils/pipeline-manager.ts, pipeline-factory.ts, src/services/pipeline-worker.ts) and the metadata service (users, teams, agents, assets, ACLs, in src/metadata/*).
(2) MemoryProxy: an Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible LLM API proxy. Agents (Claude Code, Codex, CodeBuddy and others) point their base URL at it. It parses each request and injects memory blocks through InjectionPipeline (src/injection/pipeline.ts). It records turns for extraction, gated by src/extraction-gate.ts. It brokers skill calls (src/skill/skill-bridge.ts) and pins skill versions per session.
(3) MemoryKnowledge: the Wiki and CodeGraph service, plus the project's only MCP server (src/mcp/server.ts, tools.ts). Its tools are code_search, code_explore, code_callers, code_callees, code_impact, code_node, code_status, code_files, wiki_search, wiki_read, wiki_list and wiki_graph. CodeGraph wraps the third-party @colbymchenry/codegraph (src/engines/code/bridge.ts).
(4) MemoryPanel: a human admin web UI and API.
Storage sits behind pluggable store interfaces (core/store/types.ts IMemoryStore, skill/skill-store.interface.ts ISkillStore, metadata/store/interface.ts). Backends are SQLite (sqlite-vec + FTS5), MongoDB, and Tencent Cloud VectorDB (TCVDB, which has native dense+sparse hybrid search). Blobs (skill resource dirs, JSONL shards, scene blocks, persona) live on COS object storage or the local fs through a StorageAdapter. Redis or COS-KV holds proxy session state and version pins.
Data model:
- L0: conversation messages.
- L1: atomic memories. Fields are record_id, content, type (persona/episodic/instruction/work_*), priority, scene_name, version, team/user/agent/session/task ids and metadata_json. They are dual-written to append-only daily JSONL (records/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl) and to the vector/FTS store.
- L2: scene-block markdown files.
- L3: persona markdown. L2/L3 are also mirrored as ProfileRecord rows with a version.
- Skills: a single table with one row per (skill_id, version) plus an is_head flag.
- Metadata: AssetEntity rows (asset_type skill|llm_wiki|code_graph|chat_memory, visibility private|team|restricted|agent|task, status draft|candidate|approved|deprecated|archived|failed, version, usage_count, expires_at). Also AclEntity and FixedAssetBinding (agent -> asset, with injection_mode direct|summary|tool|reference).
API surface: REST v2/v3 (/v3/skill/{create,update,patch,delete,get,list,search,versions,files/*,extract,...}, /v3/chat-memory/*, /v3/meta/*, /v3/memory-generation-log/*). OpenClaw plugin tools tdai_memory_search and tdai_conversation_search (MemoryCore/index.ts:379-543). The MCP server covers only knowledge (Wiki/CodeGraph). Chat memory and skills reach agents through proxy injection and REST, not MCP.

mechanisms.name: Skill immutable version rows + head flag
mechanisms.how_it_works: Each (skill_id, version) is an immutable snapshot row (content, content_hash, manifest_json, storage_dir). appendVersion runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE, sets UPDATE is_head=0 on the old head, INSERTs the new row with version+1 and is_head=1, syncs FTS, then COMMITs. Resource files are copy-on-write: copyTree(oldVersionDir -> newVersionDir), then the write/remove mutations are applied to the new dir only. If content_hash and resources are unchanged, it returns the old head, so the write is idempotent. A partial unique index (team_id, owner_agent_id, name) WHERE is_head=1 AND status='active' prevents two live heads with the same name. Names cannot change across versions. Old non-head versions are pruned by TTL and by count, the newest 3 are always kept, and the head is never deleted (cleanupExpiredVersionsForSkill). Delete is a soft archive of the head (status=archived).
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryCore/src/core/skill/skill-versioning.ts (appendNextVersion ~L210-300, createNewSkill, deleteSkill, cleanupExpiredVersionsForSkill); MemoryCore/src/core/skill/skill-store-ddl.ts L20-60 (UNIQUE(skill_id,version), uniq_skills_team_agent_name_head); MemoryCore/src/core/store/sqlite/skill-store.ts appendVersion L272-330; mongodb/skill-store.ts appendVersion (insert new row then flip is_head; crash leaves newest resolvable by version DESC)
mechanisms.limitations: Versions are linear: no branches or alternatives and no parent pointer beyond version-1. Cross-system writes (COS + DB + meta_assets) have no real transaction. Consistency relies on ordering plus compensation, and orphans are self-healed on read (onSkillAccessed). Mongo does a two-step insert and then flips the head, which is not atomic. Pruning destroys history.
mechanisms.why: This closely matches ContextDB's immutable revisions plus logical head. The partial-unique-index-on-head trick, copy-on-write blob dirs and the content-hash no-op are cheap, proven details worth copying.

mechanisms.name: expected_version optimistic lock on skill writes
mechanisms.how_it_works: Every skill mutation (update, patch, files/write, files/remove) requires expected_version. SkillCore calls assertVersionFresh(head, expected), which throws SKILL_VERSION_STALE (HTTP 40901) if head.version != expected. As a backstop, UNIQUE(skill_id, version) rejects a concurrent insert of the same version number.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryCore/src/core/skill/skill-permission.ts assertVersionFresh L57-68; MemoryCore/src/core/skill/skill-core.ts L147-178 (input types), L316/341/405/426 (assertVersionFreshWrap calls)
mechanisms.limitations: The freshness check happens in application code before the transaction; getHead in SqliteSkillStore.appendVersion is read before BEGIN IMMEDIATE. So the CAS is check-then-act, and only the unique constraint stops lost updates. There is no merge or rebase on conflict: the client just gets the error. Delete is unconditional.
mechanisms.why: This is ContextDB's CAS on logical heads. ContextDB should do the compare inside the transaction (UPDATE ... WHERE head_rev=?) rather than copy the TOCTOU form.

mechanisms.name: Session-scoped lazy version pinning (snapshot reads + implicit CAS) in proxy
mechanisms.how_it_works: The proxy keeps a per-session hash in Redis or COS-KV, keyed skill:vpin:{user}:{agentSource}:{session}, that maps skill_id to a version. On the first successful read or search response, tryLazyPin records the version it saw. A Lua script does the HSETNX equivalent so the first pin wins atomically, and a TTL (default 30 min) is refreshed on each call. On later get or files/read calls, the proxy injects version=pinned, so the agent keeps reading the same snapshot even after another agent updates the head. On update, patch, files/write and files/remove, the proxy injects expected_version=pinned, so a write based on a stale snapshot fails with 40901. After a successful write, upsertVersion moves the pin to v+1.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryProxy/src/skill/version-pin-repo.ts (pinMany Lua, upsertVersion); MemoryProxy/src/skill/kv-version-pin-repo.ts; MemoryProxy/src/skill/skill-bridge.ts L178-193 (READ_VERSION_OPS/WRITE_LOCK_OPS), L865-881 (inject version/expected_version), L970-974 and tryLazyPin L1155-1230
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented (references docs/design/2026-06-29-skill-version-pinning.md, which is not in the repo)
mechanisms.limitations: Best effort: every error degrades silently to reading the head. It applies to skills only, not chat memory, wiki or code graph. Pins live only for the session TTL. The agent never learns that its pinned version is stale until a write fails, because there is no notification. Delete ignores pins.
mechanisms.why: This is a working, deployed form of ContextDB's Pin dependency and certified reads: read-your-snapshot plus write-guarded-by-snapshot, enforced transparently at a proxy layer. ContextDB can generalize it so a session's read set (pinned revisions) becomes the certificate checked at write/action time, and add push notification when a pin goes stale.

mechanisms.name: LLM-judged L1 memory dedup/supersession (store/update/merge/skip)
mechanisms.how_it_works: For each batch of newly extracted atoms: (1) candidate recall per atom via hybrid search (native hybrid, or FTS plus vector merged by RRF), top-K=5, scoped by the IsolationFilter. (2) One LLM call returns, for each atom, an action in {store, update, merge, skip} plus target_ids and merged_content/type/priority/timestamps. writeMemory then computes version = max(target.version)+1, deletes the targets from the vector store (deleteL1Batch), appends the new record to JSONL and upserts it into the vector store. The new record gets a new record_id. JSONL keeps the old lines until a periodic memory-cleaner reconciles them.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryCore/src/core/record/l1-dedup.ts batchDedup, findCandidates, runLlmJudgment, parseBatchResult; MemoryCore/src/core/record/l1-writer.ts writeMemory L163-350 (DedupAction type L114); prompts in MemoryCore/src/core/prompts/l1-dedup.ts
mechanisms.limitations: Supersession is destructive. Old rows are hard-deleted from the retrieval store and no supersedes pointer is kept: the new id has no link to its predecessors, though merged_timestamps keeps a time trail. The delete and the upsert are separate non-transactional steps. Failures are logged and ignored, so duplicates or lost memories are possible. If the LLM fails, everything defaults to 'store'. Isolation is session-scoped, so cross-agent contradictions are not detected. Nothing downstream (scenes, persona) is invalidated when a target is deleted.
mechanisms.why: The recall-then-LLM-judge pattern is a proven way to propose supersession edges. ContextDB should keep the proposal but record it as a new revision with a supersedes edge and a PENDING semantic status, not delete the old row.

mechanisms.name: JEV gate: LLM change-impact classifier deciding whether L3 persona must be regenerated
mechanisms.how_it_works: When L2 scenes change, evaluateL3JevGate loads the scenes changed since checkpoint.last_persona_time, together with the current persona. It asks an LLM (via a decision provider) for a single label using strict priority: conflict > boundary_change > new_rule > reinforcement > none. conflict, boundary_change and new_rule trigger immediate persona regeneration. reinforcement and none defer it. If inputs are unreadable, too large (>32k chars) or the call fails, it reports 'unavailable' and defers without advancing the persona checkpoint, so the change is retried later. It emits diagnostics and an invariant check that the scenes it chose match the L2 diff.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryCore/src/core/persona/jev-gate.ts (JEV_INSTRUCTIONS, JEV_CRITERIA, IMMEDIATE set L30, evaluateL3JevGate L115-380); jev-diagnostics.ts; core/decision/registry.ts
mechanisms.limitations: Coarse-grained: it decides whether the whole persona is regenerated, not which claims inside it are invalidated. It is purely semantic and uses no structural dependency edges. It is time-cursor based (last_persona_time), not dependency based. It covers only the L2->L3 edge; the L1->L2 and L0->L1 layers have no equivalent.
mechanisms.why: This is close to ContextDB's semantic-validity check. Structural change marks dependents PENDING, and an LLM judge classifies them as conflict, boundary change or reinforcement before anything flips. Its label taxonomy and its 'don't advance the checkpoint on failure' rule are directly reusable for the Sem dependency type.

mechanisms.name: Memory generation log (input_refs -> output_refs + prompt version)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Each L1, L2 or L3 generation writes a MemoryGenerationLog. Fields: generation_id, layer, status, the identity tuple, prompt {memory_prompt_id, version, source, prompt_sha256}, input_refs [{layer: l0|l1|l2, record_id}], output_refs, model, latency and error. There is a per-memory ref record (mgr:{layer}:{sha256(memoryId)}) that points from a memory to its generation log. L1 records also carry source_message_ids (L0 ids) in JSONL.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryCore/src/core/memory-generation-log/types.ts (MemoryGenerationLog, MemoryGenerationRefStore.getMemoryGenerationRef); writers at core/record/l1-extractor.ts L385, utils/pipeline-factory.ts L992 (L2 from L1), L1297 (L3 from L2); /v3/memory-generation-log/{get,list} in gateway/v2-router.ts; l1-reader.ts L80 notes source_message_ids are not stored in SQLite
mechanisms.limitations: Write-only audit trail. Lookups go one way only (memory -> log), and nothing uses input_refs to propagate invalidation when an input is deleted or superseded. The edges are untyped, with no AND/OR structure and no support counting. source_message_ids are dropped by the SQLite store.
mechanisms.why: The provenance capture points already exist at each derivation step, including the prompt version hash, which is a nice touch for reproducibility. ContextDB would turn these into indexed typed justification edges with reverse lookup and propagation.

mechanisms.name: Asset visibility + ACL permission model (owner > membership > visibility > role default > ACL)
mechanisms.how_it_works:
checkPermission evaluates rules in this order:
1. If the asset is missing or archived: deny.
2. If the user is the owner: allow.
3. If the user is not an active team member: deny.
4. Visibility: private means owner only (even admins are denied). restricted means non-admins need an explicit allow ACL (subject user, team_role or agent). task means read-only for non-admins. team and agent pass through.
5. Role defaults: admin gets read/write/assign/share; member gets read.
6. Explicit allow ACL for the requested permission (read/write/delete/assign/share/use).
Agents receive assets through FixedAssetBinding, which has an injection_mode and a priority. canBindAsset checks whether visibility allows the binding. Lists filter out assets with status archived, deprecated or failed.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryCore/src/metadata/service/permission-checker.ts checkPermission, roleDefaultCovers, canBindAsset; MemoryCore/src/metadata/types.ts L35-62, L183-300; MemoryCore/src/metadata/service/metadata-service.ts L246 FILTERED_STATUSES
mechanisms.limitations: Allow-only. Status lifecycle values (draft/candidate/approved/deprecated) exist, but no enforced state machine or review transition logic turned up beyond filtering. expires_at on assets is stored but not enforced anywhere except user keys. Permissions apply per asset, not per memory item.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB needs scoping for shared context across agents and humans. This rule order and the agent-as-ACL-subject idea are a practical baseline. Status 'deprecated' could map onto ContextDB's supersession/validity states.

mechanisms.name: Profile (L2/L3) optimistic-lock sync via baselineVersion
mechanisms.how_it_works: A ProfileSyncRecord carries the baselineVersion seen at the last pull. On MongoDB, updateOne({_id, version: baselineVersion}) with upsert:false runs. If nothing matches and the doc exists, it throws a conflict; if the doc does not exist, it inserts. On TCVDB it reads the current row: if the md5 is equal it skips, if baselineVersion != currentVersion it logs a conflict and skips, otherwise it upserts with currentVersion+1.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryCore/src/core/store/types.ts ProfileSyncRecord L292-295; core/store/mongodb/memory-store.ts L703-725; core/store/tcvdb/memory-store.ts ~L1625-1665; core/profile/profile-sync.ts L441; gateway/v2-router.ts L1684-1734
mechanisms.limitations: The TCVDB path is read-then-write, so it has a TOCTOU window and silently skips on conflict instead of reporting it. The losing writer's change is dropped with no merge. Granularity is the whole file.
mechanisms.why: This is the conditional-update CAS pattern for heads. The Mongo form (a filter on the version field) is the correct one, and the TCVDB form shows the backend-capability pitfall ContextDB must avoid.

mechanisms.name: Checkpoint per-file async lock + distributed lease lock with renewal
mechanisms.how_it_works: Pipeline progress state (per-session L0/L1 cursors and pipeline counters, split into two namespaces so neither overwrites the other) is mutated only inside withFileLock, an in-process promise chain per file path. When injected, withDistributedLock adds an acquireLock(key, ownerId, ttl) lease with periodic renewLock. If a renewal fails, lockLost is set and the write is rejected as untrustworthy (CheckpointLockUnavailableError). Writes use an atomic tmp file plus rename.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryCore/src/utils/checkpoint.ts header L1-25, withFileLock L150-180, CheckpointDistributedLock L187-230, withDistributedLock L388-475
mechanisms.limitations: No fencing token, so a paused holder can still write after its lease expires and before the renewal check. It protects pipeline cursors, not memory items.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB's propagation workers need single-writer cursors. If leases are used, add fencing tokens (monotonic lease epochs checked by the store).

mechanisms.name: Transparent LLM-API proxy for capture + context injection
mechanisms.how_it_works: Agents set their API base URL to MemoryProxy. Per agent source (claude-code, codex, codebuddy, and others) a protocol adapter parses the request into an AgentContext. Registered InjectionHooks (with a cacheStrategy of none, session_init or hybrid, and prewarm) add ContextBlocks for recalled memory, persona and bound assets, and the adapter serializes the modified body upstream. On the response side, turns are recorded and skill extraction is triggered when isExtractionAllowed(config, asset) passes, a permissive YAML whitelist gate. Cost-guard routing (guard-adapter.ts) chooses upstream models; it does not gate actions.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryProxy/src/injection/pipeline.ts InjectionPipeline; injection/index.ts, prewarm.ts, injectors/; MemoryProxy/src/extraction-gate.ts isExtractionAllowed; MemoryProxy/src/guard-adapter.ts; pipeline/runners/anthropic.ts L1412, L1575 (tool_use counting for skill trigger)
mechanisms.limitations: Context is packed as opaque text blocks with no certificate or record of which revisions were injected that could be checked later. The proxy sees tool_use blocks but only counts them; it never blocks or validates an action. It depends on a proxy-compatible agent.
mechanisms.why: A proxy is the deployment point where ContextDB can attach a read certificate (the set of revision ids injected) to each turn and validate it against current heads when the model emits tool_use, without any agent cooperation. That would turn this proven integration channel into action-time gating.

mechanisms.name: Hybrid recall (native dense+sparse or FTS || vector with RRF) under isolation filter
mechanisms.how_it_works: recallL1Candidates prefers the store's native hybrid search when capabilities.nativeHybridSearch is set (TCVDB). Otherwise it runs FTS and client-embedding vector search in parallel and merges them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. It degrades to FTS-only when vectorSearch=false or embedding fails. The IsolationFilter (team/user/agent/session) is applied. StoreCapabilities lets callers adapt to each backend.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryCore/src/core/tools/l1-candidate-recall.ts recallL1Candidates; core/record/l1-dedup.ts findCandidates; core/store/types.ts StoreCapabilities L250-266; core/hooks/auto-recall.ts
mechanisms.limitations: No validity or staleness awareness in ranking. Superseded rows are absent only because they were deleted.
mechanisms.why: Standard, proven retrieval path. ContextDB can reuse the capability-negotiated backend pattern and add filtering by head and validity status.

mechanisms.name: Knowledge (CodeGraph/Wiki) auto-sync by periodic polling
mechanisms.how_it_works: AutoSyncScheduler scans ready repos every N minutes (default 10), de-duplicates them with a Set into a FIFO queue, and a fixed worker pool calls CodeGraphService.sync() to pull git changes and rebuild the index. Wiki index rebuilds are transactional and evict stale read connections. code_impact (the MCP tool) delegates transitive caller analysis, depth 1-10, to third-party codegraph.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryKnowledge/src/store/auto-sync-scheduler.ts; MemoryKnowledge/src/engines/wiki/manager.ts L841; MemoryKnowledge/src/mcp/tools.ts code_impact L89-102; src/engines/code/bridge.ts
mechanisms.limitations: Time-based full refresh, not dependency-driven. No link from memory items or skills to the code symbols or wiki pages they depend on, so a code change never marks a memory stale. Disabled by default (KNOWLEDGE_AUTO_SYNC_ENABLED=false).
mechanisms.why: code_impact shows a ready-made reverse-dependency source for code. ContextDB could subscribe to sync results and use the changed symbols as structural invalidation roots for context items that hold Ref/Cur deps on those symbols.

mechanisms.name: Action gating
mechanisms.how_it_works: Does not exist. There is no pre-action or pre-tool-call validation of memory freshness. The extraction gate is a config whitelist for write-side extraction, cost-guard routes models, and skill-permission checks ownership and team on skill mutations. The only freshness-guarded 'action' is a skill write via expected_version.
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryProxy/src/extraction-gate.ts; MemoryProxy/src/guard-adapter.ts; MemoryCore/src/core/skill/skill-permission.ts; no blocking of tool_use found in MemoryProxy/src/pipeline/runners/*
mechanisms.limitations: N/A
mechanisms.why: This is the gap ContextDB fills.

mechanisms.name: Dual-write append-only JSONL log + queryable store, pluggable backends
mechanisms.how_it_works: L1 records are appended to daily JSONL shards through the StorageAdapter (COS or local), which is the source of truth for backup, and upserted into SQLite/Mongo/TCVDB for retrieval. Skill blobs live in per-version directories on object storage, and the DB is authoritative for which directory is live, so orphan blobs are never read. Metadata store backends: SQLite and MongoDB adapters with a shared contract test suite (metadata-store.contract.ts).
mechanisms.evidence: MemoryCore/src/core/record/l1-writer.ts header L1-17 and appendRecord; core/storage/adapter.ts; core/store/{sqlite,mongodb,tcvdb}/*; metadata/store/{sqlite-adapter.ts,mongodb-adapter.ts,metadata-store.contract.ts}
mechanisms.limitations: The JSONL log and the store can diverge, because the two writes are independent and each tolerates failure. Reconciliation is periodic, and the code treats the vector store as the source of truth for cleanup, which contradicts the header comment.
mechanisms.why: An append-only log plus materialized index fits immutable revisions. ContextDB should make the log authoritative and derive the index from it transactionally, and keep the shared contract test suite approach for multiple backends.

analysis.overlap_with_contextdb:
There is little overlap at the semantic core. Each item below is checked against the code.
- Dependency-driven transitive invalidation: NO. Provenance is captured as input_refs/output_refs in MemoryGenerationLog, but it is write-only audit with no reverse lookup or propagation. When an L1 atom is superseded (hard-deleted), the L2 scenes and L3 persona derived from it are not touched. Staleness elsewhere is handled by time cursors (last_persona_time), periodic polling (knowledge auto-sync) and TTL pruning.
- Semantic validity: PARTIAL. The JEV gate is an LLM classifier (conflict/boundary_change/new_rule vs reinforcement/none) that decides whether the whole L3 persona is regenerated, and it defers without advancing the checkpoint on failure. That is close to a PENDING state, but coarse and for one edge only.
- AND/OR justifications, support counting, flip-only propagation: NO.
- Alternatives/branches: NO. Skill versions are linear, and L1 merge collapses alternatives into one LLM-written row.
- Immutable revisions + head + CAS: YES for Skills (row per version, is_head, partial unique index, expected_version -> SKILL_VERSION_STALE). PARTIAL for L2/L3 profiles (baselineVersion CAS). NO for L1 chat memory (delete + new id, version counter only).
- Certified context reads: PARTIAL, for skills only. The proxy pins the first-seen version per session for reads and injects it as expected_version on writes. Injected chat-memory context carries no certificate.
- Action gating: NO. Nothing validates context freshness before a tool call or action.
- Multi-agent sharing: YES. Team/agent/user isolation dimensions on every row, asset visibility (private/team/restricted/agent/task), allow-only ACLs with agent as a subject, and per-agent fixed asset bindings with injection modes.
analysis.could_contextdb_be_built_as_plugin_on_it:
Partially, but only as a sidecar, not as a clean plugin. What helps:
- MemoryProxy's InjectionPipeline has a hook registry, so ContextDB could register an injector that adds certified context blocks.
- The proxy already parses tool_use blocks per agent protocol, which is the natural place to put action-time certificate validation.
- The store interfaces (IMemoryStore, ISkillStore, StorageAdapter) are pluggable.
- MemoryGenerationLog already records derivation inputs at every pipeline step.
What blocks it:
- The core semantics conflict. L1 supersession hard-deletes rows and mints new ids, the LLM merges rows destructively, and the delete and upsert steps are non-transactional and failure-tolerant.
- No typed dependency edges or reverse index exist.
- The memory types (L0-L3, skill, wiki, code_graph) are fixed, and the pipeline is opinionated around LLM extraction.
Adding immutable revisions and supersedes edges for chat memory, typed dependency edges, and propagation would mean rewriting l1-writer and l1-dedup, the profile sync and the pipeline-factory stages, which is more fork than plugin.
Recommended approach: build ContextDB as its own store and service. Borrow these patterns directly: the skill version table with a head partial unique index and content-hash no-op, expected_version CAS, proxy-level session version pinning generalized into read certificates, JEV-style LLM change classification for Sem dependencies, and the visibility/ACL model. Optionally ship a MemoryProxy injector plus a tool_use validator as an integration adapter for teams already running this hub.

checks.mechanism: Skill immutable version rows + head flag
checks.correction: The core claim holds: one row per (skill_id, version), is_head flag, BEGIN IMMEDIATE flip-then-insert plus FTS sync in SQLite, copyTree copy-on-write, a content_hash+no-resource-change no-op that returns the head, the partial unique index on the head, names immutable, and the head never pruned. Three parts are wrong. (1) DELETE IS NOT A SOFT ARCHIVE. Since the 2026-07 change, SkillCore.delete physically deletes every version row (deleteAllVersions) and rmdirs every storage_dir. 'archived' survives only as a wire-compatible return field and for legacy rows. (2) 'The newest 3 are always kept' applies only to the TTL dimension. The count dimension (maxNonHeadVersions) is explicitly not protected by KEEP_RECENT. Both limits default to 0, which means no pruning at all. (3) The Mongo appendVersion has a worse flaw than 'not atomic'. If a row for version head+1 already exists, it silently returns that existing doc (findOne short-circuit). A racing writer that passed the expected_version check therefore gets the other writer's row back as its own result, and its content is dropped with no error. There is also a crash window in which two rows have is_head=true. A TCVDB backend also exists and uses compensating deletes.

checks.mechanism: expected_version optimistic lock on skill writes
checks.correction: Accurate. assertVersionFresh compares against a head read outside the transaction, so it is check-then-act. The UNIQUE(skill_id,version) backstop works in SQLite: the loser's INSERT of head+1 violates the constraint and its transaction rolls back. In MongoDB, the findOne-existing short-circuit at L171-172 bypasses the backstop and turns a lost race into a silent lost update rather than an error. Delete takes no expected_version. In the gateway, SKILL_VERSION_STALE maps to 40901.

checks.mechanism: Session-scoped lazy version pinning in proxy
checks.correction: The mechanism is real. READ_VERSION_OPS={get, files/read} have version injected and WRITE_LOCK_OPS={update, patch, files/write, files/remove} have expected_version injected. search and get responses lazy-pin with first-wins semantics, successful writes overwrite the pin with upsertVersion, and every error degrades silently. Four corrections. (1) There are two backends. The ProxyStorage/COS-KV backend (KvVersionPinRepo) is preferred whenever storage.enabled. It uses one object per skill under the prefix 'nottl/<spaceId>/<user>/<agentSource>/<session>/skill-vpin/<skillId>.txt', written with putTextIfAbsent (If-None-Match / INSERT OR IGNORE). It has no 30-min TTL, so 'pins live only for the session TTL' is true only for the Redis fallback. (2) The Redis key is skill:vpin:{user}:{agentSource}:{session}; the adapter ignores spaceId. (3) files/read never pins because its response has no skill_id. (4) If neither storage nor Redis is configured, pinRepo is null and there is no pinning. A further failure mode: a pinned version can be pruned by version cleanup or by physical delete, after which pinned reads fail.

verification.overlap_verdict: Mostly confirmed, with five corrections. (1) Immutable revisions + head + CAS for Skills: YES, but delete is now a physical delete of all versions and blobs, not a soft archive. The MongoDB backend can silently drop a concurrent write because it returns the already-existing v+1 row instead of raising a conflict. The CAS is check-then-act and is reliably backstopped only in SQLite. (2) L2/L3 profile CAS: PARTIAL, and weaker than stated. The gateway write path re-reads the current version right before writing and uses it as the baseline, so client-level stale writes are effectively last-writer-wins. Only profile-sync.ts uses a real last-pull baseline. (3) Semantic validity / JEV: PARTIAL, and weaker than stated. It is opt-in (triggerMode defaults to 'current') and acts only as an early trigger when the count-based trigger says no. It never vetoes regeneration, so it is a 'regenerate sooner' classifier, not a validity gate. (4) Certified reads: PARTIAL, skills only, as claimed. Pins do not expire under the preferred COS-KV backend; only the Redis fallback has the 30-min TTL. With no storage or Redis configured, pinning is off. (5) No transitive invalidation, no AND/OR justifications, support counting or flip-only propagation, no branches, no action gating: all CONFIRMED. The proxy does have a response-interception point (it synthesizes tool_use for skill delivery) but never validates actions. Multi-agent sharing: YES, confirmed, although skill mutations use their own owner_agent_id check rather than the asset ACL model. Extra correction: the 'periodic memory-cleaner reconciles superseded JSONL lines' story is false. The cleaner only deletes by age, so superseded L1 records stay in JSONL until retention expires and are absent from the retrieval store.
