analysis.one_line_summary: agent-memory keeps memory as markdown files that are the source of truth, rebuilds a SQLite FTS index from them, and supersedes memories by validity interval (invalid_at/superseded_by) under one flock-serialized write path. It uses content-hash optimistic checks and has an LLM "sleep" pass that is capped and audited. deja-vu is a read-mostly index over 42 coding agents' transcripts, with human-promoted decision notes (accepted/rejected/superseded/stale), heuristic "superseded" hints and git "files moved since" staleness hints. Neither has a dependency DAG, transitive invalidation or action gating.
analysis.architecture:
agent-memory (packages/core, mcp, cli, adapters, executor, harness): Python 3.12.
- Truth is one markdown file per memory, with YAML frontmatter fields name, abstract, type, created, updated, valid_from, invalid_at, superseded_by, weight, author, links[], provenance[] (core/record.py MemoryRecord, FIELD_ORDER).
- Raw conversation material is append-only in archive/. Session watermarks are JSON (core/watermark.py). Failed writes are queued as pending JSONL (core/pending.py). An append-only markdown decision ledger records Manage verdicts (core/ledger.py).
- The SQLite index is a pure cache that can be rebuilt (core/database.py): tables files, records (active and invalid), FTS5 surfaces chunks (active) and history (for as_of reads), vector_files/vector_chunks, access_log. Sync is incremental by content hash (core/indexer.py Indexer.sync).
- Process model: in-process library. Each CLI/MCP/hook invocation is a short-lived process, and cross-process safety comes from fcntl.flock (core/locking.py store_lock, file_lock). The library core has no LLM client. Distillation and the Manage "sleep" pass call the host's CLI through packages/executor.
- MCP: stdio JSON-RPC (mcp/server.py handle/_route). Tools in mcp/tools.py: memory_recall, memory_read, memory_record, memory_correct, memory_supersede, memory_delete, memory_trace, memory_merge, memory_feedback.
- Hooks (adapters/hook_entry.py) only capture transcripts, trigger distillation and inject context. They always exit 0.

deja-vu (cmd/deja, internal/*): one Go binary.
- Parsers in internal/sources read 42 agents' native transcript stores (JSONL, SQLite via the sqlite3 CLI, protobuf) into model.Session.
- Custom index at ~/.cache/deja/index.db/: records.bin (length-prefixed records), buckets/*.bin (token postings), manifest.gob/sessions.gob (source file state, watermarks, dedupe keys). Ranking is BM25 (internal/search).
- Rebuilds go to a new directory and swap in with two renames under flock(<dir>.lock) (internal/index/lock_unix.go lockDir/tryLockDir, swap_window.go openIndexFile). Readers that cannot get the lock fall back to lock-free snapshot reads.
- The only writable primary data is notes.jsonl, append-only, written by `deja remember`/`promote` (internal/sources/notes.go). Forgetting a session writes a tombstone (internal/index/privacy.go).
- Cross-machine sync exchanges JSONL batches with per-peer watermarks and import dedupe (internal/index/sync.go, internal/peers).
- MCP: a single `deja` tool with modes recall/context/blame/fix/how/orient/remember/handoff (cmd/deja/mcp.go dejaTool, dispatcherModes). Hooks inject recall at session start, on each prompt and on each tool call (cmd/deja/hook_tool.go).

mechanisms.name: Validity-interval supersession (one file = one interval)
mechanisms.how_it_works: A record is active iff invalid_at is null. record.invalidate(record, at, successor) sets invalid_at = max(valid_from, at) and superseded_by = successor slug. validate() rejects superseded_by without invalid_at and rejects self-supersession. A write with supersedes=X loads X (_predecessor), requires X to be active, gives the new record a new name (_successor_placement appends -2, -3... so cited names never break), then invalidates X in the same locked batch. Old files are kept. Recall's default surface is active-only, and as_of reads the history FTS surface with _current_at(row, moment). gc() physically deletes invalid files, and only a human-run command reaches it.
mechanisms.evidence: agent-memory/packages/core/src/agent_memory/core/record.py (MemoryRecord, validate, invalidate); core/store.py Store._prepare (supersedes handling, lines ~211-279), _predecessor, _successor_placement, correct(supersede_with), supersede, merge, delete, gc; core/recall.py Recall._eligible/_current_at; core/database.py SURFACE_HISTORY
mechanisms.limitations: Supersession is name-to-name and linear, with no logical-id/head separation. The 'logical' identity is the schema key → filename, and successors get suffixed names, so there is no stable logical handle whose head moves. No CAS on head, no ABA handling, no branches. Valid time and transaction time are conflated in one interval. Only 2 states (active/invalid), and the invariants explicitly reject a third state (CLAUDE.md invariant 7).
mechanisms.why: Keeping old revisions as files, forward superseded_by pointers and as_of history reads map onto immutable revisions plus a history surface. ContextDB should add a stable logical id with a CAS-moved head (SD1/SD12) instead of renaming successors.

mechanisms.name: Update-only vs replace enforcement (fact change forces successor)
mechanisms.how_it_works: An in-place write to an existing name may change only the description (abstract, links). If the body (the fact) differs, _enforce_update_only raises 'the fact changed: write a successor with supersedes'. Schemas declare mode upsert or add_only. add_only always creates a timestamp-suffixed new file.
mechanisms.evidence: core/store.py Store._enforce_update_only, _prepare (MODE_ADD_ONLY branch); core/schema.py MODE_UPSERT/MODE_ADD_ONLY
mechanisms.limitations: Fact equality is a whitespace-stripped body string compare. Nothing is semantic.
mechanisms.why: A cheap way to stop agents silently rewriting a fact in place. ContextDB can refuse to mutate content in place and force a new revision, keeping metadata-only edits separate.

mechanisms.name: Content-hash optimistic check + global flock + snapshot rollback
mechanisms.how_it_works: Every write path takes store_lock (exclusive fcntl.flock on state/lock with a timeout and polling). MemoryRecord.from_text stores source_hash = sha256(file text). _write_locked rereads the file and raises 'memory changed since it was read' if the sha256 differs, so a read-modify-write by Manage cannot clobber a concurrent edit. Files are replaced atomically (tempfile + os.replace). record_many/merge snapshot each touched path's prior bytes and _restore_files them if any step or the index projection fails, so the batch is all-or-nothing at the file level. Individual malformed items are rejected without aborting the batch.
mechanisms.evidence: core/locking.py store_lock, file_lock, lock_is_held; core/store.py record_many, _persist, _write_locked (hash check), _replace_file, _restore_files, merge; tests/unit/test_correction_concurrency.py, tests/system/test_concurrency.py
mechanisms.limitations: Global single-writer lock with no per-key concurrency. The hash check is not exposed over MCP: memory_correct takes no expected-version argument, and correct() rereads inside the lock, so two agents' corrections are last-writer-wins. Rollback is best-effort file restore, not crash-atomic (a crash mid-batch leaves partial state). No epoch or commit counter.
mechanisms.why: Content-hash-as-version is a simple CAS token that ContextDB should expose at the API level (expected_head/expected_hash on every write), which this project fails to do. The snapshot/restore pattern is a usable M0 fallback but should give way to a real WAL/commit.

mechanisms.name: Provenance pointers to append-only raw archive + evidence-time check
mechanisms.how_it_works: Each memory carries provenance[] as session pointers into archive/ or archived excerpts written by archive.append_provenance. trace/trace_evidence returns only the cited archived messages. _reject_facts_dated_after_their_evidence refuses valid_from later than the latest cited message. reconcile.to_record_spec defaults valid_from to the latest cited message time. Reconcile 'handles' are the only way an LLM executor may name an existing memory, and check() rejects any handle not on the sheet. _unsupported_addresses rejects emails not present in the evidence (anti-poisoning).
mechanisms.evidence: core/store.py _store_provenance, trace, trace_evidence, _reject_facts_dated_after_their_evidence; core/reconcile.py build, check, to_record_spec, _unsupported_addresses, _latest_cited_time; core/trace.py
mechanisms.limitations: Provenance is evidence citation only, not a justification. Nothing propagates from evidence to the memory, and evidence is immutable by construction. No AND/OR structure.
mechanisms.why: Maps directly to ContextDB's Evidence-kind logicals (single revision, immutable head) and to Pin edges to evidence. The 'valid_from ≤ cited evidence time' and 'handles must come from the read sheet' checks are cheap write-time admission rules worth copying.

mechanisms.name: Links between memories (untyped, forward-only, validated at write)
mechanisms.how_it_works: links[] holds slugs. _validate_links requires each newly added link to name another ACTIVE memory at write time. The indexer reports dangling_links (targets not in the index). Manage T0 adds co-occurrence links automatically (_add_cooccurrence_links). merge unions the sources' links.
mechanisms.evidence: core/store.py _validate_links; core/indexer.py Indexer._dangling_links; core/manage.py Manage._add_cooccurrence_links
mechanisms.limitations: No edge types, no reverse index, no propagation. When a linked target is superseded or deleted, dependents are NOT invalidated or flagged; at most the link shows up as dangling after gc. Links are associative, not justificatory.
mechanisms.why: Shows the gap ContextDB fills. An untyped 'links' list validated only at write time goes stale silently. ContextDB needs typed Pin/Cur/Sem/Ref incidences with support counting.

mechanisms.name: Value-based forgetting and capped LLM consolidation (Manage 'sleep')
mechanisms.how_it_works: Manage.sleep runs deterministic T0 actions (normalize dates, settle weights from access_log reads, co-occurrence links, exact-duplicate merges, clustering into groups). It then drafts proposals (merge, split, abstract review, delete when hits==0 and weight≤floor) that are not already in the decision ledger. A reasoner returns verdicts. _review enforces per-kind caps (max_merges/supersedes/splits/deletes_per_sleep). decide() applies the verdict through the single write path and appends to the append-only decisions.md ledger, so a rejected proposal is never re-proposed. Each sleep writes a markdown report and makes one git commit (_commit). Auto-dream scheduling uses a lease-based claim (dreaming.claim_due: file_lock on the claim lock, lease_expires_at, a run-lock probe and a 'write pipeline settled' precondition).
mechanisms.evidence: core/manage.py Manage.sleep, _review, _caps, proposals, decide, _propose_deletions, _write_report, _commit; core/ledger.py DecisionLedger.append; core/dreaming.py claim_due, current_claim, mark_succeeded, write_is_settled
mechanisms.limitations: Staleness is usage/weight-based, not dependency-based. Deletion is an LLM-gated proposal. No structural invalidation when premises change.
mechanisms.why: For ContextDB's Sem (semantic recheck) layer, the 'proposal → capped verdict → append-only ledger → audit commit' loop is a proven pattern for PENDING→VERIFIED/REJECTED validation records. The lease-based claim is a reasonable pattern for a background revalidator.

mechanisms.name: Shared file store across hosts + watermark-driven boundary writes
mechanisms.how_it_works: Claude Code, Codex, Muse, Hermes and others point at one store directory. Hooks capture transcripts to archive/ and advance a per-session 'consumed' watermark. distill() batches messages, builds a reconcile sheet of existing memories, asks the executor for operations, applies them via record_many, queues leftovers to pending/, and only then settles the 'distilled' watermark under capture_lock. A missed hook costs latency, not knowledge.
mechanisms.evidence: core/watermark.py Mark/Watermark; core/distill.py distill; core/pending.py Pending; adapters/hook_entry.py; core/locking.py file_lock
mechanisms.limitations: Consistency is serializability through one global flock on a local filesystem only, with no network or multi-machine story. No per-agent principals or ACLs beyond the 'author' field. No read snapshots tied to a version vector.
mechanisms.why: 'Truth advances only after the projection succeeds' with a two-counter watermark (consumed/distilled) gives exactly-once ingestion. That fits ContextDB's capture layer.

mechanisms.name: Markdown truth + rebuildable SQLite projection
mechanisms.how_it_works: Invariant: rm -rf .index && rebuild loses nothing. Indexer.sync computes content hashes of the files, diffs them against the files table in the manifest, and reprojects changed files into records, FTS5 and vectors. Rebuild uses the same code path. Reads never mutate truth; access goes to access_log and is settled into weight by Manage in batch.
mechanisms.evidence: core/indexer.py Indexer.sync/rebuild/_present_hashes; core/database.py SCHEMA; CLAUDE.md invariants 1-3
mechanisms.limitations: The file-per-record scan does not scale to large stores. Every write reprojects under the global lock.
mechanisms.why: 'Truth vs derived cache that can be rebuilt' and 'reads don't write truth' match ContextDB's oracle/derived-snapshot split. An export to human-readable markdown would be a selling point for adoption.

mechanisms.name: agent-memory MCP tool surface and single-core-call adapters
mechanisms.how_it_works: stdio JSON-RPC with 9 tools (memory_recall returns ranked paths/abstracts plus recall_fingerprint, memory_read takes a level for progressive disclosure, memory_record/correct/supersede/delete/merge/feedback/trace). _require validates arguments against the schema and rejects unknown fields. CLI, MCP and hooks all call the same Store/Recall methods (invariant 8).
mechanisms.evidence: packages/mcp/src/agent_memory/mcp/tools.py (TOOL_* constants, catalogue, dispatch, _recall, _read, _record, _correct, _supersede, _delete, _merge); mcp/server.py
mechanisms.limitations: No version/hash in responses that a client can pass back for CAS, no certificate, no 'why'.
mechanisms.why: A small verb set (recall→read-by-level→record/supersede) is a proven agent-ergonomic surface. ContextDB should mirror it and add certified_read plus expected_head arguments.

mechanisms.name: deja-vu decision lifecycle notes (accepted/rejected/superseded/stale)
mechanisms.how_it_works: `promote` appends a JSONL line {kind:promoted, session, state ∈ {accepted, rejected, superseded, stale}, title, text, tags, src_ts} to notes.jsonl. History is never rewritten, and the latest line per source session wins (loadPromotedNotesFrom). An identical re-promote is skipped. ConflictingNotes finds other ACCEPTED notes in the same project sharing a tag or ≥3 informative words and shows them to the human. deja never auto-resolves. Search hits carry Lifecycle, rendered by lifecycleSummary as 'replaced by a later decision' or 'marked stale — may no longer hold'.
mechanisms.evidence: deja-vu/internal/sources/notes.go NoteStates, AppendPromotedSourced, lastPromotedNote, loadPromotedNotesFrom, ConflictingNotes; internal/search/search.go Hit.Lifecycle, lifecycleSummary
mechanisms.limitations: States are set manually per session. Nothing propagates. Conflict detection is lexical overlap.
mechanisms.why: Real-world validation that agents need a 'stale / may no longer hold' state distinct from false, which is ContextDB's PENDING-not-FALSE stance. Surfacing the state inline on every read hit is the UX to copy.

mechanisms.name: deja-vu heuristic 'superseded' hint and git 'files moved since' staleness
mechanisms.how_it_works: At search time, hit i is marked Superseded if a hit j in the same project ends more than 24h later (and not in the future), and their snippet token/bigram sets overlap ≥0.6 (search.go ~590-636). Notes are excluded. Separately, attachMoved/filesMovedSince takes the files a session touched (role 'files'/'edit'), skips them if mtime is not after the session end, otherwise runs one `git log --since=<session end> --name-only -- files` per repo under a 400-600ms budget. It annotates 'N files this session touched have changed since'. It deliberately never claims 'unchanged'.
mechanisms.evidence: deja-vu/internal/search/search.go (Superseded field, overlap loop, snippetOverlap); cmd/deja/moved.go filesMovedSince, movedNote, attachMoved, gitRootOf
mechanisms.limitations: Annotation only, computed lazily at read time and bounded by budgets. Silence means unknown. No link to specific claims.
mechanisms.why: This is a working, cheap version of a Cur/Pin dependency on code files: record the file paths and the commit or mtime a context item depended on, then check git at read time. ContextDB can turn it into typed Pin(file@commit) incidences, and its asymmetric honesty ('changed' is certain, silence is UNKNOWN) matches SD14.

mechanisms.name: deja-vu per-action recall hook (advisory, not gating)
mechanisms.how_it_works: `deja hook-tool` runs on PreToolUse-style events, reads tool_name and tool_input (command, file_path, notebook_path, path), and emits at most one line under 480 bytes containing one prior decision about that exact command/file. It fires only if the file was touched in ≥2 sessions. The README-adjacent comments cite an A/B in which a line carrying the decision changed agent behavior.
mechanisms.evidence: deja-vu/cmd/deja/hook_tool.go (toolHookInput, toolHookMaxBytes, toolHookMinFileSessionsWithDecision)
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented (advisory injection only; no deny/block decision found)
mechanisms.limitations: Never blocks an action and validates nothing. It is context injection only.
mechanisms.why: Action-time is the right hook point and the payload must be tiny. ContextDB's action-time certificate validation can attach to the same PreToolUse hook. It returns allow/deny/warn based on certificate validity instead of injecting text.

mechanisms.name: deja-vu cross-machine sync with per-peer acknowledged watermarks
mechanisms.how_it_works: Export writes records newer than the per-peer watermark (watermarkKey(peer, source)). ExportDeferred does not advance the watermark until the receiver acknowledges the batch, so delivery is acknowledged. Ties on a timestamp are handled by a capped boundary set of recordIdentity hashes. Import dedupes by recordContentKey(harness, session, role, at, textHash), skips forgotten sessions (tombstones) and the machine's own records, sanitizes control/bidi chars, and never relays a record back to its origin. peers.Peer tracks LastPush/LastPull/LastError separately.
mechanisms.evidence: deja-vu/internal/index/sync.go Export, ExportDeferred, watermarkKey, recordIdentity, recordContentKey, sanitizeSyncField, appendImportedRecords; internal/peers/peers.go Peer
mechanisms.limitations: Append-only log replication of immutable transcript records, with no conflict resolution because nothing is mutable. No causal ordering.
mechanisms.why: For a future multi-host ContextDB, immutable revisions are append-only too. Acknowledged-delivery watermarks, content-key dedupe and tombstones that survive sync are directly reusable. Head moves would still need CAS/consensus on top.

mechanisms.name: deja-vu atomic index generation swap with lock-free snapshot readers
mechanisms.how_it_works: Writers take an exclusive flock on <dir>.lock (lockDir) and run recoverIndexDir under the lock to finish an interrupted swap. A rebuild writes a new directory and swaps it in with two renames. Readers call tryLockDir. If the lock is busy, they read lock-free, and openIndexFile retries ENOENT up to 10×20ms only while swapInFlight reports a swap in progress.
mechanisms.evidence: deja-vu/internal/index/lock_unix.go lockDir, tryLockDir; internal/index/swap_window.go openIndexFile, waitOutSwapWindow
mechanisms.limitations: Whole-index rebuild granularity. A single writer.
mechanisms.why: A simple pattern that is proven at scale for publishing derived snapshots (rebuilt indexes) without blocking MCP readers.

mechanisms.name: Progressive-disclosure recall (paths/abstracts first, read by level)
mechanisms.how_it_works: agent-memory recall returns an L0 candidate list with name, abstract and path, using BM25 FTS5 plus optional dense fusion (fuse_candidates) with kind weight and recency. memory_read takes a level (outline/full), so the agent pulls only as deep as needed. deja caps hit size (MessagesCapped) and hook payloads (480B per action).
mechanisms.evidence: agent-memory core/recall.py Recall.recall/_rank/fuse_candidates; core/store.py Store.read(level); deja-vu internal/search/search.go Hit.MessagesTotal/MessagesCapped
mechanisms.limitations: Ranking is not validity-aware beyond the active/invalid filter.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB's certified context reads can return handle plus status plus certificate at L0 and expand on demand, which keeps the token cost low.

analysis.could_contextdb_be_built_as_plugin_on_it:
Not as a plugin in the strict sense, because neither exposes extension points for validity computation. The useful option is to borrow their surfaces.

agent-memory: ContextDB could treat agent-memory's markdown store as one ingestion source or an export target. For example, it could map each memory file to a revision, superseded_by to a head move, and provenance to Pin→Evidence. It could also reuse its MCP verb set and its hook/distill/watermark pipeline. But the core semantics (typed incidences, support counts, L0/L1/L2 fixpoint, CAS heads, certificates) would have to live in ContextDB's own engine. agent-memory's single global flock, name-renaming successors, two-state invariant and per-write full reprojection all conflict with the design.

deja-vu: it is best treated as an upstream evidence provider. Its 42 transcript parsers, file-touch records and git-moved checks could feed ContextDB Evidence revisions and Pin(file@commit) dependencies, consumed through its CLI/JSON output (docs/json-output.md) rather than embedded. Its PreToolUse hook placement is the model for ContextDB's action-time certificate check.

Recommendation: build ContextDB as its own store, and integrate both projects as adapters (an importer and an evidence source). Do not build it on top of either.

verification.overlap_verdict: Confirmed with corrections. Neither codebase has dependency-driven transitive invalidation, OR/alternative-support justification, support counting, logical heads with CAS, certificates, or WHY/WHY_NOT. deja's tool hook is advisory only and has no deny path, so neither has action gating. agent-memory's links are validated against active targets only when written. When a target is superseded or deleted, nothing happens to its dependents. _dangling_links flags only targets missing from the index, so a link to a superseded or deleted (still-present) target is never flagged; it shows up only after gc removes the file. Invariant 7 does reject a third state. Corrections to the overlap summary: (a) agent-memory's content-hash check is weaker than 'used internally'. It is absent from the main record_many/_persist path, and it is vacuous for correct/delete/feedback, which re-read inside the lock. It only guards Manage's Store.write of a previously read record. (b) The 'force a successor when the fact changes' rule is bypassable. memory_correct (Store.correct) rewrites the body in place without _enforce_update_only, so in-place fact mutation is possible over MCP. (c) deja's notes.jsonl is not strictly append-only, because forget rewrites it via rewriteNotes. (d) agent-memory ingestion is at-least-once (a crash between record_many and the watermark settle re-distills), not exactly-once.

analysis.one_line_summary: Three provenance and graph-memory systems for agents. brain0 is an append-only, git-anchored Rust decision graph (task to artifact-version) with drift reconciliation, a detective DLP check and signed attestations. memory-graph is a TS CLI typed-relationship store that edits memories in place, so its versioning is mostly empty. agent-memory is a Neo4j Python library and FastMCP server with entity/fact/preference memory, SUPERSEDED_BY plus valid_from/valid_until on preferences only, extraction provenance edges, reasoning traces and a lock-node serialized ontology activation. None of them has dependency-driven transitive invalidation, CAS on memory heads, or pre-action gating.
analysis.architecture:
brain0 (Apache-2.0, Rust core plus TS GUI/server):
- Crates: brain0-model (typed nodes, versions, edges), brain0-storage (Storage trait with a SQLite impl; the Postgres impl lives in a private enterprise repo per the schema/sqlite.sql header), brain0-observer (ingests git commits or watch checkpoints into artifact versions), brain0-agentsrc (parses Claude/Codex transcripts into task versions, with secret redaction), brain0-reconcile (declared vs done drift), brain0-risk (a-priori/a-posteriori risk), brain0-policy (DLP), brain0-attest (Ed25519 in-toto signing), brain0-mcp (hand-rolled stdio JSON-RPC MCP server, protocol 2024-11-05), brain0-cli.
- Data model (schema/sqlite.sql): artifact_nodes and task_nodes hold a mutable current_version pointer plus risk scalars. artifact_versions and task_versions are append-only and use INSERT OR IGNORE with deterministic hashed ids (VersionId::for_artifact in brain0-model/src/version.rs).
- Edges table: PK (kind,src,dst), idempotent. Kinds are TaskModifiesArtifact, ArtifactContains, ArtifactDependsOn, ArtifactVersionSucceeds and TaskFollows (brain0-model/src/edge.rs).
- Other tables: task_embeddings, a content-addressed payload store (blake3 refs, payload_purged tombstones), audit_log, cursors, checkpoint_files.
- Process model: single local SQLite file (WAL, busy_timeout=5000) shared by the CLI, an observer/watch daemon and the MCP server.
- MCP tools (crates/brain0-cli/src/mcp_query.rs): brain0_debug, brain0_audit, brain0_context, brain0_blame. All are read-only queries.

memory-graph (MIT, TypeScript/Bun):
- Interface: a CLI only. CHANGELOG.md line 98 and lines 154/163 say the Python MCP server was replaced by direct CLI commands (store/get/update/link/related/as-of/history/changes/warn/outcome/... in ts/src/cli.ts around line 421).
- Backends (ts/src/backends): sqlite (default; memories table plus a relationships table with FTS triggers), falkordb, falkordblite, memgraph/neo4j over bolt, cloud REST.
- Model (ts/src/models.ts): Memory has type/title/content/tags/importance/confidence/version/updated_by plus a context with project_path, git_commit, session_id, visibility and tenant_id. There are about 45 typed RelationshipTypes (CAUSES, SOLVES, DEPENDS_ON, CONTRADICTS, DEPRECATED_BY, REPLACES, ...). Relationship properties are bi-temporal: valid_from, valid_until, recorded_at, invalidated_by, evidence_count, counter_evidence_count.

neo4j-labs/agent-memory (Apache-2.0, Python async plus a TS SDK):
- Memory layers: short_term (Conversation/Message), long_term (Entity/Fact/Preference with POLE+O typing, entity resolution, SAME_AS dedup), reasoning (ReasoningTrace/Step/ToolCall with TOUCHED edges to entities).
- Other parts: consolidation (dedup, supersede detection, read audit), a versioned ontology store, and integrations (pydantic_ai, langchain, google_adk, strands, openai_agents, ...).
- Storage: Neo4j only (Cypher in src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py, uniqueness constraints on ids in graph/schema.py setup_constraints), plus vector indexes.
- MCP: FastMCP server (mcp/server.py, mcp/_tools.py). Tools include memory_search, memory_get_context, memory_store_message, memory_add_entity, memory_add_preference, memory_add_fact, memory_create_relationship, memory_start_trace/record_step/complete_trace, graph_query, memory_get_entity_provenance, memory_get_entity_history and memory_set_entity_feedback. Tools carry READ/WRITE annotations.

mechanisms.name: brain0 append-only versions with a mutable current_version head and a successor chain
mechanisms.how_it_works: Each observed change appends an ArtifactVersion whose id is a deterministic hash of (artifact_id, timestamp, author, source commit/checkpoint), stored with INSERT OR IGNORE so a replayed ingest converges on the same row. The node row's current_version is then overwritten (INSERT OR REPLACE), and an ArtifactVersionSucceeds{predecessor,successor} edge is added when prev != new. Deletions are appended as a Deleted version, not removed. Task (prompt/session) versions accumulate the same way, carrying prompt_ref, decision_summary_ref, declared changes, drift, reads and read_secrets.
mechanisms.evidence: brain0-model/src/version.rs (ArtifactVersion, TaskVersion, VersionId::for_artifact); brain0-observer/src/lib.rs about lines 243-300 (record change: get_artifact_node -> append_artifact_version -> put_artifact_node -> put_edge ArtifactVersionSucceeds) and record_deletion about lines 308-345; brain0-storage/src/sqlite.rs append_artifact_version (INSERT OR IGNORE, line 428), put_artifact_node (INSERT OR REPLACE, line 306); schema/sqlite.sql header comment
mechanisms.limitations: The head update is a non-atomic read-then-write (get_artifact_node, then put_artifact_node) with no CAS and no wrapping transaction. Two concurrent observers could both read the same prev and fork the successor chain. Versions track code artifacts, not memory claims. There is no notion of semantic supersession (a newer claim replacing an older one).
mechanisms.why: This matches ContextDB's immutable revisions plus logical heads. Content-hash idempotent revision ids and an explicit successor edge are worth adopting. The head swap must become CAS (UPDATE ... WHERE current_version = expected) inside one transaction.

mechanisms.name: brain0 intent-to-change provenance (TaskModifiesArtifact plus reads capture)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Agent transcripts (Claude/Codex adapters) are parsed into Task nodes, one per session/prompt turn, and TaskVersions that record which files the agent READ (reads_json, paths only) and which secret kinds those reads contained. The observer links each artifact version produced to the task via TaskModifiesArtifact{task, artifact, version, change_kind, lines}. TaskFollows chains tasks. brain0 provenance <sha> joins a commit to agent sessions through shared artifact versions.
mechanisms.evidence: brain0-model/src/edge.rs (Edge enum); brain0-model/src/version.rs TaskVersion.reads/read_secrets; brain0-agentsrc/src/claude.rs, codex.rs, driver.rs; brain0-observer/src/lib.rs put_edge(TaskModifiesArtifact); docs/attestation.md (provenance command)
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented (provenance/attestation CLI flow partly seen only in docs/attestation.md; edge and storage code read)
mechanisms.limitations: Reads are recorded as bare paths with no version or hash of what was read. You therefore cannot tell later whether a write was based on stale content, and nothing links a read to the specific artifact version it saw. All of this is post-hoc, reconstructed from transcripts after the fact.
mechanisms.why: This is the closest thing to ContextDB's read-set certificates: it records what reached the model and what got changed. ContextDB should record reads as (item, revision_id) pins at read time so an action can be validated against them. That turns brain0's audit trail into a certificate.

mechanisms.name: brain0 declared-vs-done drift reconciliation
mechanisms.how_it_works: An agent declares changed paths via MCP/transcript (DeclaredChange). The observer records the paths that actually changed. compute_drift returns undeclared = actual - declared and phantom = declared - actual, with score = |symmetric difference| / |union|. The Drift is persisted on the TaskVersion, and every actual change is linked to the task (gap-filling). Drift feeds the a-priori risk score.
mechanisms.evidence: brain0-reconcile/src/lib.rs compute_drift, ReconcileInput; brain0-risk/src/lib.rs apriori_score (drift factor)
mechanisms.limitations: Compares path sets only. It is detective, not preventive.
mechanisms.why: A cheap, proven signal for checking that an agent's claimed effect set matches its actual effect set. It can be a post-commit check in ContextDB, comparing the declared write-set in an action certificate with the observed one.

mechanisms.name: brain0 retroactive (a-posteriori) risk and derived-artifact purge
mechanisms.how_it_works: A-posteriori risk is event-driven from later evidence. 'reverted' fires when an artifact version returns to an earlier structural fingerprint; immediate fixes, broken tests and linked issues are the other signals. It is kept separate from the a-priori score so 'looked safe, proved dangerous' stays visible. Aggregates (file/module/repo) derive their risk from children. On payload purge (mark_payload_purged), derived data such as the task embedding is deleted while topology is kept.
mechanisms.evidence: brain0-risk/src/lib.rs aposteriori_score, derive_aposteriori_factors (about lines 223-265), apply_aposteriori, aggregate derivation about line 290; brain0-storage/src/sqlite.rs test purge_keeps_topology_and_invalidates_derivatives (line 1076)
mechanisms.limitations: Risk is a scalar recomputed per node. There is no propagation along ArtifactDependsOn beyond a fan-in/fan-out count used as the blast_radius factor, and nothing is invalidated transitively. The derived-data purge is hand-coded for one derivative (embeddings).
mechanisms.why: Splitting structural validity from later evidence-based doubt parallels ContextDB's structural vs semantic validity. 'Purge source, keep topology, drop derivatives' is a concrete instance of derived-node invalidation that ContextDB generalizes with its justification DAG.

mechanisms.name: brain0 guard/preflight DLP policy (detective, plus a pre-commit preflight)
mechanisms.how_it_works: brain0-policy::evaluate(policy, ReadEvent{path, external, secret_kinds, remote}) is a pure function returning Violations (critical for a secret in a read, warn for sensitive/external paths). cmd_guard scans recorded reads and writes audit_log entries; with --strict it exits non-zero when criticals exist. cmd_preflight scans staged files (git diff --cached) with the redactor, assuming remote=true, so it can run as a git pre-commit hook to block secrets.
mechanisms.evidence: crates/brain0-policy/src/lib.rs evaluate (line 143), module doc lines 1-7 ('detective control'); crates/brain0-cli/src/main.rs cmd_guard (line 1057), cmd_guard_watch (line 1178), cmd_preflight (line 1238)
mechanisms.limitations: Gates content (secrets) and not context freshness. It never checks whether the agent's knowledge is stale before acting, and it has no relation to the graph's versions.
mechanisms.why: The 'pure policy evaluator plus CLI exit code as a hook' pattern is a proven integration route (git pre-commit, CI). ContextDB's action-time certificate validation can ship the same way, with a validate-certificate command that exits non-zero.

mechanisms.name: brain0 signed provenance attestations
mechanisms.how_it_works: An Ed25519 Signer signs in-toto Statement JSON assembled from the decision graph (commit, agent, model, changed files, reads, secret kinds, reviewers from commit trailers). verify needs only the public key. key_id is a public-key fingerprint, which allows key rotation.
mechanisms.evidence: crates/brain0-attest/src/lib.rs (Signer, verify, key_id_for); docs/attestation.md
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented (crypto lib read; the statement assembly CLI was seen only in docs)
mechanisms.limitations: Attests history, not the validity of context at action time.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB action certificates could be signed the same way, so downstream CI can verify that an action was taken against a validated context snapshot.

mechanisms.name: brain0 minimal stdio MCP server plus a read-only query provider
mechanisms.how_it_works: JsonRpcServer<P: ToolProvider> handles initialize, tools/list, tools/call and ping over line-delimited stdio JSON-RPC, and ignores notifications. The provider exposes brain0_debug, brain0_audit, brain0_context (intents and history for an artifact, by reference) and brain0_blame (symbol_at_line resolves a line to its narrowest symbol).
mechanisms.evidence: crates/brain0-mcp/src/lib.rs handle_message, serve; crates/brain0-cli/src/mcp_query.rs tools() line 147, artifact_context line 59, symbol_at_line line 136
mechanisms.limitations: Read-only. Agents cannot write or declare through it (declarations come from transcript parsing). Single process.
mechanisms.why: Returning context 'by reference' (ids plus summaries, hydrated on demand) is a good packing pattern for ContextDB's context reads.

mechanisms.name: brain0 content-addressed payload store with crypto-shred tombstones
mechanisms.how_it_works: Large blobs (prompts, diffs, summaries, checkpoint file contents) live in a blake3 content-addressed payload store referenced by PayloadRef. The graph rows keep only refs. Purge sets payload_purged=1 (a tombstone) without breaking the append-only topology. SQLCipher-style open_encrypted is available.
mechanisms.evidence: crates/brain0-storage/src/payload.rs; crates/brain0-storage/src/lib.rs verify_payload; sqlite.rs mark_payload_purged (line 777), open_encrypted (line 65); schema/sqlite.sql payload_purged columns
mechanisms.limitations: Single-node SQLite.
mechanisms.why: Splitting the immutable revision graph from content-addressed bodies, and supporting GDPR-style purge without rewriting history, fits ContextDB's immutable revisions.

mechanisms.name: memory-graph in-place memory update ('version' field never incremented)
mechanisms.how_it_works: _handleUpdateMemory reads the memory (db.getMemory), mutates its fields in JS, and calls updateMemory, which runs UPDATE memories SET ... version = ? ... WHERE id = ?. That writes back whatever version value was read, so the field is never bumped. The interface methods getMemoryVersions/getMemoryStateAt are optional and implemented by no backend. MemoryDatabase falls back to returning the current memory ('no versioning available').
mechanisms.evidence: ts/src/tools/memory.ts _handleUpdateMemory (about lines 96-117); ts/src/backends/sqlite.ts updateMemory (about lines 682-716); ts/src/database.ts lines 86-88 and 255-285 (fallbacks); grep shows no backend implements getMemoryVersions
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: partially: the version field exists in the schema, but history is effectively README/interface-only
mechanisms.limitations: Lost updates under concurrent writers (read-modify-write with no WHERE version = expected). No memory history.
mechanisms.why: A counter-example. A 'version' column without CAS or immutable rows gives neither history nor concurrency safety.

mechanisms.name: memory-graph bi-temporal relationship properties
mechanisms.how_it_works: Every relationship stores valid_from, valid_until (null means current), recorded_at and invalidated_by (id of the superseding item). Temporal CLI tools filter on these: as-of keeps edges where valid_from <= t < valid_until; history splits current from invalidated edges and prints 'Superseded by'; changes lists new and invalidated edges since t.
mechanisms.evidence: ts/src/models.ts RelationshipPropertiesSchema (about lines 160-176); ts/src/backends/sqlite.ts relationships DDL (about lines 175-190), createRelationship insert (about line 784), what-changed query line 1133; ts/src/tools/temporal.ts handlers (as_of about line 77, history about line 179, what_changed about line 248)
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: partially: read/query side implemented, but no code path sets valid_until or invalidated_by on an existing edge (only initial props at create or import). docs/temporal-memory.md describes more than the code does.
mechanisms.limitations: Validity is per edge, set by hand. Nothing propagates. Memory nodes themselves have no validity interval.
mechanisms.why: Separating valid time from recorded time and storing invalidated_by is a cheap, popular pattern for supersession metadata. ContextDB should derive these from revision heads and the justification DAG rather than leave them to manual entry.

mechanisms.name: memory-graph typed relationship vocabulary plus deprecation warnings
mechanisms.how_it_works: About 45 enumerated relationship types grouped as causal, solution, context, learning (CONTRADICTS, CONFIRMS), workflow (DEPENDS_ON, BLOCKS) and quality (DEPRECATED_BY, VALIDATED_BY). They are validated on create (isRelationshipType). warnPotentialIssues extracts entities from the current context and runs Cypher MATCH (old)-[:DEPRECATED_BY]->(new) where old MENTIONS those entities, warning the agent that a known-deprecated approach is relevant. Edges carry evidence_count and counter_evidence_count, and 'outcome' records success/failure to adjust effectiveness.
mechanisms.evidence: ts/src/models.ts RelationshipType (about lines 35-95); ts/src/proactive/predictive.ts warnPotentialIssues (line 201); ts/src/cli.ts cmdWarn (line 1483), cmdOutcome (line 1513)
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented (Cypher-capable backends only; guardSqliteFallback disables warn/outcome on sqlite)
mechanisms.limitations: Edges are informational. DEPENDS_ON does not cause invalidation. The warning relies on heuristic entity matching and is advisory text.
mechanisms.why: A proven, agent-friendly typed-edge vocabulary. ContextDB's Pin/Cur/Sem/Ref dependency types could add semantic labels (CONTRADICTS, DEPRECATED_BY) as Sem edges, and a 'warn on relevant superseded items' retrieval hook is a useful UX.

mechanisms.name: memory-graph observe-only guard (explicit anti-gating)
mechanisms.how_it_works: When MEMORYGRAPH_AUTO_MODE is set, assertAutoModeSafe(op) throws ObserveOnlyViolation if an operation is in BLOCKING_OPERATIONS. That set is empty of exposed operations, by design: memory 'MUST NEVER be on a code path that can block a Done-flip, gate, or commit'.
mechanisms.evidence: ts/src/observe-only-guard.ts (module doc lines 1-30, assertAutoModeSafe)
mechanisms.limitations: The design intentionally forbids the gating that ContextDB wants.
mechanisms.why: Shows the opposite design choice. Worth noting that popular memory tools deliberately avoid gating, so ContextDB's action gating is a differentiator and should be opt-in and fail-open-configurable.

mechanisms.name: agent-memory preference supersession (SUPERSEDED_BY plus a validity interval)
mechanisms.how_it_works: add_preference sets p.valid_from = datetime(). supersede_preference(old,new) runs MATCH old, new MERGE (old)-[:SUPERSEDED_BY]->(new) SET old.valid_until = coalesce(old.valid_until, datetime()), which is idempotent. get_preferences_for(active_only=True) filters NOT (p)-[:SUPERSEDED_BY]->(), and as_of filters by the validity interval. Consolidation detect_superseded_preferences finds candidates by vector similarity in the same category with newer created_at and different text, then applies the same Cypher (dry_run by default) and records a ConsolidationRun.
mechanisms.evidence: src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/long_term.py add_preference (about line 983), supersede_preference (lines 1060-1083), get_preferences_for (lines 1085-1125); memory/consolidation.py detect_superseded_preferences (about lines 230-310)
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented (preferences only; Fact has valid_from/valid_until fields but no supersede operation, and Entities are mutated in place)
mechanisms.limitations: Supersession is node-to-node with no head pointer and no CAS. Two concurrent supersessions of the same old preference both succeed, creating a branching SUPERSEDED_BY with no conflict detection. Nothing depending on a superseded preference is invalidated. Similarity-based auto-supersede is heuristic.
mechanisms.why: Idempotent MERGE edge plus coalesce on valid_until is a clean, proven supersession write. The 'consolidation proposes, dry-run by default, recorded run' workflow fits ContextDB's semantic-validity PENDING step: an LLM or similarity check proposes, then a human or policy confirms.

mechanisms.name: agent-memory extraction provenance and reasoning traces
mechanisms.how_it_works: Extracted entities get (e)-[:EXTRACTED_FROM {message_id, confidence, start_pos,...}]->(Message) and (e)-[:EXTRACTED_BY]->(Extractor). get_entity_provenance returns {sources, extractors} and is exposed as the MCP tool memory_get_entity_provenance. Reasoning memory records ReasoningTrace -> ReasoningStep -> ToolCall and (ReasoningStep)-[:TOUCHED]->(Entity) edges, written explicitly or by on_tool_call_recorded hooks that infer touched entities.
mechanisms.evidence: graph/queries.py CREATE_EXTRACTED_FROM_RELATIONSHIP (line 1090), CREATE_EXTRACTED_BY_RELATIONSHIP (line 1106), GET_ENTITY_PROVENANCE (about line 1129); memory/long_term.py get_entity_provenance (line 2224); memory/reasoning.py record_tool_call (about lines 629-730), _record_touched_edge (line 608), on_tool_call_recorded (line 590); mcp/_tools.py memory_get_entity_provenance
mechanisms.limitations: Provenance points at messages and extractors only. It is not used for invalidation: deleting or correcting a source message leaves derived entities untouched. TOUCHED edges are entity-level with no revision pin.
mechanisms.why: Source and extractor provenance edges are the raw material for ContextDB's justification DAG. ContextDB would make them justification edges with support counting so a retracted source flips derived items to PENDING or invalid.

mechanisms.name: agent-memory singleton lock-node serialization for ontology activation
mechanisms.how_it_works: ACTIVATE_ONTOLOGY_VERSION runs MERGE (lock:OntologyLock {id:'active'}) SET lock.updated_at = datetime() first, in the same write transaction, before SET v.is_active=true and clearing the others. Writing one shared node, backed by a uniqueness constraint, takes a Neo4j write lock and serializes concurrent activators, keeping 'exactly one active version' true. Ontology revisions are immutable: update() appends revision n+1 (CREATE (o)-[:HAS_VERSION]->(v:OntologyVersion{revision, schema_hash, document})) and never rewrites one.
mechanisms.evidence: src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py comment lines 2067-2073 and ACTIVATE_ONTOLOGY_VERSION (lines 2074-2086), CREATE_ONTOLOGY_VERSION (line 1995); graph/schema.py constraints list incl. ontology_lock_id (lines 105-128); ontology/store.py update (lines 445-492), activate (line 494), _add_version (line 890)
mechanisms.limitations: Applies only to the ontology, not memory items. update() computes revision = max_revision+1 via a separate read (GET_ONTOLOGY_MAX_REVISION) before the write, and there is no uniqueness constraint on (ontology_id, revision), so two concurrent updates can create duplicate revision numbers. That is a lost-sequence race.
mechanisms.why: This is the one real concurrency primitive across the three repos and a proven Neo4j idiom: serialize by writing a lock node, plus immutable revisions with a single active head. ContextDB's head CAS can use the same idea (write the head node first in the txn, compare expected revision). It should also avoid the max+1 race by putting a uniqueness constraint on (item, revision) or by using CAS on the head.

mechanisms.name: Tenant/visibility scoping (agent-memory multi_tenant, memory-graph visibility)
mechanisms.how_it_works: agent-memory: when multi_tenant=True, _enforce_multi_tenant raises if user_identifier is missing. Data hangs off (:User {identifier}) via HAS_PREFERENCE etc., and reads are scoped by MATCH from the User. memory-graph: MemoryContext carries tenant_id, team_id, created_by and visibility (private/project/team/public), used as filters. brain0: task_nodes carry session_cwd and agent_name for project scoping in one shared SQLite DB.
mechanisms.evidence: agent-memory memory/reasoning.py _enforce_multi_tenant (line 406), long_term.py get_preferences_for; memory-graph ts/src/models.ts MemoryContextSchema (about lines 115-132), docs/MULTI_TENANCY.md; brain0 schema/sqlite.sql task_nodes.session_cwd
mechanisms.limitations: Sharing is plain shared storage. None of them gives agents read snapshots, a notion of 'context I read at revision X', conflict detection between agents, or change notification/subscription.
mechanisms.why: Scoping keys (tenant/team/agent/session) are table stakes that ContextDB must carry. They do nothing for consistency, which is ContextDB's actual contribution.

mechanisms.name: agent-memory opt-in read audit (MemoryReadAudit)
mechanisms.how_it_works: record_read_audit(query, user_identifier, kind, result_count, metadata) creates a (:MemoryReadAudit) node and optionally links (:User)-[:PERFORMED_READ]->(audit). It is deliberately explicit opt-in: reads are not intercepted automatically, to avoid doubling traffic.
mechanisms.evidence: src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/consolidation.py (about lines 385-450); config/settings.py about line 579; graph/schema.py constraint memory_read_audit_id
mechanisms.limitations: Records the query text and a count only, not which item revisions were returned. It cannot be used to validate an action later.
mechanisms.why: Precedent for persisting read events as graph nodes. ContextDB's certified context read is this, strengthened to store the exact (item, revision) set returned and made mandatory for gated actions.

mechanisms.name: Hybrid retrieval and context assembly
mechanisms.how_it_works: agent-memory: memory_get_context assembles short-term messages, long-term entities/preferences/facts and similar reasoning traces via vector indexes (db.index.vector.queryNodes) and text indexes. memory-graph: FTS5 on sqlite plus recall/contextual-search with relationship enrichment. brain0: task embeddings (local FNV hash embed or model embed) with cosine search, and MCP tools return references hydrated on demand.
mechanisms.evidence: agent-memory mcp/_tools.py memory_get_context (line 120), memory/reasoning.py get_context (line 1186); memory-graph ts/src/backends/sqlite.ts FTS triggers (about line 209), ts/src/tools/search.ts; brain0 crates/brain0-storage/src/lib.rs local_embed, sqlite.rs search_tasks_by_vector (line 830)
mechanisms.limitations: No retrieval path filters out stale or superseded items, except agent-memory preferences (active_only). Results carry no validity or certificate metadata.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB needs the same hybrid retrieval but must annotate every returned item with its revision and validity status (VALID/PENDING/INVALID) and emit a read certificate.

analysis.overlap_with_contextdb:
Little overlap on ContextDB's core semantics. Per mechanism, checked in source:

(1) Dependency-driven transitive invalidation: absent in all three.
- brain0 has an ArtifactDependsOn edge, but it is used only to count fan-in/out for a risk factor (brain0-risk/src/lib.rs derive_apriori_factors). Nothing propagates.
- memory-graph's DEPENDS_ON, CONTRADICTS and DEPRECATED_BY edges are informational. Its valid_until/invalidated_by fields are never set by any code path after an edge is created.
- agent-memory's SUPERSEDED_BY touches only the superseded preference itself. Its EXTRACTED_FROM provenance is never used to retract derived entities.
- The nearest analogues: brain0 purges derived embeddings when a payload is purged (hand-coded, one level deep), and its a-posteriori 'reverted' risk is recomputed per node.

(2) AND/OR justification and support counting, or alternative support: absent everywhere. No item records multiple alternative justifications, and nothing counts support.

(3) Immutable revisions plus heads: brain0 has them for code artifacts and tasks (append-only *_versions, a current_version pointer, a successor edge), but the head update is a non-atomic read-then-write with no CAS. agent-memory has them only for ontologies (immutable revisions, single active flag serialized by an OntologyLock node). memory-graph updates memories in place and never increments its 'version' field.

(4) CAS or conflict detection on memory items: absent in all three. The only concurrency control is agent-memory's lock-node write for ontology activation, which itself has a max+1 revision race in update().

(5) Structural vs semantic validity (PENDING): absent. The closest analogue is agent-memory consolidation proposing supersede candidates with dry_run on by default. memory-graph's evidence_count/counter_evidence_count are confidence counters, not states.

(6) Certified context reads and action-time validation: absent.
- brain0 records which files an agent read (paths only, no revisions) and gates secrets via guard --strict and preflight on staged files. That is content DLP, not freshness.
- agent-memory's MemoryReadAudit records the query text and a count only.
- memory-graph explicitly forbids gating (observe-only-guard.ts).

(7) Typed dependencies Pin/Cur/Sem/Ref: not present. memory-graph's typed relationship vocabulary is semantic labeling only.
analysis.could_contextdb_be_built_as_plugin_on_it:
Mostly no. None of the three can host ContextDB's core as a plugin without replacing its write path.

- brain0 has the best-aligned substrate: an append-only versioned graph, typed edges, a pluggable Storage trait (brain0-storage/src/lib.rs) and an MCP server. But it is scoped to code artifacts and agent tasks reconstructed after the fact from git and transcripts. Its storage trait has no transactions or CAS, the MCP surface is read-only, and its model has no memory or claim items. The realistic route is to treat brain0 as an upstream provenance source, or a companion that ContextDB feeds or ingests: commits and transcript reads become Pin-dependency evidence. Its patterns are worth borrowing, not building on: content-hash idempotent revision ids, a blake3 payload store with purge tombstones, declared-vs-done drift, a pure policy evaluator exposed as a CLI exit-code gate, and Ed25519 in-toto attestations of certificates.
- agent-memory (Neo4j) could serve as a storage and retrieval backend. Its Cypher, constraints, vector indexes and FastMCP tool registration (mcp/_tools.py register_tools) are extensible, and ContextDB's revisions, heads and justification edges could be modeled as extra labels with the OntologyLock idiom for CAS. But its Entity/Fact writes are in-place and unversioned, so ContextDB would bypass its LongTermMemory write API and use only the client, schema and MCP scaffolding plus the extraction pipeline as a source of EXTRACTED_FROM justifications.
- memory-graph is a CLI with in-place updates, no versioning and an explicit observe-only (anti-gating) stance. It is useful only as a reference for an agent-friendly typed relationship vocabulary and the 'warn on deprecated approach' retrieval hook.
analysis.license: brain0: Apache-2.0 (open-core; the Postgres backend and enterprise parts live in a private repo, and contributions require a CLA, see cla/). memory-graph: MIT. neo4j-labs/agent-memory: Apache-2.0 (pyproject.toml).

checks.mechanism: brain0 append-only versions + mutable current_version head + successor chain
checks.correction: None material. VersionId::for_artifact hashes (artifact_id, timestamp rfc3339, author key, source ref). append_artifact_version uses INSERT OR IGNORE; put_artifact_node uses INSERT OR REPLACE. The observer does get_artifact_node, then append, then put_artifact_node, then the ArtifactVersionSucceeds edge when prev != new. record_deletion appends a Deleted version. No transaction exists anywhere in the crates: grep for transaction/BEGIN/savepoint finds nothing, only PRAGMA WAL + busy_timeout. So the non-atomic, no-CAS limitation holds. One addition: replay idempotency also depends on the timestamp being deterministic. The id includes the timestamp, so a re-ingest with a different observer timestamp does not converge.

verification.overlap_verdict:
Mostly correct ('little overlap on core semantics' holds), but these per-mechanism statements need corrections.

(1) Transitive invalidation: absent, as claimed. But brain0's ArtifactDependsOn is not just fan-in/out. blast_radius (brain0-risk/src/lib.rs:183-200) does a transitive BFS that counts all dependents, so a transitive dependency walk exists. It yields only a risk scalar, with no state flip.

(2) Support counting: the claim 'nothing counts support' is too strong. agent-memory RELATED_TO edges have r.support, incremented on every re-observation, plus r.source_message_ids (capped at 25) and an AND-folded r.derived (asserted vs derived) flag (graph/queries.py:431-466, 555-628). It is a monotonic observation counter: never decremented, not touched by DELETE_MESSAGE, with no AND/OR justification semantics. So no TMS-style support counting, but it is the closest raw material.

(3) Immutable revisions plus heads: the memory-graph statement is wrong for its default backend family. On FalkorDB/FalkorDBLite, updateMemory snapshots the prior state into :MemoryVersion (state_valid_from/state_valid_until, version_number) and increments m.version, with getMemoryStateAt/getMemoryVersions for as-of reads (falkordb-shared.ts:615-645, 980-1060). Only the sqlite fallback updates in place. It is still copy-on-write snapshots behind a mutable stable-id node, with no CAS or expected-version check. The brain0 claim (no transaction anywhere, no CAS) and the agent-memory ontology claim are confirmed.

(4) CAS: confirmed absent. OntologyLock is the only serialization, and the max+1 race in ontology update() is real (no (ontology_id, revision) constraint).

(5) PENDING: confirmed absent. The nearest analogue is the dry-run consolidation.

(6) Certified reads: confirmed absent. brain0 reads are paths only, and MemoryReadAudit stores query text and a count. memory-graph observe-only-guard.ts forbids blocking operations only when MEMORYGRAPH_AUTO_MODE is set; it is a no-op otherwise.

(7) Pin/Cur/Sem/Ref: confirmed absent.

Also: brain0's provenance and attest CLI flows are implemented in code (main.rs:1424, 1461), not only in docs.
