analysis.one_line_summary: Three small repos that tie memory to code (git, SQLite). Kage hashes cited files and symbols so stale memory is kept out of recall, and promotes memory only when a branch merges. agents-remember keeps a memory-commit to code-commit ledger in Code-Commit trailers and reopens cited claims when the cited code changes. agent-memory-mcp adds valid_from/valid_until supersession chains that it writes in one transaction, plus a drift scan based on file mtimes. None of them has a justification DAG, transitive invalidation, CAS heads or action-time certificate checks.
analysis.architecture:
KAGE (TypeScript/Node, GPL-3.0). Most of the logic is in one large file, mcp/kernel.ts (about 21.9k lines). Storage: each memory is a "packet" file (OKF markdown or legacy JSON) under .agent_memory/packets/ (approved) or .agent_memory/pending/, committed to the code repo's git. Derived indexes (code graph, knowledge graph, FTS, vectors) live behind a StoreBackend interface (mcp/store/types.ts) with JSON (store/json.ts) and node:sqlite (store/sqlite.ts) backends. Tables: packets, packet_paths(sha256), packet_symbols(sha256), files, symbols, import_edges, call_edges, kg_*. Data model: MemoryPacket{id, status: pending|approved|deprecated|superseded, paths[], freshness{path_fingerprints[{path, sha256, size, symbols[{name, kind, sha256}]}], last_verified_at, ttl_days, superseded_by}, edges[{relation, to, evidence, created_at}], quality{contradicts[], reports_stale, superseded_by}} (kernel.ts:95-123). Audit log: append-only .agent_memory/audit/events.jsonl, written by recordMemoryAudit (kernel.ts:~4808), with actor, branch and git head. Process model: an MCP stdio server (mcp/index.ts, about 85 kage_* tools) plus a CLI (mcp/cli.ts) and a local daemon/HTTP app (mcp/daemon.ts, mcp/delegation/api.ts, protected by delegation/guard.ts: loopback-only, Origin check, 0600 token). A delegation subsystem (mcp/delegation/*) runs agent "runs" in git worktrees under a state machine (contract.ts LEGAL_TRANSITIONS) and merges them through ratify.ts mergeRun. MCP tools include kage_recall, kage_learn, kage_capture, kage_supersede, kage_feedback, kage_pr_check, kage_verify_citations, kage_memory_lineage, kage_conflicts, kage_branch_overlay, kage_dispatch, kage_merge_run.

AGENTS-REMEMBER (Python, MIT, about 251k lines, FastMCP stdio). Memory ("onboarding" markdown docs with citation tables) lives in a separate external memory git repo/worktree paired with the code repo. Kernel: mcp/src/agents_remember/kernel/ (memory_ledger.py, memory_attribution.py, memory_cache.py, file_lock.py, atomic_write.py, git_freshness.py). Quality and staleness checks: memory_quality/style/citations/* (claim_reopen.py, claim_change_router.py, provenance.py, model.py) and memory_quality/integrity/onboarding_drift_check/*. A large worktree lifecycle/closeout/integration orchestration (worktrees/*, serving/*). MCP surface (models/tools/public_roster.py): context_packet, resolve_context, drift_check, memory_quality_check, citation_fix, memory_carryover_plan/apply, memory_baseline_*, worktree_start/sync/closeout_preview/closeout_apply/integrate/abandon, lifecycle_gate, gate_decide, gate_list, dispatch_agent, message_parent/child, grepai_*/cgc_* code search.

AGENT-MEMORY-MCP (Go, MIT, about 33.7k lines). A single SQLite database (internal/dbutil/sqlite.go: WAL, busy_timeout 5000, _txlock=immediate). The memories table has valid_from, valid_until, superseded_by, replaces, observed_at, sediment_layer and a metadata map (internal/memory/memory.go:57-59, 665-688). Process model: one Go server over stdio or HTTP (docs/SHARED_SERVICE.md: bearer token, Docker), with an in-process writeMu and a cache. A steward service (internal/steward/*) runs scans for drift, contradictions and duplicates, keeps an inbox and a policy with auto-merge and a killswitch. MCP tools (internal/server/tools_*.go): store_memory, update_memory, mark_outdated, merge_duplicates, promote_to_canonical, recall_memory, recall_as_of, knowledge_timeline, recall_multihop, drift_scan, verify_entry, verification_candidates, conflicts_report, steward_run/inbox/policy, store_decision/runbook/incident/dead_end, sediment_cycle, and others.

mechanisms.name: Kage: symbol-anchored content fingerprints for cited code
mechanisms.how_it_works: Write time: memoryPathFingerprints(projectDir, paths, anchorText) stores {path, sha256, size} for each cited path. For TS/JS files it also extracts symbols (extractSymbols), hashes each symbol's line span, and keeps a symbol only when (a) the memory's text mentions its name as an identifier and (b) the name resolves to exactly one span in the file. It stores up to 32 {name, kind, sha256} per file. Check time: fingerprintPathContentChanged returns false if the whole-file sha matches. If the file differs and has anchored symbols, it returns true only when an anchored symbol is gone or its span hash changed. Otherwise any whole-file change counts. A process cache keyed by mtime+size avoids re-hashing. CHANGELOG/HISTORY files are skipped (isAppendOnlyLedgerPath).
mechanisms.evidence: mcp/kernel.ts: MemoryPathFingerprint/MemorySymbolFingerprint (125-140), memoryPathFingerprint (~3925), symbolSpanHashesFromText/fileSymbolSpanHashes (~4005-4065), memoryPathFingerprints (~4070-4101), fingerprintPathContentChanged (~4109-4130), APPEND_ONLY_LEDGER_RE (~4163)
mechanisms.limitations: Symbol anchoring covers TS/JS only; other languages use the whole-file hash. Anchors are chosen by matching names in prose, so this is heuristic. Hashes are byte-level, so a format-only change trips them. It never asks whether the claim still holds, only whether the evidence bytes moved.
mechanisms.why: This is a working, cheap way to implement ContextDB's Pin/Cur structural dependency on code: a dependency target of (path, symbol, span-hash) gives finer invalidation than a whole file and fits 'structural change -> PENDING'.

mechanisms.name: Kage: hard vs soft staleness tiers, applied to recall and the PR gate
mechanisms.how_it_works: staleMemoryReasons collects reason strings: status deprecated/superseded, reports_stale>0, TTL past last_verified_at, all or some cited paths missing, linked path content changed. staleSeverity sorts them into 'hard' (status, reported, TTL, all paths missing) and 'soft' (partial missing, content changed). recallHardStaleReason/recallStaleReason drop hard-stale packets from recall and also drop packets whose cited content changed (strict recall). prCheck fails (errors[]) only on hard-stale packets or out-of-date graph artifacts. Soft-stale packets, contradictions and reconciliation items only produce warnings. reverifyMemory re-stamps fingerprints and last_verified_at in place, and refuses when all evidence is gone.
mechanisms.evidence: mcp/kernel.ts: staleMemoryReasons (4167-4207), staleSeverity (4214-4222), recallHardStaleReason (4229-4253), recallStaleReason (4260-4269), prCheck (19473-~19570), reverifyMemory (20788-20835), staleCatch (19422-19460)
mechanisms.limitations: Staleness is recomputed from the filesystem on each read and never stored as a state transition. It does not propagate: when packet A goes stale, packets built on A are unaffected. The reasons are untyped strings matched by prefix. There is no PENDING state; a soft-stale packet is either withheld (strict recall) or flagged.
mechanisms.why: It shows the PENDING-vs-FALSE split working in practice: the soft/hard split maps onto ContextDB's structural-invalid -> PENDING vs semantic-FALSE. The 'reverify in place vs supersede' choice maps onto revalidating a revision versus writing a new one. ContextDB should store the state and propagate it instead of recomputing ad hoc.

mechanisms.name: Kage: supersede as a bidirectional edge plus status flip, with contradiction clearing
mechanisms.how_it_works: supersedeMemory(old, replacement, reason) checks both exist and that old != replacement. It sets old.status='superseded', writes superseded_by/superseded_reason/superseded_at into quality and freshness, upserts edge superseded_by on the old packet and supersedes on the replacement, then removes the old id from every packet's quality.contradicts. It rewrites the affected files, appends an audit event and rebuilds indexes. Packets are mutated in place; there are no immutable revisions. Lineage comes from edges plus the audit log (kage_memory_lineage/timeline).
mechanisms.evidence: mcp/kernel.ts: upsertPacketEdge (20579-20588), packetSupersededBy (20590-20597), supersedeMemory (20837-20944), recordMemoryAudit (~4805-4830)
mechanisms.limitations: Mutation in place with plain writeFileSync: not atomic and no lock (writeJson, kernel.ts:2632-2639). Three or more files are written without a transaction, so a crash leaves a half-superseded pair. Dependents of the superseded packet are not re-examined. There is no CAS against the head the caller read.
mechanisms.why: Superseding resolves open contradictions, and the edge carries a reason. ContextDB should keep that semantics but implement it as a new head revision under CAS.

mechanisms.name: Kage: merge-ratification (git merge promotes branch-local memory)
mechanisms.how_it_works: A delegated run's learnings are committed on the run's own branch as pending packets (tagged with runTag). mergeRun refuses unless the run state is 'ready' (or 'approved' when review_required is set), a claim record exists, the branch has commits (for feature/bugfix/refactor/migration), and the reviewer's uncommitted files do not overlap the branch's. It then runs git merge --no-ff, flips that run's packets pending->approved (setPacketStatus), commits 'kage: ratify N learning(s)', transitions the run to merged and refreshes indexes.
mechanisms.evidence: mcp/delegation/ratify.ts: header comment (1-4), mergeRun (142-240), packetFilesForRun, setPacketStatus; mcp/delegation/contract.ts LEGAL_TRANSITIONS (49-93), transitionRun (1087-1128)
mechanisms.limitations: Git provides the only isolation and serialization: memory conflicts become git text conflicts. Ratification is all-or-nothing per run. There are no per-item heads, so two branches editing the same packet conflict at the file level.
mechanisms.why: It shows branch-scoped context promoted on an explicit commit point, similar to ContextDB's proposal -> publish. ContextDB could expose 'publish on merge' as a hook policy on top of CAS heads.

mechanisms.name: Kage: run state machine + verified-claim merge gate + PR check
mechanisms.how_it_works: contract.ts enforces LEGAL_TRANSITIONS: illegal transitions throw, every task.json write is atomic (temp+rename), and each transition is appended to a runs ledger. The verify step produces a ClaimRecord of checks that the kernel ran, not the agent. claimVerdict labels it VERIFIED / NOT VERIFIED / UNVERIFIED (static only). mergeRun requires the run to be ready/approved. prCheck (kage_pr_check, git hooks installed by kage) blocks a PR on hard-stale memory and on generated graphs whose stored head/tree/inputHash differ from the current ones (graphIsCurrent). preflight.ts gives a forecast-only blast radius before work.
mechanisms.evidence: mcp/delegation/contract.ts (20-93, 1087-1128), mcp/delegation/verify.ts claimVerdict (473-481), mcp/delegation/ratify.ts mergeRun, mcp/kernel.ts prCheck (19473+), mcp/delegation/preflight.ts, mcp/delegation/verify-lock.ts (machine-wide O_EXCL-style lockfile around check commands)
mechanisms.limitations: The gate covers merge/PR, not each agent action. It does not check that the context an agent read is still valid when it acts: there is no read certificate and no version vector. The graph-currency check is the closest thing (hash of inputs vs the stored artifact).
mechanisms.why: graphIsCurrent(head, tree, inputHash) is effectively a whole-repo certificate check at merge time. ContextDB generalizes it to per-read certificates checked at action time.

mechanisms.name: agents-remember: dual-revision ledger via Code-Commit git trailers
mechanisms.how_it_works: Each memory-content commit in the external memory repo carries a 'Code-Commit: <sha>' trailer, appended by render_memory_content_message, the one writer. derive_memory_ledger walks git rev-list from the memory tip, parses the last trailer block with %(trailers:key=Code-Commit,valueonly), and builds newest-first LedgerRow(code_commit, memory_commit) rows. Commits without a trailer produce no row. A row counts only if code_commit_exists in the code repo. memory.md is a disposable, gitignored cache of that derivation (refresh_memory_cache writes it atomically only when the bytes change). validate_ledger requires the first row to equal lastVerifiedCodeCommit/lastMemoryContentCommit. find_mapping(code_commit) answers 'which memory state was verified against this code commit'.
mechanisms.evidence: mcp/src/agents_remember/kernel/memory_attribution.py: CODE_COMMIT_TRAILER_KEY, render_memory_content_message, parse_code_commit_trailer, AttributedCommit.row; kernel/memory_cache.py: derive_memory_ledger, refresh_memory_cache, prepare_memory_cache; kernel/memory_ledger.py: MemoryLedger, validate_ledger, prepend_mapping, find_mapping, contains_mapping
mechanisms.limitations: The granularity is the whole repo (code commit to memory commit), not per item. The attribution is only as honest as the writer. Branch awareness comes from git ancestry, with no explicit per-branch heads. Mapping only goes from memory to code.
mechanisms.why: This is a clean, immutable answer to 'context revision R was verified against code revision C'. ContextDB can store code_commit on each revision/certificate, the same way, so certificates can be checked against HEAD.

mechanisms.name: agents-remember: citation claim reopen (structural fingerprints, report-only vs enforced)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Memory docs contain claims, each with anchors (a backticked identifier, a #heading, or a quoted literal) and citations path:start-end, plus a lastVerifiedCommitHash stamp. claim_change_router first proves the cheap case: when every cited path's git blob is unchanged from the stamp through HEAD and the working tree, the claim is 'proven-unchanged'. Otherwise it is 'semantic-required'. anchor_change resolves each anchor at the stamp and now, and compares structural fingerprints that ignore layout, comments, line numbers and delimiters. Results fall into three buckets. Invalid (0 or more than 1 matches): a hard provenance finding. Changed and not covered by a cited range: an enforced reopened claim. Changed but still exactly once inside a cited range: a 'surfaced' report-only finding for curator review. Mechanically projected ranges are enforced. Memory-relative citations use ledger-mapped memory history. Dependency citations compare locked requirement or npm versions. _gate_result returns enforced, surfaced and debt buckets.
mechanisms.evidence: mcp/src/agents_remember/memory_quality/style/citations/claim_reopen.py (module docstring 1-45, anchor_change 452-509, _anchor_in_cited_range 511, evaluate_claim 657-700, _gate_result 801-826); claim_change_router.py (RouteStatus proven-unchanged|semantic-required|error); model.py (Anchor, Citation, Claim); provenance.py (GitHistory, LockedVersion, requirement_versions, package_lock_versions)
mechanisms.limitations: It runs as a batch quality check over markdown docs, not as an online database. Claims are independent and do not propagate to other claims. The source admits it cannot detect a 'dishonest stamp' (verification advanced without review). It is heavy, using git history reads.
mechanisms.why: This is the most mature structural-vs-semantic split of the three. The exact/unique-resolution rule and the three-bucket outcome (broken / reopened / review-only) map directly onto ContextDB's structural validity giving PENDING with a reason. The cheap blob-equality fast path before semantic comparison is a good engineering pattern.

mechanisms.name: agents-remember: onboarding drift check (git blob-set fingerprints)
mechanisms.how_it_works: Each onboarding doc/entity records evidence paths and a fingerprint 'git-blob-set-v1' = sha256 over sorted 'path\0<git blob hash at ref>'. drift_check recomputes and classifies each source as up to date, drifted, missing verification, missing, orphaned, disabled or unsupported. Staged and unstaged local changes are reported separately (local_change_note). The MCP tool drift_check is described as a 'task-start gate'.
mechanisms.evidence: memory_quality/integrity/onboarding_drift_check/git_ops.py: compute_git_blob_set_fingerprint, git_blob_hash, local_change_note; models.py CLASSIFICATIONS/ACTIONABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS; drift.py classify_source; mcp/registration/memory.py drift_check
mechanisms.limitations: Whole-file blob granularity. Read-only reporting. It gates only by convention (agent instructions), not by enforcement.
mechanisms.why: Using git blob ids as content hashes avoids re-hashing and makes cross-branch comparisons cheap. A set-fingerprint fits a Pin dependency on a file set.

mechanisms.name: agents-remember: verified flock + thread RLock, atomic writes
mechanisms.how_it_works: exclusive_file_lock(resource) takes a per-resource threading.RLock and then fcntl.flock on a sibling '<name>.lock'. It supports same-thread reentrancy through a thread-local depth counter. On first use it probes that flock really excludes (two fds in one process; the second LOCK_NB must fail) and refuses NFS/SMB/WSL DrvFs with LockCapabilityError. atomic_write.py writes via temp+rename. Git provides the transaction semantics for memory content (closeout/integration commits).
mechanisms.evidence: mcp/src/agents_remember/kernel/file_lock.py: exclusive_file_lock, _verify_lock_capability, thread_mutex_for, lock_held; kernel/atomic_write.py
mechanisms.limitations: Pessimistic, single-host locking only. There is no CAS or version check on memory items; conflicts surface as git conflicts.
mechanisms.why: The lock-capability probe is a cheap safety check worth copying for any local single-host ContextDB deployment that relies on flock.

mechanisms.name: agents-remember: lifecycle_gate / gate_decide (structural gates on task documents)
mechanisms.how_it_works: An agent raises a gate of a given kind on its canonical task document, with ask, packet, required_decision and evidence_refs, and optionally waits. A parent or authorized role decides it with gate_decide. Zero or multiple open matches fail closed. Gate and lifecycle ids are never exposed to models; identity comes from ambient control-plane state. Git hooks (.githooks/_gate.sh) run deterministic checks pre-commit and pre-push.
mechanisms.evidence: mcp/src/agents_remember/mcp/registration/gates.py: lifecycle_gate, gate_decide, gate_list; .githooks/_gate.sh
mechanisms.readme_vs_code: implemented (gate plumbing); not tied to memory validity
mechanisms.limitations: These are human/parent approval gates. They do not check whether the context the agent relied on is still valid.
mechanisms.why: Orchestration approval, not data-validity gating. The fail-closed-on-ambiguous-match rule is the only reusable idea.

mechanisms.name: agent-memory-mcp: bitemporal supersession chain written in one transaction
mechanisms.how_it_works: MarkOutdated(id, reason, supersededBy) holds Store.writeMu and re-reads the row under the lock. It sets status 'superseded' (or 'outdated'), archived=true, valid_until=now, superseded_by, and caps importance at 0.25. If the successor exists it sets successor.valid_from=now, successor.replaces=id, and increments its referenced_by_count. Both rows are written in one SQL transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE through _txlock=immediate). A dangling successor id is tolerated: the pointer is recorded without a back-link. RecallAsOf(query, asOf) filters valid_from<=asOf<valid_until. knowledge_timeline orders related entries by valid_from.
mechanisms.evidence: internal/memory/write.go MarkOutdated (229-357); internal/memory/temporal.go RecallAsOf, isValidAt, SetTemporalFields (1-140); internal/memory/memory.go columns/indexes (57-59, 665-688); internal/dbutil/sqlite.go (WAL, busy_timeout, _txlock=immediate)
mechanisms.limitations: Rows are mutated in place; there are no immutable revisions. writeMu is per-process, so a second server process relies only on SQLite locking. There is no expected-version CAS: the last writer wins on update_memory. The validity interval is wall-clock, not tied to code commits. Supersession is not transitive (no dependents).
mechanisms.why: valid_from/valid_until plus the superseded_by/replaces pair in one transaction is the minimum correct form of supersession. ContextDB's head CAS should keep the as-of read but key it by revision/commit instead of time only.

mechanisms.name: agent-memory-mcp: steward drift scan (mtime vs last_verified_at)
mechanisms.how_it_works: DriftScan loads active memories, regex-extracts path references from content (extractPathRefs), and checks each path stays inside RootPath. A missing path gives source_missing (confidence 0.85, suggested action mark_outdated). File mtime > last_verified_at gives source_changed (0.70, verify). Entries not verified within the stale-days policy give stale_unverified. Findings go to the steward inbox. Policy may auto-apply actions; runs are serialized by runMu and a killswitch exists.
mechanisms.evidence: internal/steward/drift.go DriftScan (60-~170); internal/steward/steward.go Run/runMu (39-44, 132-138), applyAction, ResolveInbox; internal/steward/scanner_contradiction.go scanSemanticConflicts (embedding similarity >= 0.75 within subject groups)
mechanisms.limitations: mtime is a weak signal: a checkout or touch causes false positives and there is no content hash. Path refs are scraped from prose instead of declared. Reporting only, no propagation.
mechanisms.why: Kage's content/symbol hashes and agents-remember's blob fingerprints are strictly better. Keep only the inbox/suggested_action UX.

mechanisms.name: agent-memory-mcp: provenance-gated promotion to canonical
mechanisms.how_it_works: PromoteToCanonical(id, owner, verified) refuses with ErrPromotionRequiresVerification unless verified==true (a human or MCP review) or the memory's provenance is already trusted (verified/external). PromotionAllowed is the single predicate shared by dry-run and real paths so previews match writes. deriveTrust computes confidence from source type, lifecycle, owner, layer and last_verified_at.
mechanisms.evidence: internal/memory/write.go ErrPromotionRequiresVerification, PromotionAllowed, PromoteToCanonical (358-480); internal/memory/trust.go deriveTrust
mechanisms.limitations: It gates trust-level changes, not agent actions.
mechanisms.why: A memory-poisoning defense: ContextDB's publish of agent-originated facts into a shared head could require a provenance class. Sharing one predicate between preview and commit is a good discipline for certificate validation too.

mechanisms.name: Kage: token-bounded context block, stale packets withheld
mechanisms.how_it_works: boundContextBlock(block, budget) splits the assembled context by '## ' sections and keeps sections in priority order until estimateTokens fits, appending a trimmed note. Recall withholds hard-stale and content-changed packets and reports the suppression count. The brief compiler (delegation/brief.ts compileBrief) packs recalled memories with provenance (git author via one git log pass, delegation/provenance.ts) and the checks the run will be held to.
mechanisms.evidence: mcp/kernel.ts boundContextBlock (182-196), recallStaleReason usage; mcp/delegation/brief.ts compileBrief; mcp/delegation/provenance.ts packetProvenance
mechanisms.limitations: Greedy section-level trimming. The context returned to the agent carries no certificate or version.
mechanisms.why: ContextDB's certified read should return the packed block plus the set of (item, revision, validity) it depended on. Kage already computes the 'withheld because stale' list, which a certificate could carry.

analysis.overlap_with_contextdb: Partial, and only on the structural-staleness side. None of the three implements dependency-driven transitive invalidation. Kage, agents-remember and agent-memory-mcp all judge each memory item independently against code: Kage by file/symbol sha256, agents-remember by blob or structural fingerprints per claim, agent-memory-mcp by mtime. Memory-to-memory edges exist (Kage packet.edges superseded_by/supersedes/references_code, quality.contradicts; agent-memory-mcp superseded_by/replaces, referenced_by_count, multihop triples). None of them propagates invalidation along those edges, and there are no AND/OR justifications, no support counting, and no alternative support. Alternatives: only Kage's contradiction detection (detectContradictions, kernel.ts:3784) and agent-memory-mcp's embedding-based conflict scan, which flag pairs for a human to supersede one. Neither keeps several justifications for one belief. Versioning: all three mutate items in place. Kage and agents-remember lean on git history for immutability. agent-memory-mcp has bitemporal valid_from/valid_until. There are no logical heads with CAS anywhere. agent-memory-mcp uses an in-process mutex plus SQLite immediate transactions (last writer wins). Kage writes packet files with no lock and non-atomically. agents-remember uses flock plus git. Structural vs semantic: agents-remember's claim_reopen comes closest (proven-unchanged, then semantic-required, then invalid/reopened/surfaced-for-review). Kage has soft vs hard staleness and reverify-in-place. Neither has an explicit PENDING truth value. Action gating: Kage gates merge (run state machine, verified ClaimRecord, prCheck blocking on hard-stale memory and stale graph artifacts by head/tree/inputHash). agents-remember has human lifecycle gates. agent-memory-mcp gates canonical promotion on provenance. None issues read certificates or re-validates the context an agent used at the moment it acts.
analysis.could_contextdb_be_built_as_plugin_on_it: No, not as a plugin on any of them, but specific mechanisms are worth lifting. Kage (GPL-3.0, so copying code would force GPL on ContextDB; reimplement from the idea instead) keeps everything in one 22k-line kernel.ts. It has no storage abstraction for memory items: packets are files written in place without locks, StoreBackend only covers derived indexes, and there is no transaction or CAS layer to extend. agents-remember (MIT) is a large git-worktree orchestration system whose memory unit is a markdown document checked in batch. It suits lifting kernel/memory_attribution.py (Code-Commit trailer ledger), citations/claim_reopen.py and claim_change_router.py (structural claim fingerprints with a blob fast path), and kernel/file_lock.py, but not hosting a database. agent-memory-mcp (MIT, Go, SQLite) is the most database-like host: its memories table already has valid_from/valid_until/superseded_by/replaces and runs immediate transactions. ContextDB would still need immutable revision tables, a heads table with CAS, a justification/dependency edge table and a propagation engine, which amounts to a rewrite of the store layer. Recommended approach: build ContextDB standalone (SQLite + MCP). Adopt Kage's symbol-anchored fingerprint as the Cur/Pin code dependency type and its hard/soft tiers and PR-check gate shape. Adopt agents-remember's code-commit attribution on each revision/certificate and its three-bucket structural reopen logic. Adopt agent-memory-mcp's transactional supersede pair, as-of reads and provenance-gated promotion. Optionally ship adapters that import Kage packets and agents-remember ledgers.

verification.overlap_verdict: Confirmed. None of the three propagates invalidation along memory-to-memory edges. Kage judges each packet against code on its own (staleMemoryReasons, recallHardStaleReason, staleCatch). supersedeMemory only clears contradicts entries and never re-examines dependents. agents-remember evaluates each claim on its own (evaluate_claim). agent-memory-mcp's only 'cascade' is ON DELETE CASCADE storage cleanup of triples when a memory is deleted (memory.go:829-843, triples.go:194), which is not validity propagation. None of them has AND/OR justifications, support counting, logical heads with CAS, or read certificates checked at action time. Three corrections to the summary. (1) Kage's PR-time blocking runs in CI and through the 'kage pr check' CLI. The hooks Kage installs (post-commit/post-merge/post-checkout) only re-index, and the pre-commit/pre-push 'staleguard' is advisory (exit 0). (2) prCheck decides 'hard' with recallHardStaleReason (stored-fingerprint files all deleted, status, reports, TTL), not with the soft/hard classifier staleSeverity. (3) Kage does have some atomic writes: run task.json writes and packet status flips during ratification use temp+rename. Only the core packet writes (writeJson in supersede and reverify) are non-atomic and unlocked.

designs.strategy:
做一个独立产品：Rust 写的 counting-TMS 内核，完全按照 IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN 的 SD1-SD17 实现（base 与 head 无关、role×currency 四种边 Pin/Cur/Sem/Ref、每条 incidence 一个 sat 位、只在翻转时传播、L0/L1/L2 三层不动点、stateless 的 Sem 验证、certificate 依赖版本向量）。外面依次包上 SQLite 持久化（WAL，单 writer 线程）、本地守护进程、MCP server、Claude Code/Codex hooks。从已分析的项目里只移植 verdict 为 confirmed 或 partially 的机制，每一项都写明来源。

挑选规则如下。
(1) 证据权重排在 star 数前面。refuted 或只出现在 README 里的机制一律不用，包括：mem0 的 linked_memory_ids、hosted MCP 工具集；Hindsight 压缩后再注入 last_recall；cognee 的 improve MCP 工具；Tencent 的 memory-cleaner 对账和软删除；agent-memory 的 exactly-once；memory-graph 在 sqlite 上的版本化。
(2) 高 star 项目（mem0 67k、Hindsight 52k、OpenViking 40k、cognee/Graphiti 32k、Tencent 30k、Letta 25k、Dolt 25k）主要提供"产品外壳"：作用域、hook 接线、检索与打包、outbox、MCP 词汇、版本行与 head CAS。低 star 项目（Kage、agents-remember、deja-vu、brain0）概念上最接近，主要提供代码锚点失效和 provenance 的细节。
(3) 所有被借用的机制都要按 ContextDB 的语义改写：删除改成 RetractBase 或移动 head，因果失效改成 STALE 或 PENDING 而不是删掉，last-writer-wins 改成 mandatory CAS，只读日志改成可在行动时校验的 certificate。

产品定位是给多个编码 agent 共用的、带认证的上下文库。agent 读到的每条上下文都附带 (logical, revision, status) 和一个 certificate。在 PreToolUse 时校验这个 certificate，回答"我依赖的东西还成立吗？"。

关于"整合 ultracode"：本机 ~/Dev 和 ContextDB 目录里都没有找到名为 ultracode 的代码库。所以我把 ultracode 理解为这个整合产品的代号或品牌名。如果它其实指某个已有的代码库，需要你提供路径，再规划怎么接入。
designs.pitch: ContextDB（产品代号 ultracode）是给 Claude Code、Codex 等多个编码 agent 共用的一个上下文数据库。每条事实、决策、计划和代码锚点都存成不可变 revision，logical head 只能通过 CAS 移动。它们之间的依赖带类型（Pin/Cur/Sem/Ref），并且有 AND/OR 理由。前提一变，依赖它的条目会被精确标记：结构上失效的标 STALE，需要重新语义确认的标 PENDING，不会被误删。如果某个结论还有其他理由支撑，它会保持有效（CurrentViaAlternative）。agent 读上下文时拿到一个 certificate，执行动作前由 PreToolUse hook 校验。我们核查过的 13 个项目（合计约 32 万 star）里，没有一个同时做到依赖驱动的传递失效、support counting、PENDING 和行动时认证这四件事。

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Scope lanes: repo/dir/user/session lanes. The shared lane is project + repo; the personal lane is user + repo. Every ancestor directory is tagged into a dirs chain, and wildcard identities are rejected.
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (note: the dir scope narrows only the shared lane)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Becomes the scope layer above logicals: every logical carries scope_lane and dirs[]. ctx_recall filters by lane, and wildcards are refused so a query cannot accidentally widen its scope. Shared-vs-personal visibility then feeds Authorized(principal, r) in SD11.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Idempotent, content-addressed client outbox. Hook events land in local SQLite. Flushes run under BEGIN IMMEDIATE with packet_id = sha256(repo|session|start|end) and INSERT OR IGNORE, retries are bounded, and crashed flushes are recovered.
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Each hook process writes its events to ~/.contextdb/outbox.sqlite and exits. The daemon consumes them asynchronously and keys each commit by packet_id, so a crash or compaction never yields duplicate revisions. Delivery is at-least-once and dedup makes the result idempotent. This is the honest version of the claim; agent-memory's exactly-once claim was refuted.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Capturing git_sha / branch / repo provenance per session (mem0 records it but never validates it)
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (the data actually flows to the hosted Platform path)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: SessionStart pins repo, branch and HEAD. Every revision an agent writes automatically gets a Pin dependency on that session's CodeAnchor revision. When HEAD diverges, the observer moves the anchor head and Pin-strict marks downstream revisions STALE(SupersededPinnedPremise). This adds the validation step mem0 is missing.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Hybrid scoring (semantic + BM25 sigmoid + entity boost) and a per-session injection ledger
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (the ledger uses INSERT OR IGNORE and keeps stale first-injection text, which we fix)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Retrieval reuses the scoring formula as-is. The ledger is upgraded to record (session, logical, revision, layer, epoch), so it becomes the certificate's read-set; replaying it can detect that context injected earlier has since changed.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Retracted-grounding detection: a MEMORY_BACKED allowlist, an 'unresolvable = all citations missing → treat as broken link' guard, and skip_if_in_flight to coalesce refreshes
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: The import path uses the unresolvable guard: when every premise of an imported rule is missing, it is reported as a broken import, not a retraction. The LLM revalidation queue uses skip_if_in_flight. The allowlist decides which kinds of premise are allowed to resolve against which tables.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Two-phase prepare-then-commit: slow LLM/embedding work runs with no connection open; a short transaction then re-reads, validates, and either commits or discards (internal OCC on updated_at, text-CAS)
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (internal OCC confirmed; the public API is last-writer-wins)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Semantic validator workers run the LLM outside the writer. On submit they carry the curvec they validated against, and the single writer rechecks curvec == current head vector inside the transaction before writing the ValidationRecord. On mismatch they re-prepare, in line with SD10 (VR is keyed by (RuleId, curvec)).

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Hybrid recall with RRF (k=60), cross-encoder rerank and a max_tokens budget; retain/recall/reflect-style MCP verbs
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (MCP tool count partially: 39)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: ctx_recall fuses the FTS5 and vector arms with RRF and takes a token budget. Status is a hard filter before ranking: certified mode returns only CERTIFIED items, and other statuses are returned as tagged items.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: OperationValidatorExtension hook shape: accept / reject / accept_with(enrichment), plus a precheck-before-parse split
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: The write admission policy layer and the PreToolUse decision API both use this three-way result: allow, deny with a reason, or allow while injecting a <=480B warning or a refreshed context delta.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Upward summary freshness: semantic_body_digest early cutoff + pending_child_changes counter + ratio threshold MARK_PENDING
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Applied only to derived artifacts such as summaries and embeddings, not to belief validity. When a derived summary's inputs change, the content digest decides whether to propagate upward. The PENDING state is surfaced on read, which OpenViking does not do. The idea is reimplemented, because OpenViking is AGPL.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: RefStore::cas_update(expected=None means create-only), returning ConcurrentCommit to the caller, with the order: swap the ref first, then run side effects
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (mechanism confirmed; locking happens in the Python layer)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Head API semantics: expected_head=None means create_only. A CAS failure returns PreconditionFailed{expected,current} without retrying. Projections (FTS, vectors, markdown export) update only after the commit succeeds.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Tiered, budgeted context assembly (L0 abstract → L1 overview → L2 body, per-type quotas) with a cross-turn recall ledger cooldown
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Default packing policy for ctx_recall. Every item in a packed block carries its revision and status, and the ledger records the tier actually served, so the certificate covers only content that was really served.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: ResourceDiff IndexState enum with strict precedence (ABSENT/COMPLETE/MISSING/PARTIAL/STALE/OBSOLETE/ORPHAN/LEVEL_CONFLICT)
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Tracks embedding and FTS projection health. It is kept as a separate dimension from belief validity (L0/L1/L2) and drives rebuild-and-repair.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Refcounted multi-owner source refs with idempotent, ordered deletes: vectors first, then detach refs from surviving artifacts, then delete unowned artifacts
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (key format and step-3 details corrected; mechanism real)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Confirms in production that OR support counting works. Derived-index cleanup follows the same order: derived projection first, then source records, with every step idempotent. The kernel itself never deletes; it only flips S.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Read-set recording plus fixpoint propagation: each QA turn stores used_graph_element_ids; on deletion, invalidation follows turn → feedback → lesson → later turns to a fixpoint
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (fires only on hard delete; deletes instead of marking)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Strong evidence that certified reads are necessary (COG-5835: an answer cited deleted facts). ContextDB turns it into a precise version: the session read-set is pinned by revision, and propagation runs through the justification DAG and marks STALE or PENDING rather than deleting.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Write a review_pending marker first and clear it last (crash-safe asynchronous semantic review)
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (date-conflict handling downgrades to 'conflicting' instead of rejecting)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: A validator job writes a job record with state=launching before calling the LLM and clears it when the ValidationRecord commits. After a crash, the leftover marker is found and the job is retried.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: PROV-O audit vocabulary (used_entities, derived_from, supersedes, invalidated_by/reason) with a hash-chained checksum ledger
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (opt-in, invalidate() has no production caller; the chain itself works)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: The append-only op log gets a previous_checksum chain for tamper evidence and export uses the PROV-O field names. Unlike cognee, the dependency fields here really drive propagation.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Persisting the 'invalidated by' link: Graphiti computes an invalidated_by map but never stores it, so the invalidated fact cannot be restored once its invalidator is retracted
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (the gap is confirmed)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Supersession is an explicit SetHead plus a head-history row, and contradiction is a persisted Conflict artifact. Retracting the invalidator or rolling the head back (SD12 allows ABA) automatically restores the old state.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: LLM contradiction candidates (two hybrid searches: same endpoint pair + group-wide) followed by a deterministic interval-overlap rule
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (the rule silently does nothing when valid_at is missing; the exact-text fast path skips the check)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Used as a candidate generator for Sem conflicts. Uncertain verdicts go to PENDING or a Conflict artifact, never FALSE. The prompt design for contradicted_facts is reused. Valid time remains a v0 non-goal (SD16) and is stored only as metadata.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: OR support counted over source episodes: remove_episode deletes a fact only when no supporting episode remains
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Confirms that 'keep the fact while support > 0' is something people actually use. Generalized to AND/OR rules plus flip-only propagation per SD3.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Immutable version rows with an is_head flag, a partial unique index (WHERE is_head=1) so only one live head exists, a content_hash no-op, and copy-on-write version blob directories
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (the SQLite path is confirmed; delete is now physical and the Mongo path can drop concurrent writes)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: The SQLite schema uses a partial unique index as a backstop for the single-head invariant. Identical content is a no-op that returns the existing revision. Delete is never physical (it is RetractBase or a head move), avoiding Tencent's mistake.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: expected_version optimistic lock (SKILL_VERSION_STALE 40901)
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (the check is check-then-act outside the transaction; only the SQLite unique constraint acts as a backstop)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Every agent write must carry expected_head or create_only. The compare happens inside the single-writer transaction (UPDATE heads ... WHERE rev=?), not as a TOCTOU check.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Proxy-layer session version pinning: pin the first version read; inject the pinned version into later reads and inject expected_version into writes
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (two backends; the COS-KV backend has no TTL; no pinning when unconfigured)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Generalized into the certificate. The set of revisions a session has read is its pin vector, PreToolUse checks it, and the daemon actively pushes 'pin is stale' (Tencent gives no notification).

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Memory generation log: input_refs → output_refs plus prompt {id, version, sha256}
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (write-only audit)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Rules derived by an LLM and ValidationRecords carry prompt_sha256 and model, which makes derivations reproducible. Unlike Tencent, the inputs become indexed premise incidences.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Permission order: owner > membership > visibility (private/team/restricted/agent/task) > role default > allow-only ACL, with agents as ACL subjects
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (governs metadata assets only)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Baseline implementation of Authorized(principal, r) in M3. UNAVAILABLE has the highest precedence (SD13) and returns no payload and no WHY.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Revision-pinned compiled context: record memfsRevision; when only memory changed, append a <memory_update> delta message instead of rewriting the system prompt, which keeps the prompt cache
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (LocalBackend only)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: UserPromptSubmit compares the session read-set with current status. If anything changed, it injects a <context_update> delta listing which revisions went STALE or PENDING and what replaced them, without rewriting the whole context. This saves tokens and keeps the cache.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Token-fenced idempotent claims keyed by a state signature (pid liveness, token-checked transitions)
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (single-slot marker)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Background revalidation jobs are deduplicated with claim key (rule_id, curvec), so the same PENDING state never triggers repeated LLM calls. The job table holds one row per key instead of Letta's single slot.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: A pid + process start-time fenced O_EXCL file lease, reaped only after the owner is dead
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (post-turn sync uses no-wait claim; repair has its own lock)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Ownership lease for the contextdbd daemon and its WAL, so only one daemon runs per data directory. Combined with agents-remember's flock capability probe, it refuses network filesystems.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Pre-commit declarative policy gate (protected read_only fields, readOnlyFiles globs, size and depth budgets)
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Write admission policy (.contextdb/policy.toml) checked inside the single writer, so it cannot be bypassed with --no-verify. It is kept separate from the semantic validity machinery.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: memory_updated{affected_paths} change feed plus point-in-time reads (memory_file_at_ref)
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: ctx_changes(since_epoch) and a subscription stream push status-change diffs (final vs pre-txn per SD8). ctx_read(rev) gives point-in-time reads.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Atomic multi-dataset CAS: CommitDatasets with an ExpectedHead/NotEqual precondition per dataset, rechecked on every retry
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (function-style preconditions are single-dataset only; the two are never combined)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: ctx_commit takes a batch of operations with an expected_head per head. Because the system has a single writer, ContextDB can do what Dolt does not combine: multi-head CAS plus certificate read-set validation in one atomic step.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Classified three-way merge ops (one-sided / convergent / divergent-resolved / divergent-conflict / delete-conflict), a pluggable RowMergePolicy, and merge-base --all
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Used for M2 branch merges. After the structural merge, the justification/dependency re-propagation runs, which Dolt does not do.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Conflicts and violations persisted as versioned artifacts that block commits
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Conflict, PENDING validations and invariant violations are stored as artifacts keyed by (revision, type, info_hash). In the L2 gate, Conflicted(r) blocks CERTIFIED.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Single-writer actor (mpsc + oneshot), a partial unique index for one is_latest per key, a precondition_failed error carrying expected/current, claim-once handoff (UPDATE ... WHERE state='open'), and as_of windows closed on every retirement path
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (correction: page writes take the shared mutation_lock plus a per-path mutex)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: The core of the persistence layer: all mutations go to one OS thread that owns the rusqlite writer, and reads use separate connections. ctx_handoff_begin/accept follows the claim-once pattern, and accept also revalidates the certificate attached to the handoff. Head-history windows are closed in the same transaction.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Write-time contradiction candidates: top-5 nearest neighbors with cosine >= 0.95 and text divergence >= 0.2; a guarded supersede UPDATE ... WHERE superseded_by IS NULL
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: A cheap candidate generator that writes Conflict artifacts and marks both revisions disputed or PENDING. The supersede path insert-and-moves the head in a single transaction instead of mcp-memory-service's two-phase saga.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Asymmetric 'files moved since' check: git log --since over the files a session touched; 'changed' is certain, silence means UNKNOWN, and the work runs under a budget
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: The cheap path for the CodeAnchor observer. A detected change moves the anchor head. Missing information never produces a claim of 'unchanged'; it maps to the UNKNOWN/PENDING variant reserved by SD14.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: PreToolUse injects a single line of at most 480 bytes, only for the file or command the tool is acting on
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (advisory, never denies)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Payload limit for ContextDB's PreToolUse output: a decision plus a reason of at most 480 bytes. The difference is that ContextDB can return deny or ask.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Evidence-time admission rules: valid_from must not be later than the cited evidence; an LLM may only reference handles from the sheet it was given; unsupported email addresses are rejected
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Write-time checks: rules derived by an LLM may only use premise revisions from the certificate read-set it received, which blocks hallucinated dependencies and memory poisoning.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Content-hash idempotent revision ids, a blake3 content-addressed payload store with crypto-shred tombstones, declared-vs-done drift, a pure policy evaluator exposed as a CLI exit-code gate, and Ed25519 in-toto attestations
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (attestations partially: the code is real)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Revision bodies go into a blake3 CAS; topology stays immutable while bodies can be purged. A certificate's declared write-set is diffed against the actual write-set after the action, giving a drift score. `ctxdb cert verify` can be a git pre-commit hook or CI step. In M3, certificates can be signed in in-toto format.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Symbol-anchored content fingerprints: whole-file sha256 plus span hashes of symbols that the text names and that resolve uniquely
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (TS/JS only; byte-level hashes)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Revision content for the CodeAnchor logical kind is (path, symbol, span_hash). A memory's Pin/Cur premise points to a symbol-level anchor revision, which is finer-grained than file-level. Reimplemented, because Kage is GPL.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Three-bucket claim reopen: a blob-equality fast path, then a structural fingerprint that ignores layout and comments; unique resolution → invalid / enforced-reopen / surfaced-for-review
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: The observer's precise path. Blob unchanged means no action. A broken anchor means STALE. A change outside the cited range means a new anchor head (Cur → STALE). A change only inside the cited range goes through Sem to PENDING for review. This lowers false positives from byte-level hashing.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Code-Commit trailer ledger (memory commit ↔ code commit)
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (the existence check runs only in some callers)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Every revision and certificate stores code_commit, so ctx_cert_check can answer 'was this verified against the current HEAD?'. Commit trailers are written when the markdown/git mirror is exported.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Provenance-gated promotion: one shared predicate PromotionAllowed used by both dry-run and the real write
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: Putting an agent-originated revision on a shared-lane head (AssertBase) requires a trusted provenance class or explicit verification. Certificate checks and their dry-run preview share one predicate, so the preview always matches the real result.

rejected_mechanisms: mem0 linked_memory_ids supersession links: the OSS code never reads the field, and the prompt asks for UUIDs while only giving the model integer ids, so it is broken in two places (refuted).
mem0 hosted Platform MCP tool set: appears only in the README/docs, so it cannot count as a proven mechanism.
mem0 update(): overwrites in place plus a side history log, with no cross-store transaction. This is the anti-pattern ContextDB replaces.
Hindsight 'post-compaction re-injection of last_recall': last_recall.json is written but never read (refuted). ContextDB replaces it with Letta's delta mechanism.
Hindsight delete_stale_observations as the propagation semantics: one hop, deletes when any single source is lost, and does no support counting. Only its lock-ordering detail is kept.
Hindsight proof_count as a support counter: verification shows it is only a roughly 5% rerank boost and does not decide survival.
OpenViking memory replacement = delete + write that re-points the old links to the replacement: trust is silently transferred, which is the opposite of the Pin/Cur semantics.
OpenViking PathLock as a correctness primitive: it has no fencing token, so a paused holder can still write after takeover. Leases are only for work distribution and need an epoch fence added.
OpenViking MCP edit as read-then-write: no precondition, so updates can be lost.
cognee improve as an MCP tool: it is not registered (refuted).
cognee skill _apply_proposal: stores old_procedure but never compares it on apply. This is the counter-example of 'looks like review but detects no conflict'.
cognee process-local asyncio dataset locks: documented as not cross-process.
Graphiti 'expired edges filtered by default' / 'current = expired_at IS NULL': search and the MCP tools do no such filtering (refuted), and MCP cannot even filter on expired_at.
Graphiti MERGE ... SET r = edge full overwrite: last-writer-wins with no version.
Graphiti handle_multiple_group_ids as general namespace isolation: in fact FalkorDB-only routing (partially refuted).
TencentDB 'delete = soft archive': now a physical delete of every version (refuted).
TencentDB 'memory-cleaner periodically reconciles JSONL with the vector store': only deletes by age (refuted).
TencentDB L1 destructive supersession: hard-deletes the old row and issues a new id, with no supersedes link.
TencentDB JEV as a validity gate: it can only trigger regeneration early and never vetoes (partially refuted). Only its label taxonomy is kept as validator output.
TencentDB Mongo appendVersion: returns the existing v+1 row, which silently loses a concurrent write.
TencentDB profile sync in the gateway write path: rereads the current version as the baseline, so the CAS is effectively last-writer-wins.
Letta V1 Block version_id_col plus linear undo that truncates future history: clients cannot pass an expected version and history is destructively truncated. Letta itself retired it.
Letta whole-repo HEAD SHA as the dependency granularity: too coarse for the item-level semantics.
Dolt CommitHook as a veto point: its errors are explicitly ignored by the caller.
Dolt prolly trees implemented in v1: high complexity; SQLite revision rows are enough at this scale.
Embedding Dolt as the storage substrate: a heavy Go/MySQL dependency, its single-root CAS serializes every ref update, and whole-database branches do not map to scoped alternatives.
agent-memory (tigerless) exactly-once ingestion: actually at-least-once (refuted).

agent-memory memory_correct in-place body rewrite: it bypasses _enforce_update_only, so the 'force a successor when the fact changes' rule must be enforced on every path, which agent-memory fails to do.
agent-memory untyped links validated only at write time: they go stale silently.
agent-memory-mcp drift scan on mtime: checkout and touch cause false positives. Kage and agents-remember fingerprints are strictly better.
memory-graph 'version' field: never incremented on the sqlite backend, and bi-temporal valid_until has no code path that updates it.
memory-graph observe-only anti-gating stance: opposite to the product's direction. It is kept only as a warning that gating must be fail-open configurable.
neo4j-labs/agent-memory ontology update max+1 revision numbering: a race with no uniqueness constraint.
Kage staleguard as a hard gate: pre-commit/pre-push is advisory with exit 0; only pr check in CI blocks.
Kage writing packet files with writeJson: non-atomic and unlocked, so a supersede can be left half done.
mcp-memory-service belief contradiction input: storage has no .graph and get_edges is undefined, so it is dead code.

mcp-memory-service HLC sync as the head-move resolution: per-field LWW. Head moves must use CAS or alternatives. HLC is only for future replication of immutable events, and UNIQUE(agent_id, event_id) does not dedup when agent_id is NULL.
designs.architecture:
Process model (single machine, co-located; this follows B13 and avoids PlanFence's centralized-link penalty):

1) contextdbd daemon, one per data directory, normally ~/.contextdb/<workspace>.
- Ownership: Letta-style pid+start-time lease plus the agents-remember flock capability probe; refuses NFS/SMB.
- Inside it: the Rust kernel holds all state in memory, using IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN §5's compact layout, counting propagation (§6.2) and Pearce-Kelly rank (§6.3).
- One writer OS thread owns the rusqlite writer connection, after ai-memory. Commit flow: staged ops → validation, CAS and cycle checks → net-delta propagation → append the op log in one SQLite transaction → publish the diff.
- Readers serve MCP and hook queries from a snapshot (epoch) with no lock.

2) Persistence: SQLite WAL with an append-only op log as the source of truth.
- On startup the kernel is rebuilt by replaying the log, with periodic snapshot checkpoints to speed this up. This moves the M4 persistence work earlier, in the simplest possible form.
- The op log carries a cognee-style previous_checksum hash chain.
- Revision bodies are stored in a blake3 content-addressed payload store (brain0) that supports purge tombstones.
- Derived projections can be rebuilt: FTS5, an optional vector index (sqlite-vec), markdown/git mirror export with Code-Commit trailers (agents-remember/Letta). Projection health uses the OpenViking IndexState enum.

3) contextdb-oracle: the naive least-fixpoint oracle (§6.4). It is used for exact counter comparison in debug and test builds. In production it can run as a sampling self-check (`ctxdb doctor`).

4) Code anchor observer, a daemon subtask.
- On git events (post-commit / post-checkout / post-merge hooks plus fs watch) it runs: deja-vu-style git log --since cheap detection → agents-remember blob fast path → Kage symbol span hash and structural fingerprint.
- It writes new revisions for CodeAnchor logicals and runs SetHead. Downstream Cur premises become STALE, Pin-strict produces STALE(SupersededPinnedPremise), and Sem goes to PENDING.
- Asymmetric honesty: missing information is never treated as 'unchanged'.

5) Semantic validator worker pool, separate processes.
- Uses the host CLI or API as the LLM.
- Jobs are claimed with a token fence keyed by (rule_id, curvec) (Letta) and recorded marker-first (cognee).
- Work is prepared outside the writer and the curvec is CAS-checked on submit (Hindsight).
- Candidates come from Graphiti / mcp-memory-service contradiction generators. Output is a ValidationRecord with prompt_sha256 (Tencent).
- Dry-run by default with per-run caps (agent-memory Manage / neo4j agent-memory consolidation).

6) MCP server, Rust rmcp: stdio, plus loopback HTTP protected by a token with 0600 permissions (Kage delegation guard pattern).

7) `ctxdb hook <event>`: a short-lived Rust binary called by Claude Code / Codex hooks.
- Writes events to the local outbox SQLite (mem0 pattern) or calls the daemon synchronously for PreToolUse decisions.
- The daemon being unavailable is configured as fail-open (default warn) or fail-closed.

Language: everything is Rust; the hooks are a single static binary that starts fast. The implementation adopts no code from AGPL/GPL projects (OpenViking, Kage); only their ideas are reimplemented.
designs.data_model_and_api:
SQLite tables (truth = op_log; everything else is materialized from it or derived):
- op_log(epoch, seq, op_blob, principal, prev_checksum, checksum)
- logicals(id, kind ∈ {Fact, Decision, Plan, Summary, CodeAnchor, Evidence}, scope_lane, dirs_json, created_epoch)
- revisions(id, logical_id, payload_ref blake3, content_hash, code_commit, author_principal, created_epoch, adopt_as_base_bit). Content hash makes ids idempotent (brain0); identical content is a no-op (Tencent/ai-memory).
- heads(logical_id PK, rev_id, epoch), plus head_history(logical_id, rev_id, from_epoch, to_epoch). A partial unique index is the backstop.
- base(rev_id)
- rules(id, concl_rev, enabled, flags RECURSIVE reserved, canonical_hash, prompt_sha256?), plus incidences(rule_id, premise_rev, kind ∈ {Pin, Cur, Sem, Ref}). Normalized per SD6; append-only per SD4.
- validation_records(rule_id, curvec_hash, curvec_json, verdict, validator, prompt_sha256, epoch)
- artifacts(rev_id, type ∈ {Conflict, PendingReview, PolicyViolation}, info_hash, payload) (Dolt)
- sessions(id, harness, repo, branch, head_sha, principal)
- read_ledger(session_id, logical_id, rev_id, layer, epoch, tier). Upgrades the mem0/OpenViking ledger.
- certificates(id, session_id, pin_vector_json, epoch, code_commit, strict_no_aba, signature?)
- jobs(claim_key, token, state, pid, started)
- handoffs(id, owner, state open|accepted|cancelled, cert_id, summary)

The client outbox is a separate SQLite file: events(id, packet_id UNIQUE, ...).

MCP tools (names stay close to familiar mem0/Hindsight/Graphiti/ai-memory verbs):
- ctx_recall(query, scope{lane, dir?}, budget_tokens, mode: certified|all, tiers) → {items:[{logical, rev, status: CERTIFIED|PENDING|STALE{reason}|CONFLICTED, dims{semantic, currency}, tier, snippet}], certificate_id, withheld:[...]}
- ctx_read(logical | rev, level: abstract|overview|full) → also appended to the read-set.
- ctx_put(logical? | new{kind, scope}, content, deps:[{rev, kind: Pin|Cur|Sem|Ref}] (no default kind), expected_head | create_only (required), adopt_as_base: bool (required)) → {rev, epoch} | PreconditionFailed{expected, current} | CycleDetected{op_index, path} | DuplicateRule{existing, enabled}
- ctx_commit(ops[]) is the batched, atomic multi-head version. Ops: AddRevision, SetHead(CAS), AssertBase, RetractBase, AddRule, SetRuleEnabled, Rebind, AddValidation. Optional with_cert: the read-set is rechecked in the same transaction.
- ctx_validate(rule_id | rev, verdict, evidence, curvec_seen)
- ctx_why(rev) / ctx_why_not(rev, depth)  (SD15)
- ctx_cert_check(cert_id | pin_vector, strict_no_aba?) → {valid, per_item:[{rev, status, current_via_alternative, replaced_by?}], code_commit_match}
- ctx_changes(since_epoch, scope) and subscribe → status diffs (Letta memory_updated pattern)
- ctx_handoff_begin / ctx_handoff_accept (claim-once; accept revalidates the cert)
- ctx_conflicts / ctx_resolve (resolve = SetHead or SetRuleEnabled, never a delete)

Hook contract (Claude Code / Codex JSON stdin/stdout):
- SessionStart: register the session; pin repo/branch/HEAD to the CodeAnchor; inject a certified briefing that respects the budget.
- UserPromptSubmit: compare the session read-set with current status; when something changed, inject a <context_update> delta (Letta); auto-recall.
- PreToolUse(Edit|Write|Bash|...): derive the certificate from the read_ledger and run cert_check.
  - Return permissionDecision: allow; ask/deny plus a reason of at most 480 bytes (deja-vu); or allow plus additionalContext.
  - Policy is configurable per tool and per path. Default is warn (fail-open), and strict mode denies.
  - Shares one predicate with dry-run (agent-memory-mcp).
- PostToolUse: record the files actually touched and diff them against the declared write-set (brain0 drift); file reads go into the read-set as Ref/Cur hints (OpenViking experience lineage, transcript-derived).
- Stop / SubagentStop / PreCompact / SessionEnd: flush the outbox; create a handoff.

CLI: `ctxdb cert verify` exits nonzero on failure, so it can be used in a git pre-commit hook or CI (brain0 / Kage pr check).
designs.differentiation:
Based on the verified overlap verdicts, none of the analyzed projects does the following:
(1) Dependency-driven transitive invalidation combined with OR support counting. The closest cases each miss part of it:
- cognee's session fixpoint fires only on hard delete, and it deletes instead of marking anything.
- Hindsight's one-hop sweep deletes the observation as soon as any single source is lost.
- OpenViking propagates only along the directory tree.
- brain0's blast_radius BFS produces only a risk scalar.
- neo4j agent-memory's r.support counter only increases.
- Graphiti's episode support is one hop and has no un-invalidation.
(2) A PENDING state orthogonal to structural validity, with the L0/L1/L2 three-layer fixpoint. The rest of the field uses a single state, or makes a binary LLM decision, or deletes the item outright. Tencent JEV is only an early trigger, and Kage soft/hard is recomputed ad hoc and never persisted.
(3) Mandatory CAS on per-item logical heads, plus atomic multi-head commits with read-set validation in the same transaction. mem0, cognee, Graphiti, OpenViking and the Hindsight public API are all LWW. Tencent's CAS is TOCTOU and covers skills only. ai-memory's CAS is optional and single-key. Dolt has multi-head CAS and per-head validation functions, but cannot combine them.
(4) A certified read whose certificate is validated at action time (PreToolUse). The projects that have a PreToolUse hook (OpenViking uri-guard, deja-vu) only route or inject, Letta gates only by path and identity, and Tencent's pinning is limited to skills and never notifies anyone.
(5) Code dependencies as first-class versioned premises. mem0, brain0 and agents-remember capture git_sha or reads, and Kage fingerprints each item on its own. Nobody connects code changes into a propagating dependency graph.
(6) Correct restore after a supersession is undone: retracting the invalidator or an ABA head move restores the previous state. Graphiti's invalidated_by is not persisted, so it cannot do this.
mvp_scope: Kernel per IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN M0+M1a: contextdb-model / core / oracle. SD1-SD17 semantics, counting propagation with net delta and rank-ordered pops, Pearce-Kelly cycle detection, L0/L1/L2 layering, WHY/WHY_NOT, and exact counter comparison against the oracle (golden tests T06a-d, T07a-e, T15/b/c, T16b, T29).

SQLite persistence: append-only op log as the source of truth plus snapshot replay; a single writer thread (ai-memory); a partial unique index as the head backstop; mandatory expected_head/create_only that returns PreconditionFailed{expected,current}; blake3 payload store.
contextdbd daemon with an ownership lease (Letta) and the flock capability probe (agents-remember).

MCP server with: ctx_recall (FTS5 + optional vectors, RRF, token budget, tiered packing, status annotations), ctx_read, ctx_put, ctx_commit, ctx_validate, ctx_why, ctx_why_not, ctx_cert_check, ctx_changes.
Session read_ledger that records revisions, giving automatic certificate generation.

Claude Code hook package (Codex version in parallel): SessionStart briefing, UserPromptSubmit <context_update> delta, PreToolUse certificate check (warn by default, strict optional, payload at most 480B), PostToolUse to record touched and read files, Stop/PreCompact to flush the client outbox (idempotent by packet_id).
CodeAnchor v1: file-level git blob plus git log --since detection, and symbol span hashes for TS/JS only. The observer moves anchor heads, which drives Cur and Pin-strict propagation.
Scope lanes (repo/dir/user/session, with wildcards rejected).
A manual semantic validation path (ctx_validate). The LLM validator ships as an optional dry-run worker that only writes PendingReview artifacts and never automatically writes a Rejected verdict.
`ctxdb cert verify` CLI (usable in pre-commit or CI) and `ctxdb doctor` (oracle sampling self-check).
roadmap: Phase 0 (about 2 weeks): M0 formal contract plus the oracle-backed store, with docs/SEMANTICS.md written in full. The kernel API is frozen but the internals can change.

Phase 1 (about 3 weeks): M1a incremental counting kernel plus SQLite op log, single writer and daemon. Exit gate: bounded exhaustive testing and proptest show zero counter mismatches against the oracle.

Phase 2 (about 3 weeks, product alpha): MCP server, Claude Code/Codex hooks, read_ledger certificates, CodeAnchor observer v1, scope lanes. Internal dogfooding of several agents working in parallel on one repo, measuring stale-action interceptions and the false-deny rate.

Phase 3 (in parallel with Phase 2, M1b/M1.5): baseline modes (RevokeAll / TypedMaxLattice / NaiveBfs / DD), and the H2/H3 experiments with conformance suites taken from PlanFence, MemTX and CoMemBench, to support the paper's claims.

Phase 4: semantic validator worker pool (prepare-then-CAS, claim dedup, marker-first, prompt_sha256), Graphiti/mcp-memory-service-style contradiction candidate generation into Conflict artifacts, handoff begin/accept with certificates, and declared-vs-done drift.

Phase 5 (M2): branches and what-if. Worktree-style branches with typed merge outcomes (Letta), Dolt DiffOp three-way merge, merge-base, and re-propagation after merge. The BRANCH_ONLY currency dimension.
Phase 6 (M3): principal / ACL (Tencent's ordering), the UNAVAILABLE precedence, provenance-gated AssertBase (agent-memory-mcp), Ed25519 in-toto signed certificates (brain0), and strict_no_aba.

Phase 7 (ecosystem): mem0/Hindsight/Graphiti-compatible API shims; importers (Kage packets, agent-memory markdown, mcp-memory-service lineage); markdown/git mirror export; a TencentDB MemoryProxy injector plus a tool_use validator adapter.

Phase 8 (scale and replication): Postgres backend using Hindsight's sorted lock ordering and SKIP LOCKED job queue; cross-machine replication of immutable events (deja-vu acknowledged watermarks plus content-key dedup, HLC used only for events, never for resolving head moves); V1 dynamic SCC (SD17).
risks: Agents won't declare dependencies (undeclared dependency, m6). Dependencies have to be derived largely from the read-set and transcripts (OpenViking lineage, brain0 reads), and their precision directly limits invalidation recall. Mitigation: auto-generate Ref/Cur hints, have the PreToolUse warning show what is missing, and report statistics on undeclared reads.

Gating friction: memory-graph's explicit anti-gating stance shows that users resist memory blocking their actions. False denies would get the product uninstalled. Mitigation: default to warn, apply strict only to configured paths and tools, have the CurrentViaAlternative path reduce replans, and track the legitimate-action allow rate as a core metric.

Novelty and prior art: PlanFence, MemTX, PACMI, Graphiti and Letta already cover much of the concept (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN §2.1). The product story has to rest on the measurable deltas in §2.2, not on vague 'TMS for agents' claims.

Byte-level fingerprint false positives (formatting changes, regenerated files): Kage's limitation applies. Mitigation: the agents-remember structural fingerprint and the 'change inside the cited range → PENDING instead of STALE' bucket. Languages other than TS/JS fall back to file level at first.

LLM validator cost, nondeterminism and poisoning: mitigated with claim dedup, caps, dry-run by default, the evidence handle allowlist, and provenance-gated promotion, but semantic correctness still cannot be guaranteed.

Moving persistence earlier than the plan's M4, and op-log replay time growing with history, need snapshot checkpoints and revision GC/compaction. Hindsight warns that keeping every version is costly. Pinned and head revisions can never be collected.

The single writer's throughput ceiling and the single-machine assumption: fine at agent scale, but multiple machines need Phase 8, and the co-located deployment assumption has to be stated explicitly in every experiment (B13).
Claude Code / Codex hook API changes, and hooks that cannot fully observe Bash side effects. Letta also leaves shells unconfined by default.
Licensing: OpenViking (AGPL-3.0) and Kage (GPL-3.0) can only be referenced at the idea level, with no code copied. The rest are Apache-2.0/MIT and can be referenced, keeping NOTICE files.
Scope conflict: the research milestones (H1-H4 experiments) and product hardening compete for the same time. Keep the kernel API stable so the product layer does not slow down the M1 exit gate.
Requirement ambiguity: no codebase named 'ultracode' was found locally. If it refers to an existing product, the integration plan has to be redone after reading it.

designs.strategy:
Sidecar strategy (the computed task) combined with the user's own request: rank projects by GitHub stars, then build the product only from mechanisms that verification marked confirmed or partially. "ultracode" does not appear in any project file. I treat it as the product's working name: UltraCode, with the ContextDB kernel inside. The product does not build its own storage or retrieval. It attaches to a popular memory system as a "dependency + certificate + gate" layer.

Star tiers and how much each one counts:
- Tier A (>20k, used as the main source of patterns): mem0 67k, Hindsight 52k, OpenViking 40k, cognee 33k, Graphiti 32k, TencentDB-Agent-Memory 30k, Letta 25k, Dolt 25k.
- Tier B (supporting): ai-memory/mcp-memory-service 11k, agent-memory/deja-vu 4.4k.
- Tier C (<1k, borrowed only for structural staleness where nothing better exists): brain0 group 587, Kage group 42.
A mechanism is adopted only if it is confirmed or partially verified, and only the verified parts are used. When two projects implement the same mechanism, I take the higher-starred one.

Host choice, decided on verified evidence:
- Primary host: vectorize-io/hindsight (52k, MIT). Reasons:
  (1) It has real extension points. OperationValidatorExtension pre/post hooks are confirmed, and the get_memories store seam is confirmed.
  (2) It already carries justification raw material that maps straight onto ContextDB rules: observation.source_memory_ids/proof_count (partially verified), mental_model.based_on, the retracted-grounding allowlist (confirmed).
  (3) 39 MCP tools (confirmed) and a Postgres backend.
  (4) Its weaknesses are exactly ContextDB's selling points: derived items are hard-deleted, there is no CAS on the public API, no PENDING state, and no action gating.
- Second adapter: mem0 (67k, Apache-2.0). It has the most stars, but no extension points and writes are last-writer-wins, so it gets only a downstream-projection / API-compatible shim. Its plugin's hooks wiring, git_sha capture and injection ledger are used as client-side patterns.
- Excluded as host: OpenViking. It is AGPL-3.0, and its write path rewrites links when content is replaced (the anti-pattern). Graphiti, cognee and Letta lack write-path hook points; their algorithms are borrowed instead. Dolt is too heavy as a dependency; only its CAS/merge design is borrowed.

Division of labour: the host does extraction, storage, hybrid retrieval and consolidation. UltraCode keeps its own immutable revision copies, logical heads with CAS, the AND/OR justification DAG (L0/L1/L2), code Pins, certificates, and the PreToolUse gate. The host's delete and rewrite actions are translated into ContextDB events: retract, head move, PENDING.
designs.pitch: UltraCode turns the memory system you already run (Hindsight, mem0) into context you can certify. Each recall comes back with a certificate that records which revisions the context depends on: which code commit and symbol hash, which facts, which derived conclusions. When an upstream fact is superseded, the code it cites changes, or a source is deleted, dependents are not deleted. They are marked PENDING or STALE precisely along the justification DAG, and alternative support (OR) is not misjudged. Before an agent edits a file or runs a command, a PreToolUse hook checks the certificate. If a dependency has gone stale the hook warns or blocks and returns a WHY_NOT explanation. Multi-agent writes use expected_head CAS. A losing writer gets a structured conflict, so nothing is overwritten silently. Every step uses mechanisms already proven in 20k+ star projects. The new part is wiring them together.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Immutable version rows + head flag + partial unique index (one live head per key) + content-hash no-op
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (the core holds; delete has become physical deletion, and Mongo's appendVersion silently drops concurrent writes); ai-memory: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: UltraCode's SQLite revisions table is append-only. The heads table is keyed by logical_id. A unique index allows only one head per logical item, and a write whose body_sha256 matches the current head is a no-op. TencentDB's 'Mongo returns the existing v+1 row' bug and its physical delete are not copied. Revisions are never physically deleted; only GC of revisions that are neither head nor pinned is allowed.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: expected_head CAS returning a structured {expected, current} conflict, with the comparison inside the transaction
adopted_mechanisms.from_project: akitaonrails/ai-memory (expected_page_id/create_only); TencentDB expected_version used as a counterexample
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (ai-memory reads and compares inside the same transaction); TencentDB: confirmed, but the check runs before the transaction (TOCTOU)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: ctx_revise/ctx_set_head require expected_head (or create_only). The comparison is UPDATE heads ... WHERE rev=? inside the single writer transaction. On failure it returns precondition_failed{expected,current}. Agent writes always use CAS; there is no optional bypass.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Multi-head atomic commit + per-head ExpectedHead preconditions re-checked on retry
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (multi-head CAS supports only hash equality; arbitrary Precondition funcs exist only on single-dataset SetHead)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: One transaction can move several heads, each with its own expected_head, all succeeding or failing together. The gap Dolt leaves (multi-head commit plus read-set validation in the same atomic step) is filled by UltraCode: certificate re-validation runs inside the same writer transaction.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Single-writer SQLite actor thread (mpsc + oneshot), WAL, separate read connections
adopted_mechanisms.verified: confirmed (correction: page writes take the shared mutation_lock plus a per-path mutex)
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: The ctxd daemon has one writer thread that owns the Rust kernel's staged transactions (SD8 batch semantics) and the SQLite commit. MCP, hooks and host adapters only send commands. There is no SQLITE_BUSY and serializability comes naturally.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Observation provenance source_memory_ids/proof_count + mental model based_on + retracted-grounding detection (MEMORY_BACKED allowlist; all citations missing = 'unresolvable', not a retraction)
adopted_mechanisms.verified: provenance: partially (proof_count is used for rerank, not as a support counter); retracted grounding: confirmed; one-hop stale sweep: confirmed
adopted_mechanisms.how_used: The Hindsight adapter maps each observation to a derived revision. Each source_memory_id produces a single-premise rule (OR support, so proof_count becomes a real support_count). based_on produces one rule with Sem incidences over every citation. The allowlist and the 'unresolvable' guard are copied directly so imports do not trigger mass invalidation. When Hindsight hard-deletes an observation, UltraCode keeps its own revision copy, marks the dependents STALE/PENDING, and waits for Hindsight to re-consolidate before rebinding.

adopted_mechanisms.mechanism: Two-phase prepare-outside / short revalidating transaction (updated_at read check + compare-and-set on text)
adopted_mechanisms.verified: partially (the public API is last-writer-wins; internal consolidation has OCC)
